# SoAI Documentation

## Introduction

### SoAI overview [page: soai-overview]

SoAI brings local inference engines and remote OpenAI-compatible providers into one model pool. You manage that pool from a browser, and applications connect through OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible APIs instead of keeping a separate configuration for each backend.

It is also a workspace for using those models. The WebUI includes chat, files, document collections, agent tools, and scheduled automations, with shared administration for users, access, hardware, and system health. You can run SoAI for one person on a workstation or make it available to a team on a private network.

#### Documentation version policy

This public documentation describes the latest SoAI release. It does not retain separate version-specific documentation sets.

#### Models and request routing

A plugin connects SoAI to an inference engine or provider. The bundled plugins cover [Ollama](https://ollama.com/), [vLLM](https://vllm.ai/), [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp), translation, embeddings, speech, and any service that exposes an OpenAI-compatible API. Local and remote models then appear together in the model catalog. See the [Bundled plugins reference](#bundled-plugins-reference) for help choosing a backend.

**A new installation has no models.** You can install a local backend and download a model, register files already on the machine, or connect a remote provider. The catalog keeps each model's source and capabilities visible, since a chat model, an embedding model, and a speech model do different jobs. The [Models catalog](#models-catalog) page covers each route.

##### How requests reach a model

Clients send requests to the `/v1` API and name a catalog model. The server checks which plugin can handle the operation, queues the work, starts a stopped local backend when needed, and sends the request when capacity is available. Clients can keep the same base URL while you change engines or providers behind it.

You can also put several targets behind one virtual model name. It can spread requests across them or use an ordered failover route. Health checks, circuit breakers, and bounded recovery keep a failed plugin from disrupting unrelated backends. Read [Resilience and self-healing](#resilience-and-self-healing) for the failure states and recovery model.

#### WebUI, APIs, and agent work

| Surface | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [Compatible client APIs](#http-api-reference) | Connect OpenAI-compatible applications and [Claude Code](#using-claude-code-with-soai) to routed models and supported media operations |
| [Model Context Protocol](#mcp-overview) | Give MCP clients access to built-in tools, or let assistants use tools from other MCP servers |
| [WebUI](#chat) | Chat, model and plugin management, files, monitoring, administration, and day-to-day work |

Support for an operation depends on the selected model, plugin, and provider. **The server presents one API surface, but it does not claim that every backend accepts the same features or request fields.**

##### From chat to agent work

Chat keeps the transcript and its model, prompt, tool, file, and Knowledge settings together. Knowledge collections index your documents so an assistant can retrieve relevant passages during a conversation. See [Knowledge and document collections (RAG)](#knowledge-and-document-collections-rag) for supported workflows.

Built-in tools let an assistant work with the web, files, a browser, shell sessions, mail, calendars, media, and system controls. You choose which tools each conversation mode receives and whether protected actions need approval. The [Agent tools overview](#agent-tools-overview) explains the controls before listing the tool families.

#### Products and setup

**SoAI Core** is the application edition for [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/), and [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) use. **SoAI OS** contains the complete Core product on a [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) appliance and adds host controls for storage, networking, drivers, updates, and operating-system users. The artifact selects the edition; a setting cannot switch Core into the appliance edition. Compare the editions in [the edition comparison](#soai-products-and-editions), then read the [appliance overview](#soai-os-overview) if you want the WebUI to manage the host as well as AI services.

[SoAI products and editions](#soai-products-and-editions) also explains the separate SoAI Connect client, the built-in SoAIBench capability, and the distribution boundary between Core and the private appliance edition.

##### Start here

Start with [Install SoAI Core](#install-soai-core), then follow the [Quickstart](#soai-quickstart) to create the first administrator, add a local model or remote provider, and send a test message. Before you connect another device, review [Security hardening](#security-hardening) and the [Hardening checklist](#hardening-checklist). Use the [FAQ](#faq) for common setup questions and the [Glossary](#glossary) for unfamiliar product terms.

### How SoAI works [page: how-soai-works]

SoAI sits between the applications that request model work and the engines or providers that perform it. A client sends an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible request to SoAI. The orchestrator checks the request against the model catalog, current plugin state, capabilities, and capacity, then dispatches it to an eligible target. The response returns through the same API, so the client does not need a separate endpoint for every engine.

#### The names you will see

A **plugin** is SoAI's adapter package for an engine or provider. A **backend** is the process or service that handles inference. A **model** is a catalog entry associated with a plugin. The External plugin represents a remote OpenAI-compatible provider; it does not install that provider on the host. A **virtual model** gives several model targets one client-facing ID. The [Glossary](#glossary) defines these and other terms used throughout the documentation.

Plugins are distributed as `.soaiplugin` packages. They declare their capabilities and lifecycle operations through the public plugin contract. SoAI runs plugin workers in their own processes and keeps package, backend, model, and runtime state distinct. See [Plugin architecture](#plugin-architecture) when you need the boundary details.

#### What happens to a request

1. A client calls an endpoint under `/v1`, such as `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`.
2. SoAI validates the request and resolves the requested catalog or virtual model ID into an execution plan.
3. The scheduler admits the work when the queue, owner, model, and plugin limits allow it.
4. The selected plugin starts or prepares its backend when the target needs it, then sends the request to that backend.
5. SoAI returns the result through the selected compatibility contract. OpenAI-compatible streams use SSE data records and end with `data: [DONE]`; Anthropic-compatible streams use [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/) event names and end with `message_stop`.

The WebUI and management scripts use the separate `/api/v1` REST surface. Live WebUI events and interactive sessions, including the [browser terminal](#terminal), use `/api/v1/system/ws`. MCP server mode uses Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`. The [HTTP API reference](#http-api-reference) lists the surfaces and their authentication rules.

#### Routing, queues, and idle resources

SoAI persists admitted inference work in a durable queue before the scheduler dispatches it. The scheduler considers target availability, queue state, model residency, declared capabilities, and routing configuration. With [`MODELS.ROUTING.DEDUPLICATION_ENABLED`](#config-MODELS.ROUTING.DEDUPLICATION_ENABLED) enabled, eligible matching non-streaming requests can wait for one lead execution and receive its result. **Streaming requests are not deduplicated.**

A virtual model puts two or more catalog models behind one client-facing ID. Clients keep using that ID while the scheduler selects an eligible member at dispatch. See [Virtual models, routing, and failover](#virtual-models-routing-and-failover) for creation, eligibility, strategies, cooldowns, and permissions. The catalog can list a model before its local backend is running; SoAI prepares it when a request needs it. Read [Install and manage plugins](#install-and-manage-plugins) and [Resilience and self-healing](#resilience-and-self-healing) for operational controls.

Model unloading and system inactivity actions are separate opt-in settings. When enabled, SoAI can unload idle model resources or perform the configured system action after its timeout. The switches are [`SYSTEM.INACTIVITY.MODELS.ENABLED`](#config-SYSTEM.INACTIVITY.MODELS.ENABLED) and [`SYSTEM.INACTIVITY.SYSTEM.ENABLED`](#config-SYSTEM.INACTIVITY.SYSTEM.ENABLED). Both are disabled by default. In the SoAI WebUI, an administrator with the **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) permission selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, selects **Advanced** in the page header, opens **System**, edits the fields, then selects **Save**.

#### Where tools and knowledge fit

The assistant layer uses the same model request path, then adds tool execution around a conversation turn. Built-in tools can work with files, browsers, the knowledge base, hardware, and connected services. SoAI can also connect to external MCP servers as a host, or expose its own tools and resources to an MCP client at `/mcp`. The [MCP overview](#mcp-overview) explains the two directions and their permissions.

RAG collections use storage and search paths distinct from the model catalog. A conversation can retrieve indexed passages and provide them as context to the selected model. That keeps model routing independent from document storage and lets you change the inference target without rebuilding the collection. See [Knowledge and document collections (RAG)](#knowledge-and-document-collections-rag) for collection behavior.

### SoAI products and editions [page: soai-products-and-editions]

The SoAI product family consists of the Core application, the private SoAI OS appliance edition, the separate SoAI Connect [Android](https://www.android.com/) client, and the SoAIBench capability built into Core. SoAI Core and SoAI OS share the Core application, WebUI, plugins, and compatible APIs. They are different editions, not modes selected in Settings.

#### Products and distribution

| Product | Role | Distribution boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SoAI Core | Self-hosted orchestration application and WebUI for a host you administer. | Source-available release artifacts for supported [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/), and [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) hosts. |
| SoAI OS | Dedicated appliance edition containing Core plus private host-management features. | Not yet available and not currently distributed. |
| SoAI Connect | Separate [Android](https://www.android.com/) client that displays a reachable server's WebUI and adds mobile integration. | Separate repository, version, APK, signing identity, and release process. |
| SoAIBench | Synthetic [OpenCL](https://www.khronos.org/opencl/) GPU benchmark and stress capability inside SoAI. | Part of the running server, not a separate inference engine or downloadable edition. |

#### Choose SoAI Core when you manage the host yourself

Core is the application edition for [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/), and [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) use. Choose it when the application will share a workstation or server with services, users, network policies, storage, and update tooling you already administer. **Core deliberately has no SoAI OS host-management routes, so it does not add appliance controls for disks, [NetworkManager](https://networkmanager.dev/), [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) packages, or [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) accounts.**

Start with the platform-specific layout and launcher described in [Install SoAI Core](#install-soai-core). This is usually the right choice for a normal workstation, an existing server, or a managed virtual machine.

#### Use SoAI OS on a dedicated appliance

**SoAI OS is not yet available and is not currently distributed.** Purchases, licenses, and appliance media are not being issued. Contact [info@soai.to](mailto:info@soai.to) to join the waitlist; joining does not grant a license or promise an availability date.

SoAI OS is the [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) 13 appliance edition for amd64 and arm64 computers. It is intended for a machine dedicated to SoAI and you want the SoAI WebUI to manage the appliance as well as the application. Authorized administrators can use [**Network**](#soai-os-network-management) and [**Storage**](#soai-os-storage-management) from the System sidebar, and **SSH** and **Drivers** from Settings. The [**Updates**](#soai-os-package-updates) page also includes [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) package updates, and **Settings > Users** includes host user mapping. Application updates use the WebUI flow described in [Updating SoAI](#updating-soai), but an appliance accepts only its edition-specific SoAI OS release payload.

These appliance-management controls require an Administrator account. **Network**, **Storage**, **SSH**, **Drivers**, and the host-user section require **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). **Settings > Users** also requires **User administration** ([`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN)). **Updates** requires **Software updates** ([`SOFTWARE_UPDATE`](#acl-SOFTWARE_UPDATE)), and its [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) package controls also require SoAI OS administration. Review the [security model](#soai-os-security-model) for the privilege boundary, and see the [SoAI OS overview](#soai-os-overview) when operating an appliance deployment.

#### The edition is fixed by its artifact and launcher

The edition is selected by the installed artifact and its launcher, not by a configuration field, environment flag, or host marker. An appliance installation starts through `./soai_os/soai-os.sh`; Core does not silently turn into the appliance edition when the private OS tree is present. **Updates validate the installed edition and reject a payload for the other edition.**

Treat a move between editions as a new installation. Back up the instance first, then use the [Backup](#backup) and [Restore](#restore) guidance to decide what should move to the target host. Do not point one edition's launcher at the other edition's installation directory.

## Install and setup

### Install SoAI Core [page: install-soai-core]

Use the platform path below for a normal SoAI Core installation. The [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/), and [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) network installers resolve the latest stable release from the **Releases** section of the official [SoAI repository](https://github.com/GetSoAI/SoAI), validate the expected artifact identity, size, and checksum, and install it into the standard SoAI location. The [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) network installer also authenticates its signed release manifest and archive inventory. The [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) and [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) bootstraps checksum-verify their downloads; use the signed release verifier below when independent publisher authentication is required.

#### Choose and verify a platform

| Platform | Installation path | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 64-bit [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) | Network installer or complete release archive for x64 and arm64. | Supported distributions are [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) 12 and 13 and [Ubuntu](https://ubuntu.com/) 24.x and 26.x. The installer targets `/opt/soai` and requires root privileges. Automatic startup requires [systemd](https://systemd.io/). |
| [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) x64 | Checksum-verifying network bootstrap, separately manifest-authenticated native setup executable, or separately authenticated complete archive with the compiled launcher. | Requires 64-bit [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) 10 or 11, or [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) Server 2016, 2019, 2022, or 2025. |
| [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) [Intel](https://www.intel.com/) or [Apple](https://www.apple.com/) Silicon | Checksum-verifying network installer or separately manifest-authenticated complete release archive. | The installer targets `/Applications/SoAI` and supports in-application updates. Core provides no GPU telemetry on [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/). |

These are SoAI Core paths. SoAI OS is a separate private appliance edition with its own artifact and launcher. See [SoAI products and editions](#soai-products-and-editions) before choosing a deployment.

##### Confirm the host requirements

The minimum and recommended CPU, memory, storage, and GPU specifications are listed in [System requirements](#system-requirements). Model files, plugin backends, databases, user files, and working space need capacity beyond the application installation. A hard disk drive (HDD), SD card, or USB drive can host SoAI, but these options are not recommended and do not satisfy the SSD-based storage tiers.

##### Understand the network and privilege requirements

Installing a third-party component for a user and redistributing that component inside the SoAI installer are different legal acts. SoAI installs packages, runtimes, browser artifacts, and optional backends that remain under their owners' licenses; the SoAI license cannot grant redistribution rights for them. SoAI does not have permission to repackage every dependency, and other licenses impose redistribution conditions that vary by component and build. A complete bundled installer would itself redistribute all of those works. SoAI therefore includes a third-party component only when its redistribution rights and notice obligations are satisfied, and otherwise downloads it from its supported source so the component is supplied under its own terms.

**Because third-party runtime dependencies must be downloaded under their respective licenses rather than bundled, an initial installation requires a temporary internet connection.** The network installer retrieves the current SoAI release metadata and the correct platform artifact, then the installed launcher provisions the managed [Python](https://www.python.org/) environment and the third-party dependencies and runtime artifacts that cannot be included in the release payload. It can also use the host package manager for missing system prerequisites. Backends, models, and optional feature assets are obtained separately when you choose them. After everything required for your deployment is present, SoAI can operate without public-network access as described in [Offline installation and operation](#offline-installation-and-operation).

On [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), root or `sudo` access is required by the standard installer because it writes the system-owned `/opt/soai` installation, creates the `/usr/local/bin/soai` command, installs missing host packages when necessary, and, if automatic startup is selected, writes and manages `/etc/systemd/system/soai.service`. `sudo` is only the elevation mechanism for those host changes; it is not required merely to use the WebUI. An extracted, verified release can instead be installed to a user-writable target without `--fast` when the host prerequisites are already installed, but that path does not install a system service or the global `soai` command.

##### Verify a release before installation

Download only the platform artifact named by the release. **GitHub-generated source snapshots are not runnable release or update artifacts.** For signed release sets, verify the manifest signature, pinned public-key fingerprint, artifact checksum, and archive inventory before execution. See [Download and verify SoAI releases](#download-and-verify-soai-releases) for the complete procedure.

#### Install SoAI Core

Run the network installer:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://soai.to/install/linux | bash
```

Unless `SOAI_INSTALL_AUTOSTART` is set, the installer asks `Start SoAI automatically at system startup? [y/N]`. No is the default. An unrecognized response, no interactive terminal, or no response within 30 seconds leaves automatic startup disabled. Selecting Yes requires a running [systemd](https://systemd.io/) service manager.

The network installer adds `soai` to the system command path. Run it from any directory; it uses `/opt/soai` as its working directory and accepts the same commands and options as `soai.sh`. **On a host with multiple installations, this command belongs only to the default `/opt/soai` installation.** Start another installation through its explicit launcher path; its installer and uninstaller do not replace or remove the default installation's command.

To request service installation and automatic startup during an unattended installation:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://soai.to/install/linux | SOAI_INSTALL_AUTOSTART=y bash
```

From an extracted and verified [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) release, choose an explicit target:

```bash
./install-soai-from-release.sh --target /path/to/soai
```

On supported [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) and [Ubuntu](https://ubuntu.com/) hosts, the fast path installs required system packages, installs to `/opt/soai`, configures and enables `soai.service`, starts the service, and verifies its health. It obtains root privileges through `sudo` when needed:

```bash
./install-soai-from-release.sh --fast
```

Without `--fast`, the installer provisions the selected application target and its managed runtime but does not claim ownership of system service supervision. Start and manage that installation through its `./soai.sh` launcher.

##### Install on Windows

Run the verified `SoAI-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe`, or use the network bootstrap below. The native installer copies the application, prepares its managed runtime, creates the registered uninstall entry and shortcuts, then offers **Start SoAI** on the finish page. **The executable is currently unsigned.** When downloading it directly, authenticate it with the signed release manifest before approving the operating-system warning. The network bootstrap instead validates the release metadata and checksum before starting the same setup.

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; irm https://soai.to/install/windows | iex
```

The setup executable is the standard installed-app and update path. As an alternative, verify and extract `SoAI-<version>-windows-x64-complete.zip`, open its `SoAI` folder, and run:

```bat
install-soai-from-release.bat --target C:\path\to\SoAI
```

The archive includes the compiled `soai.exe` launcher. Its installer bootstraps the app-local runtime, copies the managed application payload to the selected target, and provisions dependencies there. Use `--silent` for a non-interactive install. Use `soai.exe` for lifecycle and runtime-repair commands after installation. Do not substitute a [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) complete archive or a generated source snapshot for either [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) artifact.

##### Install on macOS

On [Intel](https://www.intel.com/) or [Apple](https://www.apple.com/) silicon [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/), run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://soai.to/install/mac | bash
```

The installer targets `/Applications/SoAI`. Unless `SOAI_INSTALL_AUTOSTART` is set, it asks `Start SoAI automatically at system startup? [y/N]`. No is the default. An unrecognized response, no interactive terminal, or no response within 30 seconds leaves automatic startup disabled. Selecting Yes requires the `launchctl` and `plutil` launchd tools.

The same installer is included in the published [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) complete archive and can be run locally. The WebUI supports application updates from the manifest-authenticated [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) release artifact. **It does not expose SoAI GPU telemetry or tuning on [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/).** Local backends can still use their own [Metal](https://developer.apple.com/metal/) support.

#### Finish installation and first-run setup

SoAI provisions its own [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.13 runtime and required application artifacts instead of modifying the system [Python](https://www.python.org/) environment. A network-connected first installation downloads dependencies and browser artifacts that are absent from the payload. Subsequent launches reuse that managed runtime.

**Expect that first provisioning to take several minutes rather than seconds.** It prepares the managed [Python](https://www.python.org/) environment and then installs runtime artifacts in turn, among them the [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) build, a managed [Java](https://www.java.com/) runtime, the [Apache Tika](https://tika.apache.org/) server, and a token encoding cache, and the launcher names each one as it starts. How long it runs depends on the connection and the host, so read the launcher output rather than a clock: a step that is still downloading is working, not stuck. The WebUI does not exist yet during this phase, which is why the address the launcher prints appears only once provisioning finishes.

An interrupted first install is recoverable, unlike an interrupted database check on an established instance. Stopping the launcher can leave the managed runtime incomplete, and the next start or an explicit `install-deps` provisions what is missing rather than beginning again from nothing. A lock left behind by a killed installer is reclaimed automatically once its owning process is gone, so a repeat run is the correct response to an install that ended early.

From a stopped installation, `install-deps` provisions or repairs the runtime without starting SoAI:

```bash
./soai.sh install-deps
```

On [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/), use `soai.exe install-deps`. Prepare all runtime and model dependencies before enabling offline mode; see [Offline installation and operation](#offline-installation-and-operation).

##### Start the installed edition

On [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/), start SoAI from the **SoAI** entry the setup executable writes to the Start Menu and the desktop, which runs the launcher and shows the WebUI in its own application window without a terminal or a browser. On [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) and [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/), run the launcher from a terminal:

```text
SoAI on Linux:    soai
SoAI on macOS:    sudo /Applications/SoAI/soai.command
```

Running the launcher without a command starts the application. Use `--start-no-browser` when it must not open a browser, which the [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) launcher never does in any case. The default backend port is `5090`; the configured TLS state determines whether the printed URL uses HTTP or HTTPS. **Never use the Core launcher to manage a SoAI OS installation.**

The [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) lifecycle and repair commands run through the same `soai.exe`, which a default installation places in `C:\Program Files\SoAI` without adding it to the command path, so run them from a terminal opened in the installation folder or by the launcher's full path.

##### Complete first run

1. Open the SoAI WebUI at the URL printed by the launcher.
2. Complete the setup wizard and create the first Administrator.
3. Open Plugins and install or configure an inference backend.
4. Add a model, select it in Chat, and send a bounded test message.

Before the first user exists, normal application and compatible API routes remain unavailable. After setup, the `/v1` surface remains open until an Administrator creates the first API key. Review [Authentication and API keys](#authentication-and-api-keys) before making the server reachable from another host.

### SoAI quickstart [page: soai-quickstart]

This guide takes an installed SoAI Core from first launch to a working answer: start the process, create the first administrator, connect one model source, then send a test message in the SoAI WebUI and repeat it over the compatible API. [Install SoAI Core](#install-soai-core) covers the packages, platform paths, and release verification that come before any of this.

#### Start SoAI and open the WebUI

On [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) the installer registers the application with the desktop, so open **SoAI** from the Start Menu folder of the same name or from the desktop shortcut and the launcher starts SoAI and shows the WebUI in its own application window, which needs neither a terminal nor a browser. That shortcut runs `soai.exe`, which a default installation places in `C:\Program Files\SoAI` and does not add to the command path, so the lifecycle commands in this documentation need a terminal opened in the installation folder or the launcher's full path.

On [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) and [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/), open a terminal and run the launcher for your installation.

```bash
# SoAI on Linux, installed with the network installer, from any directory
soai

# SoAI on Linux, from the installation folder
./soai.sh

# SoAI on macOS
sudo /Applications/SoAI/soai.command
```

The network installer puts `soai` on the system command path as a link to the launcher of the installation it created, and the launcher resolves that link and works from its own installation folder, so you can type `soai` anywhere and reach the same application, with the same commands and options that `soai.sh` accepts. An installation unpacked from a release archive has no such command, so run its `./soai.sh` from the installation folder. On a host carrying more than one installation, `soai` belongs to the default one in `/opt/soai` and the others need their explicit launcher paths.

Running the launcher without a command starts the application and opens the WebUI in your default browser, so pass `--start-no-browser` when it must not, or turn [`SERVER.WEBUI.AUTO_OPEN_BROWSER`](#config-SERVER.WEBUI.AUTO_OPEN_BROWSER) off to change that for every start. The default port is `5090` and TLS stays off until you configure it, which makes the first address `http://localhost:5090`. If something else already holds `5090` while [`SERVER.HTTP.NETWORK.PORT`](#config-SERVER.HTTP.NETWORK.PORT) is still at its default, SoAI logs the conflict and moves up through the fallback range ending at `5099` instead of refusing to start, while a port you set explicitly is treated as a requirement and a conflict there stops startup, so run `soai --status` when you need the address a running instance is actually serving.

The [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) launcher loads that same address into its own window rather than a browser and never opens one, which makes `--start-no-browser` and [`SERVER.WEBUI.AUTO_OPEN_BROWSER`](#config-SERVER.WEBUI.AUTO_OPEN_BROWSER) inert there. The window is the WebUI, so anything the documentation describes doing in a browser tab you do in it, and you can still reach the running instance from a browser on the same host or from another machine when the configured network binding allows it.

A first launch reaches that address slowly, because the installation still has to provision its managed runtime and the artifacts that come with it, which takes several minutes on a normal connection. The launcher names each step while it works. Later launches reuse what it prepared and start in the time you would expect. [Install SoAI Core](#install-soai-core) covers that phase and what to do when it is interrupted.

These commands drive SoAI Core. A [SoAI OS](#soai-os-overview) appliance has its own launcher at `./soai_os/soai-os.sh`, and [Launcher and CLI reference](#launcher-and-cli-reference) covers the remaining lifecycle and diagnostic commands.

##### Create the first administrator

A database with no users opens the setup wizard instead of the sign-in page. The welcome step carries the interface language selector, the license step shows the controlling document with its fingerprint and records your acceptance, and the use declaration step asks how the deployment will be used. **Personal use** is the only declaration you can select on SoAI Core, and choosing it skips the product access step, so a Core installation reaches the account form one step after the declaration. [Licensing administration](#licensing-administration) describes the entitlement paths and the controls a deployment sees once it holds one.

The account form takes a username of 3 to 50 ASCII letters, numbers, dots, underscores, or hyphens, a password of 8 to 1,024 characters, and the same password again in **Confirm password**. SoAI stores the username in lowercase, gives the account the Administrator role, and applies the language you picked on the welcome step as its interface language. Completing the wizard signs you in and opens the dashboard, and only when that session fails to activate does the final step send you to the sign-in page instead. See [Users, roles, and sessions](#users-roles-and-sessions) for later account management and [Passwords and credential tools](#passwords-and-credential-tools) before choosing the administrator password.

**Until the wizard completes, SoAI answers requests outside the wizard's own routes with `403` and `setup_required`, including everything under `/v1`.** The health, system information, system limits, and license routes stay public throughout, so a monitoring probe can still tell that the process is up while setup is pending.

#### Connect a model

Use this route when SoAI will run an inference engine on the same machine. The controls below need **Plugin read access** ([`PLUGIN_READ`](#acl-PLUGIN_READ)), **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)), **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), and **Model administration** ([`MODEL_ADMIN`](#acl-MODEL_ADMIN)).

1. Open **Plugins** and find the engine you want, such as **[Ollama](https://ollama.com/)**. A bundled plugin that is compatible with the host arrives enabled, so its card switch reads **Enabled**, and the card status tells you whether the backend itself is present, where **Not installed** means there is nothing to run yet.
2. Select **Install backend** on that card, choose a build that matches the host, then select **Start installation**.
3. Open **Models**, select **Add model**, then use **Download model** to fetch one through the plugin, or **Add model manually** to register files already on disk, which is available only to an Administrator.
4. Follow the download or registration task in [**Tasks**](#tasks-and-notifications). SoAI runs model discovery after a successful backend installation, so a local model reaches the catalog once discovery finds it.

[Adding your first backend](#adding-your-first-backend) compares the bundled engines and explains when one of these controls is hidden, and [Bundled plugins reference](#bundled-plugins-reference) describes what each plugin is for.

##### Connect a remote OpenAI-compatible provider

A model that already runs behind an OpenAI-compatible API needs no local backend. Open **Models**, select **Add model**, then **Add provider**, choose **External**, and enter a **Provider name**, **API URL**, **API key**, and an optional **Models filter** before selecting **Add provider**. SoAI asks the service for its model list and adds the models it accepts. Adding a provider requires **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)).

#### Send the first message

Open **Chat**, pick the model in the selector, and send a short message. The sidebar keeps Chat and Automation hidden until this browser has seen at least one model that is loaded or available and is not an embedding model, then leaves them in place from that point on, so an instance whose only model is an embedding model shows no Chat entry at all.

When the model is missing from the selector, check its status in **Models**, confirm the owning plugin or provider in **Plugins**, and look at the operation in [**Tasks**](#tasks-and-notifications). For a failed backend or provider request, open **Logs** from the **Settings** button at the right of the header, which is where Logs lives because the default sidebar layout hides Settings, About, and Logs, and reading it requires **Log access** ([`LOG_ACCESS`](#acl-LOG_ACCESS)). [Monitoring and observability](#monitoring-and-observability) covers the log controls.

##### Call the same model over the API

The compatible API serves the same catalog on `/v1/chat/completions`. After setup it stays open until the first API key exists, and creating one makes bearer authentication mandatory on both the OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible routes, so leave the `Authorization` line out of the example below while the instance still has no keys. To create one, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**, a tab that appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)).

```bash
curl http://localhost:5090/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -d '{"model": "YOUR_MODEL", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'
```

#### Change a Core setting

Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then select **Advanced** in the page header, which an Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) can see. Use **Search settings...** to find the field, change it, and select **Save** in the page header. [Configuration](#configuration) lists every current path with its default and description, and [Configuration scopes and restart behavior](#configuration-scopes-and-restart-behavior) explains which saves reach the running process and which wait for a restart.

### Adding your first backend [page: adding-your-first-backend]

Your first backend should match the work you want to do and the host that will run it. SoAI does not require one engine for every installation. Use the bundled plugin descriptions in [Bundled plugins reference](#bundled-plugins-reference) to choose a local engine, or add an External provider when the model already runs behind an OpenAI-compatible API.

#### Pick a starting point

- **[Ollama](https://ollama.com/)** suits a host where you already use [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) or want SoAI to manage an [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) process and its model lifecycle.
- **[llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp)** is the portable choice for GGUF models on [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/), or [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/).
- **[vLLM](https://vllm.ai/)** offers CPU and accelerator variants for workloads that benefit from higher concurrent throughput. Open **Plugins > [vLLM](https://vllm.ai/) > Manage backend** to see the builds available for the current host.
- **External** connects an existing OpenAI-compatible service. It does not install or supervise that provider's software.

[CTranslate2](https://opennmt.net/CTranslate2/), [Llama.cpp Embeddings](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp), [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper), and [Melo TTS](https://github.com/myshell-ai/MeloTTS) serve translation, RAG embeddings, speech recognition, and speech generation rather than general chat. Add those plugins when your workflow needs the corresponding API capability.

#### Install or connect the plugin

Viewing **Plugins** requires **Plugin read access** ([`PLUGIN_READ`](#acl-PLUGIN_READ)). Installing a backend or adding a provider requires **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)). Viewing the model catalog requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), while downloading or changing a managed model requires **Model administration** ([`MODEL_ADMIN`](#acl-MODEL_ADMIN)). The [Administration overview](#administration-overview) explains accounts and ACL actions.

1. In the SoAI WebUI, open **Plugins** after completing the setup wizard. A plugin card shows **Install backend** only when that plugin supports managed installation, is not permanently disabled, does not require a compatibility override, and has the status **Not installed** or an installation error.
2. For a local engine, select **Install backend**, choose a build supported by your operating system and hardware, then select **Start installation**. SoAI reports the local installation in [**Tasks**](#tasks-and-notifications).
3. For a remote service, open **Models > Add model > Add provider**. The **Add provider** tab appears when the catalog includes a plugin that supports user-managed providers. A choice in **Plugin** becomes usable only when it is enabled, available, compatible, and in a usable runtime state. Select **External**, then enter a **Provider name**, **API URL**, **API key**, and any **Models filter**.
4. For a local engine, wait for its task in [**Tasks**](#tasks-and-notifications) to finish. After a successful backend installation, SoAI triggers model discovery.
5. For an External provider, SoAI creates the provider and queues model discovery; it calls `GET /models` at the configured API URL. Discovery is skipped for a non-local provider when [`SYSTEM.RUNTIME.STAY_OFFLINE`](#config-SYSTEM.RUNTIME.STAY_OFFLINE) is enabled.

#### Add a model and test it

Open **Models** and select **Add model**. Use **Download model** or **Add model manually** when the selected plugin offers that flow. The manual tab appears only for an Administrator account. Select a variant when the plugin offers one, then wait for the task to finish. A local model appears after discovery finds it; a remote model appears after provider discovery accepts it.

Open **Chat**, choose the new model, and send a short prompt. A successful answer confirms the complete path from the catalog through the plugin and backend. You can also call `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions` from a client. See [HTTP API reference](#http-api-reference) for endpoint details and [Authentication and API keys](#authentication-and-api-keys) before sharing an endpoint with another client.

#### If the first request fails

Check the model status in **Models**, the plugin runtime in **Plugins**, and the operation result in **Tasks**. A backend can be installed while its process is stopped, loading, unavailable, or quarantined. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Logs**, and inspect the plugin log before retrying. With the default sidebar layout, Logs is hidden, but an account with **Log access** ([`LOG_ACCESS`](#acl-LOG_ACCESS)) can open it from that menu. See [Monitoring and observability](#monitoring-and-observability) for log controls, then follow [Operational runbooks](#operational-runbooks) for circuit and quarantine recovery. If the model does not appear at all, confirm its files, model ID, plugin capability, and storage path before changing runtime settings.

### Deploying SoAI Core [page: deploying-soai-core]

This guide turns a working SoAI Core installation into a durable private service. SoAI OS has a separate appliance lifecycle and launcher.

#### Choose a supported deployment path

| Host | Recommended path | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) 12 or 13, or [Ubuntu](https://ubuntu.com/) 24.x or 26.x | Use the official installer or a verified complete archive with `./install-soai-from-release.sh --fast`. | The fast path installs required packages, targets `/opt/soai`, configures `soai.service`, starts it, and verifies readiness. It requires root and [systemd](https://systemd.io/). |
| Other 64-bit [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) | Install a verified complete archive to an explicit target and operate it with `./soai.sh`. | This path is outside the supported operating-system set. Provide your own dependencies and service supervision. |
| [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) 10 or 11 on x64 | Run the verified `SoAI-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe`. | The executable is currently unsigned, so authenticate it with the signed release manifest before approval. The installer owns application setup, managed runtime preparation, shortcuts, and removal. |
| [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) on [Intel](https://www.intel.com/) or [Apple](https://www.apple.com/) silicon | Run `curl -fsSL https://soai.to/install/mac \| bash` or use the installer from a verified [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) archive. | The installer can configure launchd startup, and application updates use the manifest-authenticated [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) complete archive. |

Start with [Install SoAI Core](#install-soai-core) and verify downloaded artifacts as described in [Download and verify SoAI releases](#download-and-verify-soai-releases). **Do not deploy a GitHub-generated source snapshot as a runnable release.**

#### Configure the deployment

1. Start SoAI and open the SoAI WebUI at the URL printed by the launcher. The default port is `5090`.
2. Complete the setup wizard and create the first Administrator.
3. Add a local backend or remote provider, then send a test request in Chat.
4. Create a backup before changing network exposure or moving data paths.

**Before the first account exists, normal application and compatible API routes are unavailable.** Do not place an incomplete wizard behind a shared endpoint.

##### Set the private network boundary

Use [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls) to set the listening address, port, certificates, allowed hosts, and trusted proxy networks. A reverse proxy must preserve WebSocket upgrades for `/api/v1/system/ws` and avoid buffering compatible API streams. **A proxy does not make public internet exposure a recommended configuration.**

Complete [Hardening checklist](#hardening-checklist) before allowing other hosts to connect. Create at least one API key before exposing `/v1/*` beyond loopback: after setup the compatible API is open while the key store has no records, and creating the first key turns authentication on.

##### Plan capacity and storage

Keep the database, encryption key, model store, plugin environments, file storage, knowledge indexes, logs, and backups on durable storage sized for their workloads. Use [Data storage, retention, and relocation](#data-storage-retention-and-relocation) before changing a path and [Capacity planning](#capacity-planning) before increasing request concurrency. **A fast model does not remove disk, queue, backend, or provider limits.**

#### Operate and verify the deployment

- Use [Monitoring and observability](#monitoring-and-observability) to define normal health and stale-data handling.
- Create and test backups through [Backup](#backup) and [Restore](#restore).
- Apply signed releases through [Updating SoAI](#updating-soai).
- Keep application restart, host restart, and recovery actions distinct with [System power and application lifecycle](#system-power-and-application-lifecycle).
- Collect version, state, and bounded logs before asking for help; see [Getting help and reporting an issue](#getting-help-and-reporting-an-issue).

##### Verify after each deployment change

1. Run `./soai.sh status` on [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), `sudo /Applications/SoAI/soai.command status` on [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/), or `soai.exe status` on [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/). Confirm that it identifies the intended installation.
2. Request `GET /api/v1/system/health` on the configured scheme, host, and port.
3. Sign in through the final client URL and confirm live status updates. A page that retains old values while disconnected must show them as stale.
4. Call `GET /v1/models` with the same authentication policy clients will use, then send one bounded inference request.

- [Install SoAI Core](#install-soai-core) for platform-specific installation paths.
- [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls) for listener, certificate, and proxy configuration.
- [Hardening checklist](#hardening-checklist) before allowing remote clients.
- [Updating SoAI](#updating-soai) for signed release updates.

### Offline installation and operation [page: offline-installation-and-operation]

Offline mode blocks outbound connections to public network addresses while preserving loopback and private-network access. Local inference, installed backends, the WebUI, and private LAN clients can continue to work. **Features that require a public provider, download, update, web request, or remote synchronization return an explicit error.**

#### Prepare and enable offline operation

1. Install SoAI and start it once so the managed runtime and required bootstrap artifacts are present.
2. Install every local inference backend you need. Download or manually place the required models and test each one.
3. Exercise any feature that needs a managed browser, Java document parser, file-search binary, tokenizer tables, or optional feature asset so its required download is present.
4. Create a verified backup and keep the installer, signed release metadata, model files, backend packages, and recovery material required by your environment.

**A complete Core release archive does not contain the managed [Python](https://www.python.org/) environment or every runtime artifact that first start provisions.** It is therefore not, by itself, a zero-network first-install bundle. If policy forbids temporary public access, stage and verify every dependency through your organization's approved artifact process before the first launch.

##### Enable offline mode in the SoAI WebUI

The **Advanced** control appears only to an Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)).

1. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**.
2. Select **Advanced** in the page header and open **System > Runtime**.
3. Enable [`SYSTEM.RUNTIME.STAY_OFFLINE`](#config-SYSTEM.RUNTIME.STAY_OFFLINE) and select **Save**.

**The network policy reloads live and does not require an application restart.** Existing and later operations are checked at their outbound boundary. Treat a blocked request as a policy result, not a transient provider outage.

#### Operate and maintain the offline host

- Local backends and models whose files and dependencies are already installed.
- The WebUI and compatible APIs on loopback or private addresses.
- Private-network inference providers and MCP servers that pass SoAI's local-only URL validation, subject to their own configuration and permissions.
- Local files, conversations, prompts, knowledge collections, logs, backups, and hardware monitoring.

##### What public-network blocking affects

- Mail and calendar network operations are unavailable, and messaging gateway inventory and delivery workers pause while offline mode is enabled, regardless of endpoint location. Public-address inference, search, image, and other provider requests are also blocked.
- Model, plugin-backend, runtime-artifact, and application-update downloads.
- Browser navigation and general web requests to public addresses.
- Explicit online licensing operations and remote synchronization.

**Offline mode is not a substitute for firewall rules, network segmentation, or provider removal.** It is an application policy enforced by SoAI. Use both host controls and [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls) for a deployment that must satisfy a network-isolation policy.

##### Maintain an offline deployment

On a separate trusted machine, download the complete signed release set and verify it with [Download and verify SoAI releases](#download-and-verify-soai-releases). Transfer the verified artifacts through your approved channel. Disable offline mode only if an in-application operation must contact a public address and policy permits that temporary change; otherwise use the platform's supported manual installation path.

### Uninstall SoAI Core [page: uninstall-soai-core]

**Back up anything you intend to keep before uninstalling.** Stop SoAI first, and do not use a generic recursive-delete command against an uncertain path. The supported uninstallers verify that their target looks like a SoAI installation and avoid deleting unrelated files.

#### Remove an installed deployment

Run the uninstaller from the installation it should remove. For the default target:

```
cd /opt/soai
./soai.sh stop
./uninstall-soai-linux.sh --dry-run
./uninstall-soai-linux.sh
```

`--dry-run` prints the exact plan without changing anything. The final command asks for confirmation and elevates with `sudo` only when ownership or the matching [systemd](https://systemd.io/) unit requires it. Use `--yes` for an intentional unattended removal.

By default, the script removes SoAI-managed application files, the managed runtime, the installation's data directory, transaction remnants, and the `soai.service` unit only when that unit points to this installation. Use `--keep-data` to retain the installation's `data` directory, which contains models, database, chats, logs, and configuration. Data paths configured outside the installation and shared system packages are kept in either case.

The script refuses to operate on a running instance, a Git working tree, a broad system directory, or a directory it cannot identify as SoAI. Resolve that condition instead of bypassing the check.

##### Windows installer deployment

Close SoAI, then use **Uninstall SoAI** from the SoAI Start Menu folder or uninstall SoAI from the [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/) installed-apps settings. The installer registers `Uninstall.exe` for this purpose. The uninstaller stops SoAI, removes its shortcuts and registry entries, then removes files recorded by the install manifest and known SoAI-owned runtime and data directories. It leaves unrelated files beside the installation in place.

##### Windows complete-archive deployment

Stop the selected archive installation, then run its target-scoped uninstaller from outside the installation directory:

```
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\path\to\SoAI\installer-support\Remove-SoAI.ps1 -InstallRoot C:\path\to\SoAI -Mode ArchiveUninstall
```

This removes that archive deployment without changing installer-created shortcuts or registry integration belonging to another SoAI installation. **It removes the selected target's data directory, so back up required data first.**

##### macOS installation removal

SoAI Core has no native [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) uninstaller. If you enabled automatic startup during installation, unload the exact launchd service and remove its registration first:

```
sudo launchctl bootout system/com.getsoai.soai
sudo rm -f /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.getsoai.soai.plist
```

Stop any remaining instance with `sudo /Applications/SoAI/soai.command stop`, then remove `/Applications/SoAI` in [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) Finder. The operating system may request administrator credentials. This also removes the default data directory inside the application folder. **A custom data directory outside `/Applications/SoAI` remains in place and must be removed separately if you no longer need it.**

#### Remove other installations and confirm cleanup

A portable folder has no system-wide installation record. Stop the instance with its own launcher, confirm its status is stopped, preserve any required data, then remove only that identified folder through the operating system's normal file manager.

##### Confirm removal

- The former launcher no longer reports a running instance.
- The previous WebUI address no longer serves SoAI unless another instance owns it.
- On [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), `soai.service` is absent only when it belonged to the removed installation.
- On [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/), `system/com.getsoai.soai` and its plist are absent if the installation used automatic startup.
- Any retained or external data directories still have the ownership and access policy you expect.
