### File explorer [page: file-explorer]

**Files** is the SoAI WebUI workspace browser. **It shows the workspace assigned to the signed-in account and does not expose the host's whole file system.** Paths in Files are relative to that workspace. Use the page to organize files, inspect supported content, and prepare files for a chat.

#### Open your workspace

1. Select **Files** in the sidebar.
2. Open a folder to enter it. Use **Previous location**, **Next location**, **Up one level**, or **Navigate to root**. Select **Edit current path**, enter a known workspace path, then select **Go**.
3. Use **Sort files** to sort by name, type, size, or modified time. Use **List view** or **Icon view** to change the layout.
4. Type in **Search files and folders...** to search from the folder you are viewing.

Open a file to inspect it. Text files open in an editable preview. Images, audio, and video use the matching in-app viewer when the browser supports the format. Other files, including documents, open a file panel where you can download or attach them.

#### View images

Pinch or use the mouse wheel to zoom around the point you are viewing, then drag to inspect a magnified image. Zooming out returns to the fitted image size. A pinch can stretch slightly beyond the zoom limits before settling back, and a released touch drag slows naturally. Double-tap or double-click to switch between fitted and original size; an image that already fits at original size zooms to 200% instead.

When an image is fitted, swipe horizontally to move through the images in the current folder, or swipe downward to close the preview. Short swipes return to the current image. You can also use the previous and next buttons or the left and right arrow keys, and press Escape to close. The image position, metadata, and download and attach actions follow the displayed image. Reduced-motion preferences disable momentum and animated settling.

#### Create, upload, and edit files

Select **Add** and choose **Create folder**, **Create file**, **Upload files**, or **Upload folder**. Creating a file opens an editable text preview. Saving a text preview writes its content back to the workspace. You can also change the file title before saving. These actions require **Files writing** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_WRITE`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_WRITE)); **Upload folder** also requires **Files administration** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_ADMIN`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_ADMIN)).

#### Work with a selection

Select **Select**, then choose one or more files or folders. The action bar changes with the selection.

| Control | When it appears | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Attach** | One or more selected entries | Copies a SoAI file link token. Paste that token into a SoAI chat conversation to use the file as context. |
| **Copy** or **Move** | One or more selected entries | Lets you browse to a destination. Select **Copy here** or **Move here** to start the operation. |
| **Delete** | One or more selected entries | Deletes one item after confirmation. Batch deletion runs as a tracked task. |
| **Download** | One or more selected entries | Downloads one file directly or prepares the selected set for download. |
| **Info** | One or more selected entries | Shows path, type, size, modified time, permissions, MIME type, and a stored SHA-256 value when one is available. It shows `-` otherwise. |
| **Rename** | Exactly one selected entry | Prompts for a new leaf name. |

Batch copy, move, and delete operations appear in the Files page **Tasks** card. Expand that card to check progress and the task identifier. For the header task panel and its cancellation controls, see [Tasks and notifications](#tasks-and-notifications).

#### Workspace limits and access

An Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, selects the page-header **Advanced** toggle, then selects **Data**. Select the page-header **Save** control after editing. The service can be disabled with [`DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.ENABLED`](#config-DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.ENABLED). **By default, SoAI rejects symlinks in the workspace; administrators can review [`DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.ALLOW_SYMLINKS`](#config-DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.ALLOW_SYMLINKS) before changing that policy.**

The Files sidebar requires **Files reading** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_READ`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_READ)). Creating and editing entries, uploading individual files, and copying, moving, or deleting one entry require **Files writing** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_WRITE`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_WRITE)). Folder uploads and multi-item copy, move, or delete operations also require **Files administration** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_ADMIN`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_ADMIN)). The API hash task requires **Files hashing** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_HASH`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_HASH)) as well as read access. An Administrator with **ACL administration** ([`ACL_ADMIN`](#acl-ACL_ADMIN)) manages these permissions in **Settings > ACL**.

Archive downloads are limited by [`DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.MAX_DOWNLOAD_ARCHIVE_SIZE_MB`](#config-DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.MAX_DOWNLOAD_ARCHIVE_SIZE_MB) and [`DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.MAX_DOWNLOAD_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS`](#config-DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.MAX_DOWNLOAD_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS). Text previews use [`DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.TEXT_PREVIEW_LIMIT_KB`](#config-DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.TEXT_PREVIEW_LIMIT_KB), and list pages use [`DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.LISTING_PAGINATION_LIMIT`](#config-DATA.FILE_EXPLORER.LISTING_PAGINATION_LIMIT).

#### File Explorer API

Scripts can use the authenticated `/api/v1/file-explorer` API in the same assigned workspace. The API provides directory listing, metadata, reads, search, text writes, folder creation, uploads, downloads, previews, single and batch copy or move, and single and batch deletion. `POST /api/v1/file-explorer/hash` starts a SHA-256 task for a path. The WebUI shows a SHA-256 field in **Info**, but it does not request a hash or expose a separate **Hash** command.

For chat attachments and file context, see [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context). Agent file and shell tools are documented separately in [File and shell tools](#file-and-shell-tools).

### Prompts [page: prompts]

**Prompts** stores reusable text templates for the signed-in account. It is a normal top-level sidebar page on a fresh installation unless that account hides it. Saved prompts can be inserted from the prompt picker in the Chat composer.

#### Create a prompt

1. In the SoAI WebUI, open **Prompts** in the sidebar.
2. Select **Add prompt**. On an empty page, select **Create prompt**.
3. Enter a name and content. Choose an optional color to make related templates easier to scan.
4. Select **Save**.

Open a card or list row to preview the full content. From there, use **Edit**, **Copy**, or **Delete**. **Deletion requires confirmation and cannot be undone.**

#### Find and organize templates

Use the header search to match prompt names or content. The sort control orders by date, name, or color, with ascending or descending direction. The view button switches between card and list layouts. Page statistics show **Total prompts**, **Colored prompts**, **Total characters**, **Last created**, **Last modified**, and **Selected**.

Select **Select** for batch mode. Choose individual prompts or **Select all**, then use **Duplicate**, **Download**, or **Delete**. **Download exports the selected prompts; there is no matching import control on this page.**

#### Enhance a saved prompt

Open a prompt, choose an available text model in the enhancer, and select **Enhance**. The result streams beside the original so you can compare them. Select **Stop** to cancel generation, or **Save** to create a new prompt from the enhanced text. The original prompt remains unchanged.

Loading the enhancement model list and running an enhancement require **Public inference API access** ([`OPENAI_API`](#acl-OPENAI_API)), non-empty content, and a verified compatible model. If the selected model is unavailable, choose another model or correct its backend before retrying. See [Models catalog](#models-catalog) for model state and [Install and manage plugins](#install-and-manage-plugins) for local backend state.

#### Insert a prompt in Chat

Open **Chat**, select the saved-prompts action in the composer, then choose a template. Select **Manage prompts** in that picker when you need to return to the full Prompts page. Inserting a template copies its text into the composer; you can edit it before sending without changing the saved prompt.

- [Chat](#chat)

### Global search [page: global-search]

Global search covers two different kinds of thing from one input. Live records come from the server, which is where models, plugins, hardware devices, conversations, prompts, and files come from, while fixed destinations inside the WebUI are assembled in your browser out of the pages, configuration paths, help sections, dialogs, and power actions your account is allowed to reach. Everything you see is filtered to what you may read or run, and the two halves arrive at slightly different moments, so a result list can grow for a second after the first matches appear.

#### Search from the header

The search control sits in the header of every page except the Search page, which hides it because that page has its own. Select it to expand the input and start typing. SoAI does nothing until you have entered 2 characters, then waits 300 ms after your last keystroke before it searches, so the panel settles instead of flickering. The dropdown holds up to 10 catalog matches and adds up to 10 file matches when the file search returns, which runs separately and usually lands a moment later.

The button's label tracks its state: **Open search** while collapsed, **Close search** once expanded and empty, and **Search** as soon as the input holds a query, so selecting it with a query submits rather than closes.

Use `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp` to move through the suggestions and `Enter` to open the highlighted one. Pressing `Enter` with nothing highlighted opens the Search page carrying the query instead, and `Escape` closes the panel and clears the input. **There is no keyboard shortcut that opens the search control itself.**

On a small screen, meaning a viewport 900 px wide or narrower or shorter than 640 px, the header search does not expand at all. Selecting it opens a browser prompt titled **Search...**, submitting a query goes straight to the Search page, and cancelling leaves the current page untouched.

#### The Search page

The page opens on **All results** and offers 11 further tabs: **Models**, **Plugins**, **Hardware**, **Files**, **Conversations**, **Prompts**, **Configuration**, **Help**, **Modals**, **Power actions**, and **Recent searches**. All of them are always present, and each carries a count for the current query, so an empty tab tells you the query found nothing in that category rather than that the category is unavailable to you. Page results such as Chat, Models, or Settings have no tab of their own and appear only under **All results**.

The page does not trim the merged list the way the dropdown does, and it asks for up to 200 file matches rather than 10, so it is the place to go when the suggestion panel cut something off.

##### Recent searches

SoAI keeps your last 50 queries and stores them with your account preferences rather than in the browser, so the list follows you to another browser or device. Select one to run it again, or **Clear all** to empty it. [Personal preferences](#personal-preferences) covers the rest of what travels with an account.

##### What a result opens

A model opens its detail page and a plugin opens the Plugins page. A hardware result opens Hardware focused on that component, including the GPU index or the disk and network interface it names. A configuration result opens Settings, either on the tab it belongs to or scrolled to the exact path when the result is one. Help opens that section of Help, and a dialog result opens the owning page with the dialog already up, so **Add model**, **Add plugin**, **Create automation**, **Add server** for MCP, and **Chat configuration** are each one selection away from anywhere. A power action opens Power with that action chosen. A conversation opens in Chat, a prompt opens its preview, and a file opens its content preview, falling back to [File explorer](#file-explorer) with the entry highlighted when the preview cannot open.

Results are navigation, not copies of the resource, so opening one still enforces the destination's permissions and its current state.

#### Search by identifier

A configuration path is searchable as itself, so pasting [`TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_TOP_K`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_TOP_K) goes straight to that setting. Dots and underscores are treated as separators rather than characters to match, which means the tail of a path finds it as well: `DEFAULT_TOP_K` or `default top k` both reach the same entry, and a fragment such as `DEFAULT_TOP` brings back every path containing it. An exact path outranks a tail, and a tail outranks a fragment, so the more of the path you type the closer the setting moves to the top. These entries exist only for an Administrator who can change configuration, which the next section covers.

Two pasted forms are handled on their own rather than ranked among everything else. A conversation identifier by itself returns that conversation and skips every other category, and a SoAI link token by itself resolves to the file or folder it points at, returning nothing when that path no longer exists.

File results match names, not contents, and the search walks the whole workspace from its root rather than the folder you happen to be viewing. Case is ignored. A query containing `*`, `?`, or `[abc]` is treated as a glob pattern, and anything else is matched as a substring of the name.

#### What each category needs

The Search page itself only requires a signed-in session. **Internal search access** ([`SEARCH_READ`](#acl-SEARCH_READ)) gates the endpoint behind models, plugins, hardware, conversations, and prompts, and Standard user accounts hold it by default. Without it those categories come back empty while pages, configuration, help, dialogs, and power actions keep working, because the browser builds them from what you can already reach.

Each family then applies its own permission. Models need **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), plugins need **Plugin read access** ([`PLUGIN_READ`](#acl-PLUGIN_READ)), hardware needs **Hardware read access** ([`HARDWARE_READ`](#acl-HARDWARE_READ)), and files need **Files reading** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_READ`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_READ)). Conversations and prompts are scoped to your own account and are returned only for a browser session. Configuration results list the Settings tabs you can open, while the individual configuration paths are added only for an Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Power actions require an Administrator with **System power control** ([`SYSTEM_POWER`](#acl-SYSTEM_POWER)), and a dialog appears only when you can reach both its page and its action, so **Add plugin** needs **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)).

One limit is worth knowing because it fails quietly: the search endpoint accepts at most 50 characters, and a longer query returns no live records at all while the browser-built categories still answer. Shorten the query if models or conversations you expected are missing.

### Models catalog [page: models-catalog]

The **Models** page is SoAI's model catalog. Use it to add local models or external providers, change model settings, test inference, and control which models users can select. Virtual models appear in the same list.

#### Add models

A fresh SoAI installation does not include any models. Choose how you want to add your first one:

| If you want | What to do in the SoAI WebUI |
| --- | --- |
| A model that runs on this machine | Open **Plugins**, choose a plugin that runs the type of model you want, and select **Install backend**. When the backend is ready, return to **Models**, select **Add model**, and download a model for it. |
| A model hosted by a remote service | Open **Models**, select **Add model**, then select **Add provider**. Choose the bundled **External** plugin and enter the provider details. External connects to an OpenAI-compatible API and does not need a local backend installation. |

See [Install and manage plugins](#install-and-manage-plugins) for the backend installation workflow and [Bundled plugins reference](#bundled-plugins-reference) if you need help choosing a local backend.

##### Download a local model

1. Open **Models** and select **Add model**.
2. On the **Download model** tab, choose the plugin that will run the model.
3. Enter at least two characters under **Model search**, then select **Search**. Choose a result, or enter the exact **Model download ID** when you already know it.
4. Select a quantization or variant when the plugin offers more than one. Select **Check** to review whether the model fits in memory, VRAM, and local storage. The report also gives size and timing estimates.
5. Select **Download model**. The modal shows progress while the plugin downloads the files.

SoAI discovers the model after the download and adds it to the catalog. The plugin selector includes plugins that support model downloads. **A plugin can be selected only when it is enabled, available, compatible, and not blocked by its backend or runtime state.**

##### Add model files that are already on the machine

The **Add model manually** tab appears only for an Administrator account. Open it to see the configured models folder. **Copy** copies that path. **Open Files** opens the [Files page](#file-explorer), but it does not open the models folder or extend the account's workspace access. If the models folder is inside your assigned workspace, use Files to create the plugin's required directories and upload the model files. Otherwise, an administrator must copy them through the host's normal file transfer workflow or the [WebUI Terminal](#terminal). Check the backend's documentation for its directory layout and supported model files, then return to **Add model manually** and select **Discover models**. SoAI refreshes the catalog without a restart.

##### Add models from an external provider

The **Add provider** tab appears when the catalog includes a plugin that supports user-managed providers. A choice in **Plugin** becomes usable only when it is enabled, available, compatible, and in a usable runtime state. If the tab is missing, open **Plugins** and add or enable a plugin that supports user-managed providers.

1. Open **Models**, select **Add model**, then select **Add provider**.
2. Select **External** under **Plugin**.
3. Enter a **Provider name** you will recognize later.
4. Enter the provider's OpenAI-compatible **API URL**, including its `/v1` base path when required by that service, and enter the **API key**.
5. To import only part of a large catalog, enter comma-separated terms under **Models filter**. Leave it empty to import every model returned by the provider.
6. Select **Add provider**.

SoAI checks the provider and reads its model list. The Models page then lists each matching model beside your local models. To remove or correct a provider, select the page-header **Providers** control, select **Delete** beside its name, and confirm the deletion. **SoAI removes every model imported from that provider.** Select **Add model** and **Add provider** to add it again with a new URL, API key, or model filter.

#### Find and manage models

Search matches a model's display name, alias, source ID, plugin, provider, or description. Sort the results by name, type, provider, plugin, status, or size. Use **All plugins** to show one plugin, and use the view button to switch between cards and a compact table.

The summary above the catalog shows model counts, loaded models, external providers, requests, the last-used model, and the total size reported for the catalog. Each model entry identifies its source, type, status, and parameter state. It also shows model size and request or token totals when SoAI has those values.

##### Manage a model

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Availability** | Turn availability off to block requests and remove the model from model pickers. This control does not unload the backend. |
| **Delete model** | Deletes a local model through its plugin. You cannot undo this action. SoAI shows it only when the plugin supports model deletion. Remove external-provider models through **Providers** instead. |
| **Edit model** | Opens shortcuts for **Model information**, **Rename**, **Test model**, **Edit parameters**, **Copy**, and **Delete**. The same dialog has the model's availability and capability controls. Virtual models use an **Edit virtual model** control instead. |
| **Edit parameters** | Opens the model detail page. Use the **Parameters** tab to search or filter the settings exposed by that plugin, change the values you need, and select **Save**. A **REQUIRES RELOAD** badge marks settings that need the plugin to reload before they apply. Select **Reset** to discard your unsaved edits and return every field to the values the page loaded. |
| **Rename** | Sets a display alias while keeping the source model ID unchanged. Leave the alias empty to return to the source name. |
| **Stop model** | Appears only for a non-virtual model with **READY** or **PROCESSING** status whose plugin is not persistent. It stops the whole plugin, including access to any other models it serves. SoAI starts the plugin again when a later request needs one of those models. |
| **Test model** | Opens a short or long inference test and shows the model state, plugin state, elapsed time, response, and plugin activity. Use this after a download or configuration change to confirm that the model runs. |

##### Load and use a model

**Unloaded** means SoAI has not loaded the local model into backend memory. It does not mean the model is missing, and the Models page has no separate load button. Open **Chat**, choose the model, and send a message. SoAI starts the plugin and loads the model for that request. SoAI may unload an idle backend later, and the next request starts it again. A disabled model stays out of model pickers until you enable it.

#### Routing, permissions, and troubleshooting

Select **Virtual models** to put two or more eligible catalog models behind one client-facing name. [Virtual models, routing, and failover](#virtual-models-routing-and-failover) covers constituent validation, load-balanced ordering, ordered failover, cooldowns, editing, and routing permissions.

##### Permissions

You need **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)) to view the catalog and model details. You need **Model administration** ([`MODEL_ADMIN`](#acl-MODEL_ADMIN)) to download, delete, enable, rename, or configure a model. Adding or removing an external provider requires **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)). Viewing virtual-model and routing configuration requires **Routing read access** ([`MODEL_ROUTING_READ`](#acl-MODEL_ROUTING_READ)). Creating or changing a virtual model requires **Model routing** ([`MODEL_ROUTING_ADMIN`](#acl-MODEL_ROUTING_ADMIN)). The manual model tab also requires an Administrator account. If a control is missing, ask an administrator to check your permissions and the plugin's current state.

##### When no models appear

| What you see | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| A blank catalog after installation | A fresh installation starts with no models. Follow [Install and manage plugins](#install-and-manage-plugins) to install a local backend, then return to Models and download a model. You can also add an external provider instead. |
| A model is missing from Chat | Chat omits models recognized as embedding-only. Other catalog models can appear, but the selector disables one unless it is loaded or available. Select **Edit model** and check **Availability**, then check its runtime state. |
| An external provider reports an error | Select **Providers** and check the status. If the URL, API key, or model filter is wrong, select **Delete**, confirm the deletion, and add the provider again. Check the provider's own documentation if SoAI still cannot connect. |
| No **Add provider** choice | The tab is hidden when no catalog plugin supports user-managed providers. Open **Plugins** and add or enable a provider-capable plugin. A choice in **Plugin** becomes usable only when it is enabled, available, compatible, and in a usable runtime state. You also need **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)) to add the provider. |
| No plugin under **Download model** | Open **Plugins**, enable the plugin, and select **Install backend**. If SoAI still leaves it out of the list, check whether the plugin supports model downloads and whether its card reports an error or compatibility problem. |

### Virtual models, routing, and failover [page: virtual-models-routing-and-failover]

A virtual model puts several catalog models behind one stable name. Clients select that name in Chat or through the OpenAI-compatible API, and SoAI picks an eligible member for each request, which lets you spread load across models or fall back to another one without changing anything in the client. Use it when the members can genuinely serve the same workload, because a text model and an embedding-only model do not become interchangeable by sharing a name.

#### Create and route a virtual model

Every constituent must be an active, enabled catalog model whose plugin is installed, enabled, and not in an incompatible or error state, and a virtual model needs at least 2 of them with no duplicates. SoAI checks each one when you create or edit the alias and names both the model it rejected and the reason, so a rejection tells you what to fix. There is no upper limit on membership and no per-member weight or priority: for failover the configured order is the priority, and for load balancing the order is recalculated on every request.

**Passing that check is not a promise that a member runs.** At request time SoAI evaluates each one again and drops any that has been disabled or is no longer active, cannot satisfy the capabilities or modalities the request asks for, sits behind a plugin in a prohibitive state or an open circuit, or is still inside a cooldown from a recent failure. Only what survives that pass is ordered and tried.

##### Create a virtual model

1. In the SoAI WebUI, open **Models** and select **Virtual models**.
2. On **Create virtual model**, enter a **Virtual model name**. Letters, numbers, spaces, slash, underscore, period, and hyphen are accepted, and the name needs at least one letter or number.
3. Choose **Load balancing** or **Failover** under **Strategy**.
4. Search **Available models** and select at least 2 constituents.
5. Select **Create**.

**The name is the client-facing identity, so it cannot duplicate another virtual model or the name or alias of a local model.** Once created, it appears in the catalog and in model pickers as soon as they refresh, and in the OpenAI-compatible model list beside ordinary models, where its advertised capabilities and modalities are the union of what its members support. A request that needs a capability only one member has still succeeds, because the runtime check drops the members that cannot serve it, but the advertised profile is broader than any single member.

##### Choose a routing strategy

Failover keeps the order you configured, skips the members that are not eligible, and starts with the first one that is. Choose it when one model is the one you actually want and the others exist to cover it.

Load balancing rebuilds the order for every request, scoring each eligible member on how much work is already reserved against it, how much its plugin has active and queued, and whether choosing it would make a local backend swap the model it currently holds. Members that score identically take turns when [`MODELS.ROUTING.FAIR_TASK_ROTATION`](#config-MODELS.ROUTING.FAIR_TASK_ROTATION) is on, which spreads a steady stream of similar requests instead of sending all of them to the same leader; that rotation is kept per virtual model and only breaks a tie at the front of the order.

#### When a member fails

Both strategies fail over. After an attempt fails for a reason worth retrying elsewhere, SoAI puts that member on a cooldown, excludes it from the rest of that request, and moves to the next member in the plan. Retry counts and backoff against a single target are the ordinary retry policy, which [Resilience and self-healing](#resilience-and-self-healing) describes; the virtual model adds a second target rather than replacing that behavior.

Failover has one hard boundary. It can only happen before the client has been given anything, so once a response has started streaming or delivery is otherwise under way, SoAI cannot move that request to another member and the failure reaches the client. **A virtual model covers a member that fails to start or fails early, not one that dies mid-response.**

When nothing is eligible, what happens depends on why. If the members are held out only by cooldowns, the request is deferred rather than failed and reports that the backends are on cooldown, and the same deferral applies to the whole alias for one cooldown window after a request through it fails terminally. If they are ineligible for a reason waiting cannot fix, such as none of them supporting a requested capability or modality, the request fails with a reason naming that requirement.

[`MODELS.ROUTING.HEALTH_CHECKS.VIRTUAL_MODEL_FAILOVER_COOLDOWN_SEC`](#config-MODELS.ROUTING.HEALTH_CHECKS.VIRTUAL_MODEL_FAILOVER_COOLDOWN_SEC) sets both windows and defaults to 15 seconds. Change it after looking at task outcomes, plugin state, and queue depth rather than before, because a long cooldown hides a backend that is flapping while a short one sends work straight back into it. [Scheduler and runtime tuning](#scheduler-and-runtime-tuning) covers the rest of the routing controls.

#### Manage, disable, and delete

Open **Virtual models**, then **Manage virtual models**. The edit action changes the strategy or the constituent list, while the name is fixed after creation because it is what clients send, so renaming means creating the replacement and deleting the original. Delete asks for confirmation and removes only the alias, never the models behind it.

To take one out of use without deleting it, turn off its toggle on the Models page. A disabled virtual model leaves the model pickers and the OpenAI-compatible model list and stops accepting requests, and its constituents keep working under their own names. The **Edit model** dialog and its **Availability** control belong to ordinary models, and a virtual model opens **Edit virtual model** instead.

A virtual model defined in [`MODELS.ROUTING.VIRTUAL_MODELS`](#config-MODELS.ROUTING.VIRTUAL_MODELS) belongs to the base routing configuration and is read-only to both the API and the WebUI, so an attempt to edit, enable, disable, or delete it is rejected and says why. Change it where it is defined instead, then follow the reported restart or reload behavior.

##### Permissions

Viewing virtual models and routing configuration requires **Routing read access** ([`MODEL_ROUTING_READ`](#acl-MODEL_ROUTING_READ)), which Standard users hold by default. Creating, editing, enabling, disabling, or deleting one requires **Model routing** ([`MODEL_ROUTING_ADMIN`](#acl-MODEL_ROUTING_ADMIN)) and is restricted to Administrators. Constituent models stay subject to their own model and plugin permissions.

### Knowledge and document collections (RAG) [page: knowledge-and-document-collections-rag]

Knowledge is an indexed document collection that belongs to one conversation. You add it through the same **Add attachments** picker used for uploads and workspace links, and SoAI parses, chunks, and embeds the files in the background so a model can search them with a tool call instead of reading them in the prompt. [Chat](#chat) covers preparing an embedding model and the steps for adding documents inside a conversation; this page covers what the indexing and retrieval settings actually do.

#### Knowledge and ordinary attachments

A Knowledge collection is an attachment in almost every visible sense. It comes from **Add attachments** > **Knowledge**, it produces an attachment card above the composer and keeps that card in the transcript after you send, it counts toward the 6 cards shown inline before the rest move into **Message attachments**, where the filters separate Attachments, Knowledge, and SoAI links, and it has to reach a terminal state before the message will send, exactly like a direct upload that is still processing.

What differs is what reaches the model. A direct upload is parsed and its text goes into the request, where it competes with every other inline attachment for a bounded share of the model's context. A Knowledge attachment sends only a short reference line naming the collection and how many items it holds, so it costs almost nothing in the prompt, and the passages arrive later only if the model calls `knowledge_search` and only for the query it asks. That is why a collection too large to attach directly is still usable as Knowledge, and why a Knowledge answer that misses something is usually a retrieval problem rather than a size problem.

Failure looks familiar too. A Knowledge card can go unavailable after the fact the way a SoAI link can, because items linked from another conversation record a reason and go unavailable when their source is removed, and cloning a conversation copies ready direct files but not the indexed collection, which leaves the clone's Knowledge cards unavailable until you add the documents again. [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context) covers the picker, the other methods, and every server-side limit.

#### What indexing does

Each document moves through the same pipeline, and the Knowledge pane names the stage it reached: **Queued for processing**, **Fetching content**, **Parsing content**, **Creating searchable chunks**, and **Creating embeddings**. A document ends completed, cancelled, or in error, and a file SoAI could open but could not extract text from is marked **Unreadable**. When the batch settles, the pane says whether the files are ready or whether some need attention, and the per-file card carries the error for the ones that failed. Use **Remove** on the attachment card to take the collection out of the current conversation.

Chunking happens before embedding and decides what a search can return, because a retrieved passage is a chunk rather than a document.

##### Choose a chunking strategy

`token_based` is the default and measures both size and overlap in `cl100k_base` tokens, which keeps a chunk close to what the embedding model actually consumes. `fixed_size` walks the same way over characters. `paragraph` groups whole paragraphs up to the size limit and ignores the overlap value entirely. `semantic` groups sentence-like segments up to the limit and turns the overlap value into a count of repeated sentences instead of using it directly, so a small nonzero value already means one sentence of overlap.

Overlap exists so a sentence split across a boundary still appears whole in one chunk. Match the strategy to the source, because prose with real paragraph breaks does well on `paragraph`, while transcripts, reference material, and anything without reliable structure are usually better on the default.

##### Choose a retrieval strategy

`similarity` returns the closest matches by vector distance and is the right starting point. `mmr` gives up some of that closeness for variety, which helps when a collection repeats itself and the top results would otherwise be near-duplicates of one passage. `hybrid` combines the vector search with keyword matching against the sparse index, which is what you want when the answer turns on an exact term, an identifier, or a name that a purely semantic match blurs.

**Top K** sets how many passages come back and **Similarity threshold** discards the weak ones. A higher Top K widens the evidence and spends more of the model's context, while a higher threshold makes retrieval stricter and can legitimately return nothing when the collection does not hold the answer.

##### Reindex after a change

**Changing the embedding model does not re-embed what is already indexed, and neither does changing the chunk size, overlap, or strategy.** Existing chunks keep the vectors they were built with, so a collection holding two generations of embeddings retrieves badly. Select **Reindex** in **Add attachments** > **Knowledge** after any of those changes. SoAI builds a fresh collection, re-embeds every document into it, then swaps it in and removes the old one.

#### What retrieval needs

SoAI turns the Knowledge tools on for a conversation by itself, but only while all four of these hold: **Enable RAG** is on under **Chat configuration** > **Knowledge**, the collection has at least one document, the Knowledge access tools are available, and the conversation model supports tool calling. **Miss one and the tools stay off and the answer comes from the prompt alone, with ready documents sitting unsearched.** While the conditions do hold, the ordinary Tools control cannot remove those tools, so turn off **Enable RAG** first if that is what you want.

Knowledge actions require **RAG access** ([`RAG_USE`](#acl-RAG_USE)), and **Load from Workspace** requires **Files reading** ([`FILE_EXPLORER_READ`](#acl-FILE_EXPLORER_READ)) as well. The default policy grants both to Administrator and Standard user accounts. An Administrator with **ACL administration** ([`ACL_ADMIN`](#acl-ACL_ADMIN)) can change that: in the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **ACL**.

#### Agent and MCP tools

Three tools read a collection, and they are the three SoAI enables on its own. `knowledge_search` runs a query with the strategy, Top K, and threshold it is given, `knowledge_list` reports the documents and their processing status, and `knowledge_config_get` returns the conversation's Knowledge settings.

Two more manage a collection and stay off until you select them. `knowledge_reindex` rebuilds the collection with a named embedding model, refuses `auto`, and requires confirmation because it is destructive. `knowledge_web_fetch` fetches a URL and ingests it into the collection, which is the whole difference from `web_fetch`, since that one returns the content without storing it.

**All of them act on one conversation's collection and no other.** They are also not part of what MCP server mode publishes by default, so a third-party client connected to SoAI as an MCP server sees `web_fetch` and the web search tools, and an administrator has to add a Knowledge tool to the exposed list before that client can reach a collection at all. [MCP overview](#mcp-overview) covers server-mode exposure and permissions.

#### Server defaults and storage

Global defaults are available to an Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, then **Advanced** in the page header. Open **Tools**, use **Search settings...** to find a path, change the value, and select **Save**.

[`TOOLS.RAG.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.ENABLED) turns the capability on and ships on. A conversation that has not chosen its own values takes [`TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL) (`auto`), [`TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE) (500), [`TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_CHUNK_OVERLAP`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_CHUNK_OVERLAP) (100), [`TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_TOP_K`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_TOP_K) (5), and [`TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD) (0.3). The size and overlap defaults are read in the unit of the active strategy, so 500 is 500 tokens under the default `token_based` and 500 characters under the others.

SoAI keeps the vectors under [`TOOLS.RAG.CHROMA_PATH`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.CHROMA_PATH) (`chroma_rag`) and the keyword index that hybrid retrieval uses under [`TOOLS.RAG.SPARSE_INDEX_DIR`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.SPARSE_INDEX_DIR) (`rag_sparse_index`), both resolved inside the system data directory. [Data storage, retention, and relocation](#data-storage-retention-and-relocation) covers moving that directory. Web ingestion has its own controls in [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.ENABLED), [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.MAX_URL_SIZE_MB`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.MAX_URL_SIZE_MB) (10), and [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.REQUEST_TIMEOUT`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.REQUEST_TIMEOUT) (30).

### MCP overview [page: mcp-overview]

SoAI uses the Model Context Protocol in two independent directions. In **host mode**, SoAI connects to external MCP servers and can use what they publish. In **server mode**, authenticated MCP clients connect to SoAI at `/mcp`. Both modes can run at the same time.

#### Choose the direction

| Goal | SoAI's role | Continue with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use tools, resources, or prompts from another MCP service in SoAI conversations | Host or client | [Connect MCP servers to SoAI](#connect-mcp-servers-to-soai) |
| Give an IDE, coding agent, or other MCP client selected SoAI capabilities | Server | [Use SoAI as an MCP server](#use-soai-as-an-mcp-server) |

#### Configure MCP access

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings > MCP**. The tab requires an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)). It contains runtime status, configured servers, connections, resources, prompts, tools, pending interactions, client roots, search-provider keys, and MCP tokens. Reading runtime status and the Resources, Prompts, and Tools panels also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)).

**The global MCP runtime, host mode, and server mode are enabled by default.** A connection or server exposure can still be unavailable because its own feature switch, authentication, permission, provider, or runtime requirement is not satisfied.

##### Keep credentials separate

**An MCP token authenticates requests to `/mcp`, but it cannot sign in to the WebUI or authenticate `/v1/*`.** SoAI API keys likewise do not authenticate MCP, so issue one MCP token per client and revoke it when that client no longer needs access.

#### Understand runtime and policy boundaries

A connected external server runs its operations where that server is hosted. **A tool exposed by SoAI server mode runs on the SoAI host with the operating-system identity and permissions of the SoAI process.** Tool visibility and protocol discovery do not by themselves make a tool safe for every user or client. Keep exposure lists narrow and follow [Security hardening](#security-hardening) for high-impact capabilities.

##### Messaging uses a separate policy layer

[Discord](https://discord.com/), [Telegram](https://telegram.org/), and [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) accounts have their own Chat, Plan, and Execute tool selections under **Settings > Messaging > Edit > MCP tools and approval**. Their conversations inherit those selections, so Chat locks the corresponding controls. See [Connect messaging apps to SoAI](#connect-messaging-apps-to-soai) for sender access and remote approval behavior.

- [Agent tools overview](#agent-tools-overview)
- [Built-in tool reference](#built-in-tool-reference)
- [Authentication and API keys](#authentication-and-api-keys)
- [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls)

### Use SoAI as an MCP server [page: use-soai-as-an-mcp-server]

Server mode exposes a selected subset of SoAI tools, resources, and prompts at `/mcp` over MCP Streamable HTTP. **It is not a WebSocket tunnel and does not use SoAI-specific protocol envelopes.**

#### Configure server exposure

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings > MCP**.
2. Under **MCP configuration**, confirm that the MCP runtime and server mode are enabled.
3. Review **Tools exposed by server mode**, **Resources exposed by server mode**, and **Prompts exposed by server mode**.
4. Select **Save** after making a deliberate change.

The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)). Reading runtime status and the Tools, Resources, and Prompts panels also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Saving exposure changes requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Server mode is enabled by default, but it exposes a curated list rather than every built-in tool.

**This exposure list governs MCP clients only.** Chat, agent turns, and automations run against the built-in tool catalog described in [Agent tools overview](#agent-tools-overview), so narrowing [`TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.EXPOSED_TOOLS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.EXPOSED_TOOLS), or turning server mode off entirely, removes capabilities from connected clients without taking them away from the workspace.

##### Know the default boundary

The default resource list contains `models`, `plugins`, and `system_status`. Mail and calendar resources require explicit opt-in. The default prompts are `system_overview`, `model_selection`, `plugin_info`, `rag_document_summary`, `rag_topic_extraction`, `rag_question_answering`, and `rag_compare_sources`.

The 19 tools exposed by default are:

| Purpose | Default tool names |
| --- | --- |
| Web search and retrieval | `web_fetch`, `web_search_duckduckgo`, `web_search_searxng`, `web_search_brave`, `web_search_tavily`, `web_search_serper`, `web_search_google` |
| Feeds and conditions | `rss_read`, `news`, `weather` |
| Utility operations | `calculator`, `datetime_current`, `wait`, `random_generate`, `hash`, `base64`, `text_stats`, `unit_convert` |
| Hardware inspection | `hardware_snapshot` |

The default tool list favors lower-impact read-only and computational capabilities. Shell, server files, browser sessions, linked mail and calendars, credentials, private knowledge, memory, plans, connected MCP resources, automations, subagents, arbitrary HTTP methods, persistent mutations, and resource-intensive media or image work require explicit opt-in. **Internal administration tools cannot be exposed through server mode.**

The generated [Built-in tool reference](#built-in-tool-reference) lists every built-in tool and its exact arguments. Compare that inventory with [`TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.EXPOSED_TOOLS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.EXPOSED_TOOLS) when deciding whether to expose anything beyond the defaults above.

##### Create a client token

1. Open **MCP tokens** and select **Create token**.
2. Enter a **Label** and choose **90 days** or **Never**.
3. Copy the secret from the confirmation. SoAI does not display the full value again.
4. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN` to `/mcp`.

Creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). The **MCP tokens** panel is on **Settings > MCP**, which appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)).

Revoke a token when a client no longer needs access. **A server-mode token has no per-tool scopes.** Every listed tool is available to that token only when the token owner's **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)), any tool-specific ACL, and the feature's runtime requirements also permit it.

#### Secure and verify remote clients

Exposed tools run on the SoAI host. **Shell execution inherits the SoAI process identity and does not pause for a WebUI approval dialog.** Shell tools also require **Terminal and shell access** ([`TERMINAL_USE`](#acl-TERMINAL_USE)). The [`TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.COMMAND_BLACKLIST`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.COMMAND_BLACKLIST) setting can reduce accidental misuse, but it is not a sandbox or security boundary. Keep high-impact exposure on a trusted local-client and local-server boundary.

##### Configure browser origins only when needed

**Server mode has no browser origins configured by default.** If a browser-based MCP client runs from another origin, add that exact origin to [`TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.ALLOWED_ORIGINS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.ALLOWED_ORIGINS). This is a browser-origin check, not a replacement for TLS, bearer authentication, network isolation, or narrow exposure lists.

##### Verify a connection

Connect the client to `http://127.0.0.1:5090/mcp` for a local default installation, or to the private TLS origin followed by `/mcp`. List tools, resources, and prompts before invoking anything. The client should see only names present in the three exposure lists and permitted by current runtime state.

### Connect MCP servers to SoAI [page: connect-mcp-servers-to-soai]

Host mode lets SoAI connect to an external MCP server, discover its tools, resources, and prompts, and make eligible items available to conversations. **Adding a server does not automatically authorize every chat to use every tool.**

#### Add and operate an external server

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings > MCP**.
2. Under **MCP servers**, select **Add server**.
3. Choose **Remote (HTTP)** for Streamable HTTP or **STDIO** for a local command.
4. Enter a **Name** and **Endpoint**. For HTTP, choose **OAuth (recommended)**, **API key**, or **None**. The STDIO form does not use remote authentication.
5. Set **Timeout (seconds)** and **Auto reconnect** if the defaults do not fit the service.
6. For OAuth, select **Save & authorize** and complete the provider flow. For API key, **None**, or STDIO connections, select **Save & connect**.

The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)), and the same requirement applies when adding or changing a server. **Host mode must also remain enabled by [`TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.ENABLED).**

##### Operate a saved connection

Use the **Enabled** switch to exclude a server without deleting its settings. Use **Connect** and **Disconnect** for the live session, **Edit** for its transport or credentials, and **Delete** to remove the record. **Connections** shows live session state. **Resources** and **Prompts** show capabilities discovered from external servers. **Tools** combines discovered remote tools with SoAI's registered built-in tools; the server name on each entry identifies its source. Reading runtime status and the discovered Resources, Prompts, and Tools panels requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)).

Automatic startup connection and bounded retry behavior are governed by [`TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.AUTO_CONNECT_ON_STARTUP`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.AUTO_CONNECT_ON_STARTUP), [`TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.RECONNECT_DELAY_SEC`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.RECONNECT_DELAY_SEC), and [`TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS). **A disconnected server remains visible with its connection state; SoAI does not present retained discovery data as a current healthy connection.**

#### Configure client capabilities

Under client roots, enter a **Root URI** and optional **Name**, then select **Save**. Roots tell connected servers about locations the MCP client considers relevant; they do not bypass SoAI file permissions or the external server's own access controls. The saved list maps to [`TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.ROOTS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.ROOTS). Reading or changing roots also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)).

##### Control server-initiated interactions

External servers can request model sampling only when [`TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.SAMPLING.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.SAMPLING.ENABLED) is enabled. They can request user input only when [`TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.ELICITATION.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HOST_MODE.ELICITATION.ENABLED) is enabled. Both are off by default. Administrators resolve waiting elicitation requests under **Pending interactions**; unresolved requests reach an explicit timeout instead of waiting forever. Viewing or resolving these requests requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)).

#### Use discovered tools in Chat

Open Chat's tool configuration and choose only the discovered capabilities the conversation needs. Tool availability still depends on the signed-in user's **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)), the current connection, the selected Chat mode, and the tool's own requirements. See [Agent mode, tool approvals, and checkpoints](#agent-mode-tool-approvals-and-checkpoints) for conversation-level selection and approval behavior.

### Terminal [page: terminal]

The Terminal page opens an interactive shell on the SoAI host. **It is not a sandbox (commands run with the operating system permissions of the SoAI process).** Use it for host work only when that level of access is appropriate.

#### Who can open Terminal

The Terminal page requires an authenticated account with **Terminal and shell access** ([`TERMINAL_USE`](#acl-TERMINAL_USE)). Administrators receive that action by default. An administrator whose ACL grants **ACL administration** ([`ACL_ADMIN`](#acl-ACL_ADMIN)) can grant or remove it for a regular account. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then select **Settings** from its menu and open **ACL**. The Terminal sidebar entry appears for every account granted the action. Each permitted user can choose whether to show or hide it with the sidebar customization control in Settings. A user without the action does not receive the navigation entry and sees an access-denied message if navigation is attempted.

The feature also requires [`SERVER.WEBUI.TERMINAL.ENABLED`](#config-SERVER.WEBUI.TERMINAL.ENABLED), which is on by default. An administrator whose ACL grants **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) can select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then select **Settings** from its menu. Select **Advanced** in the page header, open **Server**, use **Search settings...** to find the path, and select **Save**. The title changes to **Advanced settings** and the header control becomes **Basic**. **Disabling it prevents new terminal sessions even for an account that has the action.**

#### Use an interactive session

Open **Terminal** from the sidebar. The WebUI creates an interactive PTY session over the main SoAI WebSocket and starts the host's configured default shell. Input, output, and window resizing stay in that session. A WebSocket connection can have one active PTY session at a time.

The terminal toolbar provides **Increase text size**, **Decrease text size**, and **Clear terminal**. Use the page header's **Open in new window** action when a detached terminal is more convenient. **If a foreground command is still running, navigating away shows a confirmation because leaving terminates that terminal session.**

#### Session behavior and limits

SoAI sends PTY input and output through `/api/v1/system/ws`; it does not expose a separate one-shot command endpoint for the WebUI. New sessions use an 80 by 24 terminal size when no dimensions are supplied. The server limits received dimensions to 500 columns and 200 rows. Closing the session or leaving the page closes the PTY.

#### Audit and security

SoAI records terminal session connection and disconnection events in the audit log. **It does not parse every command typed into the interactive shell.** Give **Terminal and shell access** ([`TERMINAL_USE`](#acl-TERMINAL_USE)) only to accounts that should have the same host access as the SoAI process, and remove the action when that access is no longer needed.

### Automations [page: automations]

**Automation** schedules an agent conversation for a chosen time and repeats it when you select a recurrence. Each run uses its own model, workspace folder, prompts, parameters, and MCP tool policy. The run creates a chat transcript when it starts. **Open transcript** is available when that transcript exists.

The sidebar shows **Automation** after this browser has seen a selectable model. On a new installation, add or enable a suitable model in **Models** first.

#### Create an automation

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select **Automation** in the sidebar.
2. Select **Create automation** in the Automation toolbar. On a compact toolbar, open **More actions** first.
3. Enter a **Title**, choose a **Timezone**, and set **Start**.
4. Choose **Recurrence**: None, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or Yearly.
5. Select an available **Model** that supports tool calling. The list shows model availability, but it does not guarantee that a model can call tools. In **Turns**, enter the first prompt and use **Add turn** for each follow-up prompt. Each entered turn runs as one agent turn.
6. Choose a workspace with **Choose folder** when the run needs files. Recurring runs retain that automation folder.
7. Use **Edit parameters** for settings that apply only to this automation, then select **Save**.

**Automations run in Execute mode.** The editor has no Chat or Plan mode selector. Use the MCP tools and approval section to choose the tools available to the run. Turn on **Require permissions** when tool calls must wait for your approval while the automation runs. Loading and choosing tools requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)).

#### Set a run limit

**Max run minutes** accepts a value from 1 through 1440. When the limit is reached, SoAI requests cancellation and the final run shows **Error** with a timeout message. Set a limit that leaves enough time for the model and its selected tools, especially when a run reads files, uses a browser, or waits for external services.

#### Manage schedules and runs

On a wide desktop layout, the registry beside the calendar contains **Automations** and **Runs**. When the available page width is 1,400px or less, select **Pane** in the Automation toolbar to show that registry over the calendar; it changes to **Calendar** when the registry is open. The Automations section lists each schedule with an **Enabled** toggle, an edit control, and a delete control. Disabling a schedule prevents future scheduled runs and marks its queued runs **Abandoned**; it does not stop a running run.

Before deleting an automation, stop or wait for any queued or running runs; SoAI rejects the deletion while either exists. **Deleting it removes the definition and its stored run records, while existing chat transcripts remain available.** The Runs section shows upcoming and recent occurrences. Queued and running entries use **Stop run**; every other entry uses **Delete run**. **Select runs** appears when at least two runs are in the current view and lets you remove several entries at once. The confirmation warns that deleting running runs stops them. Select a run to open **Details**, which can show its plan, progress, and excerpt. Use **Open transcript** when a transcript exists.

The WebUI has no **Run now** button. An authenticated WebUI API client can create an immediate run with `POST /api/v1/automations/{automation_id}/run-now`.

#### Automation API

These are account-scoped WebUI API routes. Every route in the table requires **Internal session-cookie access** ([`AUTH_COOKIE`](#acl-AUTH_COOKIE)) through the signed-in user's WebUI session cookie. **An OpenAI-compatible API key does not authenticate them.**

| Purpose | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Delete occurrences | `POST /api/v1/automations/occurrences/delete` |
| List or create definitions | `GET` or `POST /api/v1/automations` |
| Read occurrences | `GET /api/v1/automations/occurrences` |
| Read runs | `GET /api/v1/automations/runs`, `GET /api/v1/automations/runs/active`, or `GET /api/v1/automations/runs/{run_id}` |
| Read the MCP tool catalog | `GET /api/v1/automations/mcp/tools`; requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)) |
| Read, update, or delete a definition | `GET`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE /api/v1/automations/{automation_id}` |
| Run a definition immediately | `POST /api/v1/automations/{automation_id}/run-now` |

#### Scheduling limits

An Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, selects the page-header **Advanced** toggle, then selects **Automation**. Use the page-header **Save** control after changing a limit. The scheduler interval is set by [`AUTOMATION.SCHEDULER_TICK_SECONDS`](#config-AUTOMATION.SCHEDULER_TICK_SECONDS) and the number of due entries processed per cycle is set by [`AUTOMATION.DUE_BATCH_LIMIT`](#config-AUTOMATION.DUE_BATCH_LIMIT). SoAI limits concurrent work with [`AUTOMATION.MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS`](#config-AUTOMATION.MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS) and [`AUTOMATION.MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS_PER_USER`](#config-AUTOMATION.MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS_PER_USER). Administrators can block unqualified MCP tools through [`AUTOMATION.DISALLOWED_UNQUALIFIED_TOOLS`](#config-AUTOMATION.DISALLOWED_UNQUALIFIED_TOOLS).

See [Planning and agent control tools](#planning-and-agent-control-tools) for the available automation tools and [MCP overview](#mcp-overview) for MCP setup and access requirements.

### Tasks and notifications [page: tasks-and-notifications]

The bell at the right of the SoAI WebUI header opens one dropdown that holds two panels. **Tasks** shows work that is running now, and the notifications panel holds the notices SoAI has saved for your account. Anything that keeps going after you leave the page that started it, a model download, a backend installation, an automation run, a backup, is visible in one of the two.

#### Watch active work in Tasks

Select the bell, then select the **Tasks** heading to expand or collapse the list. This browser remembers that choice, while the Notifications list underneath it starts expanded every time, and `Esc` collapses the task list again.

Each row stands for one plugin or one source of tracked work, and the heading counts the rows, as in **Tasks: 3**. A row carries a status indicator, the plugin name, and one line per operation with its label (**Model download**, **Backend install**, **RAG folder scan**, and so on), a short detail line, and a progress bar. A plugin that is loaded and ready has a row even when nothing is downloading, because the panel follows active plugins as well as operations.

Expanding the panel asks the server for the current active-task snapshot and reconciles the list against it, so work started in another session appears and anything that ended in the meantime drops out. That snapshot returns at most the smaller of [`SYSTEM.TASKS.ACTIVE_TASKS_LIMIT`](#config-SYSTEM.TASKS.ACTIVE_TASKS_LIMIT) and [`SYSTEM.TASKS.TASK_LIST_MAX_LIMIT`](#config-SYSTEM.TASKS.TASK_LIST_MAX_LIMIT), both 1,000 by default. A task that reaches a terminal state leaves the panel, so when you need its completed record or its output, return to the page that started the work.

You see your own tasks, and an Administrator also sees system-owned ones. Live task events need **Task management** ([`TASK_MANAGEMENT`](#acl-TASK_MANAGEMENT)), which a Standard account holds by default; without it the rows only change when a reconcile runs.

##### Stop or cancel active work

A row for a plugin that can be stopped shows **Stop** with that plugin's name, and selecting it stops the plugin without asking again. A row that exists only because a cancelable task is running shows **Cancel running task** instead. A persistent plugin has no control in this panel, and a few operation types never offer cancellation, so model deletion and backup creation, restore, and verification run to their end.

**Stop all activity** sits at the right of the **Tasks** heading and appears only when there is something to stop or cancel. Selecting it collapses the list and asks for confirmation, naming how many plugins it will stop and how many tasks it will cancel, and the confirmation is one dialog for both. SoAI then sends a stop request for every non-persistent active plugin and a cancellation request for every cancelable operation, and it reports what was requested, what had already finished, and what failed.

Cancellation is a request rather than an immediate stop, because SoAI records it and the operation ends when its worker observes it, so watch the row or the originating page until a terminal result arrives. A task that is already terminal answers with `400` and is simply removed from the panel. Cancelling a task you can see needs nothing beyond a signed-in session, while the cancellation-registry, sweep, reset, and cancel-all administration endpoints require **Request cancellation** ([`REQUEST_CANCELLATION_ADMIN`](#acl-REQUEST_CANCELLATION_ADMIN)).

#### Read and clear notifications

The bell badge adds unread notifications to the long-running operations SoAI tracks for you (backend installations and updates, model and plugin downloads, plugin uploads and clones, RAG document uploads, URL fetches and folder scans, software updates, backup creation and restore, and file uploads), and its tooltip names each part separately. The notification heading shows the total the list holds, read ones included.

A notification row has its title, a relative time, the message clipped to a few lines, and **Delete**. **Expand** appears only when the message is actually clipped. Selecting a row that carries a destination follows it, which can be a chat conversation, an automation run, an internal WebUI page, or an external address, and an external one goes through a confirmation dialog first.

Opening the panel while the list is expanded marks the loaded unread notifications as read, apart from the notices described below. Scrolling to the bottom of the list loads 100 older notifications at a time. **Clear all** appears whenever the list has content and asks you to confirm, since it cannot be undone, while **Delete** removes a single row straight away. Both act only on your own notifications.

Reading any of this requires **Notifications** ([`NOTIFICATIONS`](#acl-NOTIFICATIONS)), another Standard default, and plugin circuit breaker notices are filtered out unless the account also has **Plugin read access** ([`PLUGIN_READ`](#acl-PLUGIN_READ)). When the notification stream cannot be reached, the panel says that notifications are unavailable and keeps reconnecting.

##### Notices that ask for an answer

A tool approval, an agent question, and a secret request each raise a notification that stays unread until you deal with it, and it also raises a toast with an **Open** button unless you are already viewing that conversation. Opening it marks the notification read and takes you to the conversation at the pending request, where you answer in the panel above the composer. [Agent mode, tool approvals, and checkpoints](#agent-mode-tool-approvals-and-checkpoints) describes the three request kinds and what happens when one is refused or expires.

##### What raises a notification

Automation runs post a notice when they finish or fail, pointing at the run's conversation when it has one and at the run otherwise. Plugin circuit breaker trips, failed backups, low disk space, applied API rate limits, an exhausted [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) quota, and throttled sign-in attempts each raise one, and connected mail and calendar accounts add sync failures and reminders. Every new notification also raises a toast in the corner of the WebUI.

#### Administrator settings and API access

An Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, turns on **Advanced** in the page header, and then uses **Search settings...** to reach a path, or opens **System** for the task limits and **Server** for the notification settings. Select **Save** in the page header afterwards.

[`SYSTEM.TASKS.TASK_LIST_MAX_LIMIT`](#config-SYSTEM.TASKS.TASK_LIST_MAX_LIMIT) and [`SYSTEM.TASKS.TASK_LIST_MAX_OFFSET`](#config-SYSTEM.TASKS.TASK_LIST_MAX_OFFSET) bound what a task query may ask for, and a request above either one is rejected. [`SERVER.WEBUI.NOTIFICATIONS.EMIT_ON_AUTOMATION_COMPLETE`](#config-SERVER.WEBUI.NOTIFICATIONS.EMIT_ON_AUTOMATION_COMPLETE) is on by default and controls the automation notices for both success and failure. [`SERVER.WEBUI.NOTIFICATIONS.MAX_PER_USER`](#config-SERVER.WEBUI.NOTIFICATIONS.MAX_PER_USER) keeps 1,000 notifications per account, and when a new one crosses that line SoAI deletes the oldest read notifications first and only then the oldest remaining ones, so an account that never opens the panel still loses its oldest notices.

A client can do the same work over the API, where `GET /api/v1/tasks/active` lists what the panel lists, `POST /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/cancel` answers `202` with the recorded cancellation, and the notification routes under `/api/v1/webui/notifications` list, open, delete, and clear. [HTTP API reference](#http-api-reference) carries the full route inventory with its methods and permissions.

### Users, roles, and sessions [page: users-roles-and-sessions]

SoAI gives each signed-in person a separate account, workspace, conversations, prompts, messaging accounts, and interface preferences. Administrators create accounts and control role permissions from the SoAI WebUI.

#### Create and manage accounts

A new installation opens the setup wizard because no users exist. The account created there is the first Administrator. After setup, sign in with that account and add other users from Settings. See [SoAI quickstart](#soai-quickstart) for the complete first-run sequence.

##### Create and manage users

1. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings > Users**.
2. Select **Create user**.
3. Enter a username containing 3 to 50 ASCII letters, numbers, dots, underscores, or hyphens. Enter a password containing 8 to 1,024 characters, then choose **Administrator** or **Regular user**.
4. Create the account. Use **Refresh** when you need to reload the list.

The Users tab is available only to an Administrator with **User administration** ([`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN)). Each account row shows its role and workspace folder. The same permission controls **Rename**, **Password**, **Folder**, and **Delete** actions.

The **Role** selector appears after at least two accounts exist. SoAI rejects deletion of the final user or final Administrator and rejects demotion of the final Administrator. Changing a user's workspace folder removes that user's conversation folder overrides outside the new folder.

Select **Rename** on an account row to enter a new username and **Your current password**. Renaming keeps the account's files and folder paths, but signs out its other sessions. Select **Folder** to choose a new default folder or **Use default folder** to reset it.

##### Change passwords and active sessions

Select **Password** on an account row. Enter **Your current password**, a **New password** containing 8 to 1,024 characters, and **Confirm new password**, then select **Change password**.

**Changing an account password revokes that account's active sessions.** If an Administrator changes their own password, SoAI replaces the current session so the browser can remain signed in with the new credentials. **Logout** on an account row applies only to the signed-in account.

The Users tab also lists **Active devices and sessions** for the signed-in Administrator. Select **Revoke** beside another session, **Logout** beside the current one, or **Revoke all** to sign out every active device, including the current browser. Regular users do not see the Users tab and cannot use these account-management controls.

#### Roles and account ownership

Roles determine which protected actions an account can perform. Open **Settings > ACL** as an Administrator with **ACL administration** ([`ACL_ADMIN`](#acl-ACL_ADMIN)) to review or change role permissions. See [Access control](#access-control) for the complete permission table and lockout protections.

##### Understand account ownership

Conversations, prompts, uploaded avatars, layouts, and personal preferences belong to their user. Messaging accounts and the provider conversations they create also belong to the user who connected them. The Messaging tab requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), **Public inference API access** ([`OPENAI_API`](#acl-OPENAI_API)), and **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)).
