### Personal preferences [page: personal-preferences]

Each signed-in account has its own language, theme, navigation, Dashboard layout, chat presentation, and saved page layouts. Most changes take effect after you select **Save** and do not require a SoAI restart.

Account-scoped preferences are restored when that user signs in from another browser. Conversation display names belong to their conversation, and one user's theme or layout does not change another user's interface.

#### Open and personalize settings

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**. The **General** and **Theme** tabs are available to regular users and Administrators. Both use the page-header **Save** button, except where a control has its own Edit and Save actions.

##### Set language and regional preferences

**Settings > General** contains interface language, clock format, regional locale, date format, measurement units, notification duration, interface scale, notification sounds, header clock, seconds display, and the live status overlay. Language changes WebUI text. Locale, date, and measurement options change how values are displayed, not the stored timestamps or measurements.

##### Choose theme, color, and motion

**Settings > Theme > Colors** offers **Auto**, **Dark**, and **Light** themes, plus accent and surface colors. Auto follows the browser's light or dark preference. Theme also controls chart colors, code recognition, glass effects, page-header behavior, the back-to-top button, and page, modal, and notification animations. **Disable animations** affects interface motion only.

##### Reduce browser work on a low-end client

Turn on **Disable animations**, turn off **Glass effects**, and turn off **Code recognition** when large code blocks make the page slow. In General, hide the header clock or its seconds and turn off the live status overlay if you do not use them. Removing a shared wallpaper also avoids a full-window image and overlay. **These choices reduce browser rendering and timers; they do not change model speed or server capacity.**

Keep only the Dashboard elements you read, use list view for large Models, Plugins, Prompts, or Files collections, and leave live pages such as Hardware, Metrics, and Logs when monitoring is finished. Each additional browser tab or detached Chat window has its own frontend runtime and WebSocket connection, so close copies you no longer need.

#### Arrange navigation and pages

1. Open **Settings > Theme > Sidebar**.
2. Under **Visible pages**, select **Edit**.
3. Check the destinations you want, then select **Save** in **Visible pages**.

The default sidebar layout hides Settings, About, and Logs. They remain listed in the Settings menu at the right of the header. Opening Logs requires **Log access** ([`LOG_ACCESS`](#acl-LOG_ACCESS)). Opening About requires both **System status access** ([`SYSTEM_STATUS_READ`](#acl-SYSTEM_STATUS_READ)) and **Hardware read access** ([`HARDWARE_READ`](#acl-HARDWARE_READ)). Dashboard is always visible and cannot be unchecked. The editor lists only pages the account can access; a later permission change can still remove a checked page. **Status indicator** controls the system-status item at the bottom of the sidebar.

Chat and Automation have a separate first-run gate. Both stay out of the sidebar until this browser sees at least one model that is loaded or available and is not recognized as embedding-only. The browser remembers that event, so the pages can remain visible if the model later becomes unavailable. They cannot run work again until an eligible model is loaded or available. **Changing sidebar visibility does not enable a feature or grant permission.**

##### Customize Dashboard

Open **Settings > Theme > Dashboard > Dashboard elements**, select **Edit**, and choose the sections to show. The editor covers logs, plugins, models, hardware, requests, quick actions, and other optional cards. System status cannot be hidden.

The Dashboard Image card stores a personal image and saves uploads, removal, Fit, and Fill immediately. The Memo card stores a personal plain-text note through its own Edit, Save, and Cancel controls.

##### Arrange page layouts

Dashboard, Metrics, and Hardware have movable sections on screens wide enough for the full layout. Select **Edit layout**, drag sections by their headers, and select **Save changes**. The editor is unavailable in compact layouts and in a detached Hardware window.

**Settings > Theme > Dashboard > Lock layouts** removes the layout editor from all three pages. Turn it off and save Settings before rearranging a layout. It does not change Dashboard element visibility.

#### Customize chat presentation

In a conversation, open **Chat configuration**. Its General tab controls the display names and photos for you and the model, the conversation model, technical model-ID visibility, PDF export, and whether new chats reuse the latest model, tool, and Knowledge choices. Appearance controls text zoom, widescreen mode, rich-text rendering, previews, automatic titles, activity display, notifications, microphone sounds, message-box actions, and whether automation or messaging conversations appear in the chat list.

Most chat choices wait for the Chat configuration Save action. Photo upload and removal save to the account as soon as the operation succeeds. **Display choices are not sent to the model as inference parameters.** See [Conversation context, compaction, and history](#conversation-context-compaction-and-history) for request-affecting controls.

##### Set a shared background

An Administrator with **UI customization** ([`WEBUI_APPEARANCE_ADMIN`](#acl-WEBUI_APPEARANCE_ADMIN)) can use **Settings > Theme > Background** to select **Choose file** and upload a wallpaper, or enter an HTTP or HTTPS URL under **Download from URL** and select **Download**. When a wallpaper exists, **Choose file** becomes **Remove**. The wallpaper is shared by every account, and upload, download, or removal saves when the operation succeeds.

Wallpaper overlay is a per-account preference shown only while a shared wallpaper exists. Solid background color is shown to an Administrator when no wallpaper exists. Use the page-header Save button after changing either value.

#### Reset preferences and understand their scope

**Settings > Reset > WebUI** restores the current Administrator's non-advanced WebUI preferences, including language, layout, and appearance. **Page layouts** restores the saved Dashboard, Metrics, and Hardware layouts. An Administrator with UI customization permission can use **Appearance** to remove the shared wallpaper and reset shared visual settings. Read the confirmation scope before continuing.

##### Know when a change is saved

General, Theme, Chat Appearance, avatars, navigation, Dashboard cards, and page layouts belong to the signed-in account and return in another browser. Conversation display names belong to their conversation. Most General, Theme, and Chat configuration changes wait for that page's **Save** action.

Avatar upload or removal, the Dashboard image, and the shared wallpaper save when their operation succeeds. Sidebar pages, Dashboard elements, the Memo card, and movable page layouts each have their own Edit and Save controls. **A visible preview is not evidence that a pending preference has been stored.**

##### Know what preferences cannot change

**WebUI settings do not change product branding, interface labels, route definitions, new navigation destinations, or component behavior.** Those are frontend source and edition-composition responsibilities and require a new build. See [WebUI architecture](#webui-architecture) for those boundaries.

## Integrations

### Connect coding agents to SoAI [page: connect-coding-agents-to-soai]

Coding agents can use this server in three ways. Run the agent in the browser terminal, point a supported OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible client at its `/v1` APIs, or register its `/mcp` endpoint as an MCP server. The terminal provides a shell, the API provides model inference, and MCP provides tools, resources, and prompts to an external agent.

#### Choose the connection

| Method | What the agent gets | When to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **WebUI terminal** | A real shell on the SoAI host through an interactive PTY. | Use a CLI that you want to run on the server's files and processes. The CLI keeps its own model and provider configuration. |
| **Compatible model API** | SoAI's routed models through `/v1`. | Use a client that accepts a custom base URL, model ID, and API key. [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) and [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) use the [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) routes; [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/) uses the Anthropic-compatible Messages routes. |
| **MCP server** | SoAI tools, resources, and prompts over Streamable HTTP. | Use an MCP-capable agent when you want it to call SoAI's browser, files, knowledge, hardware, or other enabled tools. The agent's model remains configured in the agent. |

#### Supported clients and surfaces

"Model API" means the client can send inference requests through SoAI. "MCP" means the client can connect to SoAI's Streamable HTTP tool server. **An MCP-only client keeps using its own model provider.** Each client page includes its official graphical, browser, or interactive-terminal setup flow when that client exposes one. If the official client only supports a configuration file or command, the page documents that supported route without inventing a UI workflow.

| Client | Model API | MCP | Important boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [aider](#using-aider-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | No native MCP client | Prefix the model with `openai/`. |
| [Antigravity CLI](#using-antigravity-cli-with-soai) | No compatible custom provider | Yes | Connect SoAI as an MCP server. |
| [AnythingLLM](#using-anythingllm-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | MCP definitions originate in its storage configuration file. |
| [Claude Code](#using-claude-code-with-soai) | [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/) Messages | Yes | Use the SoAI origin without `/v1` for `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. |
| [Cline](#using-cline-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Its settings UI exposes provider capabilities and remote MCP. |
| [Codex](#using-codex-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Responses | Yes | The selected SoAI model must advertise Responses support. |
| [Crush](#using-crush-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Use provider type `openai-compat`. |
| [Cursor Editor and CLI](#using-cursor-with-soai) | No arbitrary compatible endpoint | Yes | Connect SoAI as an MCP server. |
| [DeepSeek Harness](#using-deepseek-harness-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | No remote MCP setup | Use its custom model provider. |
| [Gemini CLI](#using-gemini-cli-with-soai) | No compatible custom provider | Yes | Connect SoAI as an MCP server. |
| [GitHub Copilot](#using-github-copilot-with-soai) | Yes, in the Copilot app | Yes | The app, editor, CLI, and cloud agents have different connection boundaries. |
| [goose](#using-goose-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | SoAI is a custom [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) host and a separate extension. |
| [Hermes Agent](#using-hermes-agent-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Use a custom provider and its CA-bundle setting. |
| [Kilo Code](#using-kilo-code-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Custom provider and MCP settings are available in the extension UI. |
| [LibreChat](#using-librechat-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Declare static bearer authentication explicitly so [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) does not start OAuth discovery. |
| [LiteLLM](#using-litellm-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | It adds another gateway and credential boundary in front of SoAI. |
| [LM Studio](#using-lm-studio-with-soai) | Not a SoAI model client | Yes, with server permission | [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) hosts its own model and can call SoAI MCP tools. |
| [OpenClaw](#using-openclaw-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions or Responses | Yes | Declare only capabilities the selected model supports. |
| [opencode](#using-opencode-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Model and MCP credentials are separate. |
| [OpenHands CLI](#using-openhands-cli-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Use `--override-with-envs` when supplying the model through environment variables. |
| [Open WebUI](#using-open-webui-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Both connections are configured by an [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) administrator. |
| [Pi](#using-pi-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | No native MCP client | Add SoAI to Pi's custom model catalog. |
| [Qwen Code](#using-qwen-code-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Use its [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) model-provider entry, not a [Google](https://www.google.com/) endpoint. |
| [Roo Code](#using-roo-code-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | Yes | Agent tool use requires a model with native tool calling. |
| [SillyTavern](#using-sillytavern-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions | No native MCP client | Use its Custom OpenAI-compatible connection. |
| [Devin Desktop](#using-devin-desktop-with-soai) | No arbitrary compatible endpoint | Yes | Use the current [Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) MCP configuration; Cascade uses a separate legacy file. |
| [Zed Agent](#using-zed-agent-with-soai) | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions or Responses | Yes | ACP-hosted external agents keep separate model configuration. |

#### Prepare credentials

Finish the setup wizard first. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then choose **Settings**. The **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)** tab is visible to administrators with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)). Create a SoAI API key there when the agent will call `/v1`. Once SoAI stores an API-key record, the OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible routes require that key. The **MCP** tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)). Create a separate personal token in **MCP > MCP tokens**; token creation also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Changing the MCP runtime, server-mode, or exposure settings also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Do not put either secret in a project file that will be committed.

Replace `SOAI_HOST` with the hostname or LAN address reachable from the agent. Local clients (on the same machine) can use `http://127.0.0.1:5090`. For a client on another trusted device, use `https://SOAI_HOST:5090` over a controlled LAN or VPN. A private reverse proxy that terminates TLS on the standard HTTPS port can expose the same paths at `https://SOAI_HOST`. **Do not publish the complete SoAI interface to the internet.** Read [Security hardening](#security-hardening) for the deployment boundary and [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls) for certificate and proxy configuration.

#### Method 1: use the SoAI WebUI terminal

The **Terminal** route is available to users with the **Terminal and shell access** ([`TERMINAL_USE`](#acl-TERMINAL_USE)) permission while [`SERVER.WEBUI.TERMINAL.ENABLED`](#config-SERVER.WEBUI.TERMINAL.ENABLED) is enabled. An administrator with the **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) permission selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, selects **Advanced** in the page header, then opens **Server** and changes the **Terminal** setting before selecting **Save**. **Terminal** appears in the default sidebar for an Administrator or a Standard user who has been granted that permission, unless that user has hidden the item in their sidebar settings. Open the direct route at `/#terminal` and start the agent from the project directory. **The terminal runs with the SoAI service account's permissions.** The [Terminal](#terminal) page describes its PTY boundary and audit behavior. This method does not route the CLI's model requests through SoAI.

#### Method 2: use a compatible model API

For an OpenAI-compatible client on another device, configure the base URL `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, a model ID returned by `GET /v1/models`, and the SoAI API key. Use `http://127.0.0.1:5090/v1` only for a same-machine connection. The client must use endpoints and request fields that the selected SoAI model and plugin support. Streaming responses follow the [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) SSE format.

```bash
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'

curl https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY"

curl https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"YOUR_MODEL_ID","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with one word."}]}'
```

For [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/), set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to `https://SOAI_HOST:5090` without `/v1`; [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/) appends `/v1/messages`. Supply the same SoAI API key through `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. See the [Claude Code](#using-claude-code-with-soai) page for the complete configuration and TLS requirements.

See the individual [Claude Code](#using-claude-code-with-soai), [opencode](#using-opencode-with-soai), and [Codex](#using-codex-with-soai) pages for client-specific configuration.

#### Method 3: use MCP

Register `http://127.0.0.1:5090/mcp` for a same-machine client. A lower-impact remote client on the private network can use `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`. Send `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN`. An Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)) and **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, then opens **MCP > MCP configuration**. Enable the MCP runtime and server mode, then set **Tools exposed by server mode**, **Resources exposed by server mode**, and **Prompts exposed by server mode** for the agent. An MCP token authenticates MCP requests only. It does not authenticate `/v1` requests or create a WebUI session.

After registration, ask the client to list its MCP tools or run its MCP status command. A successful connection should show the SoAI server and its enabled tools, resources, and prompts. If the client reports an HTTP or protocol error, check the endpoint, token, server-mode setting, origin policy, and the client log before changing model settings. The [MCP overview](#mcp-overview) covers server configuration and security.

Keep high-impact MCP tools, especially shell and host-affecting tools, for a trusted local client connected to a local SoAI instance when that deployment is safe. **Do not expose them to remote clients.** Review [Security hardening](#security-hardening) before choosing the server-mode tool list or network boundary.

### Connect messaging apps to SoAI [page: connect-messaging-apps-to-soai]

The server can receive and answer messages through [Discord](https://discord.com/), [Telegram](https://telegram.org/), and [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/). A messaging account belongs to the signed-in user who creates it. Each account uses the model, workspace, response language, sender access, and tools that its owner chooses. Its conversations appear in that user's [Chat](#chat) sidebar unless messaging conversations are hidden there.

#### Choose a messaging app

- [Using Discord with SoAI](#using-discord-with-soai)
- [Using Telegram with SoAI](#using-telegram-with-soai)
- [Using WhatsApp with SoAI](#using-whatsapp-with-soai)

[Discord](https://discord.com/) connects outward through its Gateway, so normal [Discord](https://discord.com/) messages and attachments do not require a public server address. **[Telegram](https://telegram.org/) and [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) deliver incoming messages to webhooks, so their callback routes must be reachable by those providers over public HTTPS.** This does not require making the entire WebUI public.

Agent interaction prompts for tool approval, questions, and secure secret entry require an HTTPS **Public Origin** on every provider. For [Discord](https://discord.com/), this may remain a private address that the messaging account owner can reach over the local network or a VPN; it does not need to be reachable from the public internet. In the SoAI WebUI, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, selects **Advanced** in the page header, opens **Server**, and sets **Public Origin**. The setting is [`SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN`](#config-SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN).

For [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) or [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/), configure the reverse proxy to publish only the required callback routes unless the owner also needs authenticated Chat access through that address. Exposing the complete SoAI interface directly to the public internet is not recommended. Read [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls) and [Security hardening](#security-hardening) before enabling a public callback.

#### Before you add an account

You need the SoAI permissions named **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), **Public inference API access** ([`OPENAI_API`](#acl-OPENAI_API)), and **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)) to see **Messaging** in **Settings**. **These permissions do not require an external [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) account or API key.** Ask an administrator to review your access if the tab is missing. The server also needs at least one available model and access to the MCP tool catalog before it can open the account editor. See [Users, roles, and sessions](#users-roles-and-sessions) for account permissions and [Models catalog](#models-catalog) for model availability.

#### Add a messaging account

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then select **Messaging**.
2. Select **Add account**.
3. Enter an **Account label**, choose the provider, and select the **Remote response language** for SoAI's built-in provider messages.
4. Enter the credentials requested for that provider.
5. Choose who may send messages, select the model and agent mode, choose a workspace folder, and configure any MCP tools the account may use. Use **Edit parameters** to set account-specific model parameters.
6. Select **Save**.

**Remote response language** controls built-in command, status, error, and interaction messages. The model still follows its prompt and conversation context. If it must always answer in a particular language, select **Edit parameters** under **Chat execution** and state that requirement in the **System prompt**.

SoAI checks the provider credentials when you save. For [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) and [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/), it configures the provider callback (the route that receives incoming messages). The account row shows lifecycle and provider health separately. **Active** means the account is enabled; **Provider connection healthy** confirms that the provider connection works. Activation failures show as **Degraded**. Use **Edit**, **Disable**, **Enable**, or **Remove** from the account list after setup. You cannot change the provider while editing an account; add another account for a different provider.

Editing an account changes the settings used by all of its messaging conversations on later turns. Disable an account to stop new provider messages and replies without deleting its Chat history. **Remove clears the saved credentials and removes the connection from SoAI; this cannot be undone.** Existing conversations remain as local Chat transcripts and no longer receive provider messages.

When editing an account, leave every provider credential field blank to keep the saved credentials. To replace them, enter the complete credential set for that provider again.

#### Control who can use the account

Keep **Accept messages from anyone** off and enter one exact provider sender ID per line under **Authorized provider senders** for restricted access. You may add a label after `|`. An empty list means SoAI accepts no senders. Turn on **Accept messages from anyone** only when everyone who can reach the bot or business number should be able to start a SoAI conversation.

**Allow plaintext secret replies** lets a reply from the messaging app answer a SoAI secret request. **Keep it off unless you accept the risk of the secret appearing in provider history or notifications.** See [Secrets vault](#secrets-vault) for how tools request and store credentials.

#### Send files to SoAI

A user can attach a supported file in [Discord](https://discord.com/), [Telegram](https://telegram.org/), or [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/), with or without message text or a caption. The server downloads the file, processes it as a conversation attachment, and includes it in the prompt before the model answers. The message and attachment also appear in the messaging conversation in Chat. Provider and server file limits still apply. See [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context) for supported content and how models use documents, images, audio, and video.

This support is for files sent to the server. **It sends its provider reply as text; it does not attach a generated or returned file to the reply in the messaging app.** It splits a long text answer into multiple provider messages when it exceeds that provider's message length.

#### Control a conversation from the messaging app

Send one of these commands as a text-only message:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/cancel` | Requests cancellation of your active messaging request in that conversation. |
| `/help` | Lists the available messaging commands. |
| `/new` | Starts a new SoAI Chat conversation for that provider channel, chat, or sender. Earlier provider messages stay in the messaging app, and the old SoAI transcript stays in Chat, but neither is part of the new conversation's model context. |
| `/status` | Reports whether the conversation is idle, queued, running, or waiting for a response. |

In a [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) group, address a command to the bot, for example `/status@BotUsername`. In a [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) direct message, [Discord](https://discord.com/), or [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/), use the command without a bot username. A command sent with a file attachment is treated as a normal prompt instead.

SoAI processes new provider messages. **Editing or deleting a message in the provider does not rewrite the SoAI transcript or retract model context; send a new correction instead.**

#### Answer agent questions and approvals

An agent turn can pause and send a question or tool approval request to the same messaging conversation. Follow the reply format in that message and keep its six-character token in the response when requested. For a tool approval, reply with `yes`, `y`, `no`, `n`, or `always` and include the token. A direct reply to the provider prompt can also identify the pending request.

Secret questions use a secure link back to the authenticated SoAI Chat page. Vault credential requests do the same by default, and the signed-in owner of the messaging account completes them there. **Allow plaintext secret replies** changes only vault credential requests: it lets the remote sender provide the credential as provider text, does not save that reply to the vault, and can expose it in provider history or notifications.

#### Use messaging conversations in Chat

Messaging conversations appear in the Chat sidebar unless you hide them. Their model, workspace, identity, parameters, and tools come from the messaging account, so Chat locks those controls. To change them, or to update the account credentials or sender policy, select the **Settings** button at the right of the SoAI header, choose **Settings**, select **Messaging**, and use **Edit** for the account.

You can send a message from [SoAI Chat](#chat) while a messaging conversation is open. That message and SoAI's immediate reply stay in SoAI; neither is copied to [Discord](https://discord.com/), [Telegram](https://telegram.org/), or [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/). Both remain in the conversation transcript, so the model can use them as context when it answers a later message from the messaging app.

You may also attach files to a message sent from Chat in this conversation. The local message, its files, and SoAI's immediate reply stay in SoAI and can affect later model replies; SoAI does not forward them to the messaging app.

Each account can use a different context length and therefore have its own effective compaction limit. Under **Chat execution**, select **Edit parameters**, then set **Context length (tokens)** under **Model settings**. Clear it to use the selected model's default. A lower value gives the account a smaller context budget, so SoAI compacts older context sooner. If a smaller model gives worse answers as a conversation grows, lowering this value can keep its active prompt shorter without changing your other messaging accounts.

Automatic context compaction lets the conversation continue without a fixed message-count limit. SoAI keeps recent turns and may replace older details with a summary before sending the next prompt to the model. See [Chat](#chat) for context compaction and other conversation controls.

To hide messaging conversations, select **Chat configuration** in the Chat header, select **Appearance**, turn on **Hide messaging conversations**, then select **Save**.

**If you archive a messaging conversation, the next accepted provider message returns it to the active Chat list.**

### Using aider with SoAI [page: using-aider-with-soai]

[aider](https://aider.chat/) can use SoAI through its OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API. [aider](https://aider.chat/) does not provide a native MCP client, so this connection supplies model inference rather than SoAI tools.

#### Create a key and choose a model

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Then open **Models** and copy the exact ID of a model that supports Chat Completions; this requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)). Coding quality depends on the selected model's context, reasoning, and code-editing capability.

#### Run aider through SoAI

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export OPENAI_API_BASE='https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1'
export SSL_CERT_FILE='/path/to/ca-bundle-containing-soai.pem'
aider --model openai/YOUR_MODEL_ID
```

The `openai/` prefix tells aider's [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) layer to use the OpenAI-compatible adapter; it is not part of the model ID. For an unknown model, [aider](https://aider.chat/) may warn that it lacks pricing or context metadata. Supply an [aider](https://aider.chat/) model-settings file (for example, for a custom model) when accurate context limits or edit formats are needed rather than renaming the model.

#### MCP support and troubleshooting

**[aider](https://aider.chat/) does not accept an MCP server configuration.** Use an MCP-capable client when the agent must call SoAI tools; creating a SoAI MCP token does not make tools available to [aider](https://aider.chat/).

##### Troubleshooting

A 401 response means the SoAI API key was not loaded. A 404 generally means the base URL lacks `/v1` or the model ID is wrong. A remote [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) model-price download warning is independent of inference. **Trust the server's CA through a combined CA bundle; never use aider's option to disable certificate verification.**

### Using Antigravity CLI with SoAI [page: using-antigravity-cli-with-soai]

[Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/) can connect to SoAI as a remote MCP server. **Its model settings do not accept an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible provider, so this is an MCP-only connection.**

#### Configure and verify MCP access

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)), and creating a personal token also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Changing server mode or the tools, resources, and prompts exposed to clients also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)).

##### Configure Antigravity

Add the server to the user configuration at `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, or to `.agents/mcp_config.json` in one trusted workspace. The header contains the token itself, so restrict access to the file.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "disabled": false,
      "serverUrl": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Start an [Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/) session, enter `/mcp`, and confirm that `soai` is connected. Then ask it to use a harmless exposed tool. **An MCP connection does not route model requests through SoAI.**

##### Troubleshooting

For MCP failures, verify the token, server-mode exposure, trusted CA, and exact `/mcp` endpoint. Preserve normal workspace trust and approval prompts.

### Using AnythingLLM with SoAI [page: using-anythingllm-with-soai]

[AnythingLLM](https://anythingllm.com/) can use SoAI's OpenAI-compatible model API and can attach SoAI MCP tools to [AnythingLLM](https://anythingllm.com/) agents.

#### Prepare the server

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
2. For MCP, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

#### Add the server as the language model

1. Open [AnythingLLM](https://anythingllm.com/) **Settings > AI Providers > LLM**.
2. Choose **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/) (Generic)**.
3. Enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, the SoAI API key, and an exact model ID. Set the context window and token limits to the selected model's real values.
4. Save the settings, select the provider for the workspace, and send a short chat message.

#### Add SoAI MCP

Add the remote server to `anythingllm_mcp_servers.json` in AnythingLLM's storage `plugins` directory. In [Docker](https://www.docker.com/), edit the file in the mounted storage volume, not in the disposable container layer.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "type": "streamable",
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

1. Open **Settings > Agent Skills**.
2. Under **MCP Servers**, select **Refresh**, then confirm the restart and tool reload.
3. Confirm the server is healthy and inspect its discovered tools.
4. Open an Agent chat, enable the required MCP tools, and approve a harmless call.

### Using Claude Code with SoAI [page: using-claude-code-with-soai]

[Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code) can use SoAI as its model provider through the Anthropic-compatible Messages API. It can also connect to the same server's tools, resources, and prompts through MCP. These are independent connections and can be used separately or together.

#### Connect SoAI as Claude Code's model provider

1. Complete the setup wizard and select a chat model or virtual model that supports the capabilities [Claude](https://claude.ai/) Code needs, especially tool calling.
2. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, select **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**, and create a SoAI API key. This tab appears to administrators with the **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ) permission. Copy the secret when the WebUI shows it.
3. Set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to the server origin, without `/v1`, and select the model identifier. [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/) appends `/v1/messages` itself.

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL='https://SOAI_HOST:5090'
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL='YOUR_SOAI_MODEL_ID'
claude
```

`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is also accepted and is sent as `x-api-key`. When both credential forms are present, they must contain the same key. A local server certificate authority can be supplied to [Claude](https://claude.ai/) Code's [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) runtime with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. **Do not disable TLS verification.**

The server implements `POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`. The Messages route supports streaming plus the text, image, tool, reasoning, and structured-output fields listed in the [HTTP API reference](#http-api-reference). It rejects unsupported [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/) fields before inference starts.

#### Connect SoAI as an MCP server

1. In the SoAI WebUI, complete the setup wizard. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP configuration**. Enable the MCP runtime and server mode, then set **Tools exposed by server mode**, **Resources exposed by server mode**, and **Prompts exposed by server mode**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ); changing these server settings also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).
2. Open **MCP > MCP tokens** and create a personal access token. Token creation also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Copy the secret when the WebUI shows it; the full value is not displayed again.
3. Run `claude mcp add` with the Streamable HTTP endpoint and bearer header. Keep the token in an environment variable rather than putting it in shell history or a project file.

```bash
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
claude mcp add --transport http \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOAI_MCP_TOKEN" \
  soai https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp
```

Use `https://SOAI_HOST/mcp` when a TLS reverse proxy fronts the server (and terminates TLS). A local installation can use `http://127.0.0.1:5090/mcp`. [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/) stores the server entry in its own configuration; the token authenticates MCP requests only.

#### Verify the connection

Start [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/) and send a short prompt, then ask it to perform a harmless read-only tool action in a test workspace. For MCP, run `claude mcp list`, confirm that `soai` is configured, and use the `/mcp` panel to inspect exposed tools. A model response verifies the Messages connection; the MCP tool list verifies the separate MCP connection.

#### Limits and troubleshooting

**The server does not expose an Anthropic-shaped Models endpoint.** Configure `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` explicitly with an ID from the **Models** page or `GET /v1/models`. Opening the page requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)).

If model requests return 404, remove `/v1` from `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. For certificate failures, trust the server certificate authority with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. For model-provider authentication failures, verify the SoAI API key. MCP uses its own personal access token: if that server is missing, check that the MCP runtime and server mode are enabled and that its URL ends in `/mcp`. For an absent MCP tool, review the server-mode exposed-tool list and the tool's own availability requirements.

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/) can also run inside the WebUI terminal, but that gives it a shell on the host and keeps its model configuration unchanged. See [Connect coding agents to SoAI](#connect-coding-agents-to-soai), [MCP](#mcp-overview), and [Terminal](#terminal) for the surrounding permissions.

### Using Cline with SoAI [page: using-cline-with-soai]

[Cline](https://cline.bot/) can route model requests through SoAI's OpenAI-compatible API and connect separately to SoAI's Streamable HTTP MCP server. The two connections use different SoAI credentials.

#### Prepare the server

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
2. For MCP, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

#### Connect Cline to the SoAI model API

1. Open [Cline](https://cline.bot/) and select the **Settings** gear.
2. Set **API Provider** to **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Compatible**.
3. Enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1` as the base URL, paste the SoAI API key, and enter an exact model ID from `GET /v1/models`.
4. Set the context window and maximum output tokens to the selected model's actual limits. Enable image input, tool use, and other advanced capabilities only when that model advertises them.
5. Select **Verify**, then send a short request.

#### Connect Cline to SoAI MCP in its interface

1. Open the **MCP Servers** view using the stacked-server icon in the [Cline](https://cline.bot/) toolbar.
2. Open **Remote Servers**, enter the name `soai` and `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`, and choose **Streamable HTTP**.
3. Add the header `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN`, then select **Add Server**.
4. Confirm that the server connects and its tools appear. Keep automatic approval empty until each exposed tool has been reviewed.

Alternatively, open **MCP Servers > Configure > Configure MCP Servers** and add the entry below. Cline's CLI uses `~/.cline/mcp.json` and also exposes an interactive `cline mcp` wizard.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "type": "streamableHttp",
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" },
      "disabled": false,
      "autoApprove": []
    }
  }
}
```

### Using Codex with SoAI [page: using-codex-with-soai]

[Codex CLI](https://openai.com/codex/) can use SoAI as its model provider through the OpenAI-compatible Responses API. It can also register the server as an MCP endpoint when you want [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) to call its tools. These connections are independent: the SoAI API key authorizes inference requests, while the MCP token authorizes tool access.

#### Get a model ID and SoAI API key

In the SoAI WebUI, open **Models** from the sidebar, select the catalog model, and review its **Capabilities** card. This requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)). Under **Endpoints**, **Responses** must be enabled because [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) uses `/v1/responses`. [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) also sends tool definitions on every request, so the same card must show **Tool calling** and **Parallel tool calls** enabled. A model that advertises **Responses** alone is rejected during admission, before the request reaches the plugin. Then select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, select **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**, and create a SoAI API key. The [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) tab appears to administrators with the **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)) permission. Use the exact catalog model ID in the [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) configuration, including the plugin prefix that `/v1/models` returns. Identifiers look like `llamacpp/unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF/Qwen3.5-4B-UD-Q8_K_XL.gguf`; the bare model name without its prefix is not a valid ID.

```bash
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
curl http://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

#### Configure Codex to use SoAI

Add a provider to `~/.codex/config.toml`. The `wire_api` value tells [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) to use the Responses protocol, which SoAI exposes at `/v1/responses`. Replace `YOUR_MODEL_ID` with a catalog ID and keep the SoAI API key in the environment.

```toml
model = "YOUR_MODEL_ID"
model_provider = "soai"

[model_providers.soai]
name = "SoAI"
base_url = "http://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1"
env_key = "SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
```

Keep this provider block in the user-level file. **[Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) ignores `model_provider` and `model_providers` in a project-local `.codex/config.toml`.**

Use `https://` in `base_url` when SoAI serves TLS. If that certificate comes from the SoAI local root CA rather than a public authority, [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) reports no certificate error and instead retries, printing `Reconnecting... waiting for network` until it gives up, so point [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) at the CA certificate it needs to verify the connection.

```bash
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/soai/data/config/tls/soai-local-root-ca.crt
codex exec 'print the current branch'
```

Start [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) with `codex`, or use `codex exec` for a one-shot check. The request still depends on the selected model and plugin advertising the capabilities [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) asks for. Check the official [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) configuration documentation when your installed CLI reports an unknown provider field.

#### Add SoAI MCP tools

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP configuration**. Enable the MCP runtime and server mode, then set **Tools exposed by server mode**, **Resources exposed by server mode**, and **Prompts exposed by server mode** for [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/). The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)); changing those server settings also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Create a personal token under **MCP > MCP tokens**, which also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Export it, then register the Streamable HTTP endpoint:

```bash
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
codex mcp add soai \
  --url http://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp \
  --bearer-token-env-var SOAI_MCP_TOKEN
codex mcp list
```

`codex mcp list` confirms that the entry is saved; it does not prove that a live MCP session completed. Start [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/), ask it to list or use a harmless read-only tool, and confirm the connection in the client or server log. The server must expose the requested tool. **An MCP token does not authenticate the model provider or a WebUI session.** [MCP overview](#mcp-overview) covers server mode, origins, and exposed tools, resources, and prompts.

#### Separate the failure domains

If [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) cannot load a model, test `/v1/models`, the SoAI API key, the provider base URL, and the model ID. If [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) lists the model but a request fails, compare the requested operation with the model's **Capabilities** card, checking **Responses**, **Tool calling**, and **Parallel tool calls** together. A missing capability is refused during admission, and the error body reports only that validation failed; the SoAI log names the capability that was missing. MCP errors require a separate check of the `/mcp` URL, token, server-mode setting, and exposed tools.

[Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) can also run inside the WebUI terminal. **That gives it a host shell but does not route Codex's model requests through the server unless you configure the provider above.** See [Connect coding agents to SoAI](#connect-coding-agents-to-soai) for the three connection methods.

### Using Crush with SoAI [page: using-crush-with-soai]

[Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush) can use SoAI through a custom `openai-compat` provider and through its HTTP MCP client.

#### Create credentials in SoAI

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. The **MCP** tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)). Create a separate personal token under **MCP > MCP tokens**; token creation also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID and its real context/output limits; this requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)).

#### Configure Crush

Put the following commands in `~/.config/crush/crushrc`. **[Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush) distinguishes the official [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) provider from other compatible servers; SoAI must use `openai-compat`.**

```bash
provider add soai --type openai-compat --name SoAI \
  --base-url "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1" \
  --api-key "${SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY:?set SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY}" \
  --discover-models false

model add soai/YOUR_MODEL_ID --name "SoAI model" \
  --context-window 65536 --default-max-tokens 4096 --can-reason true
model large soai/YOUR_MODEL_ID --max-tokens 4096
model small soai/YOUR_MODEL_ID --max-tokens 1024

mcp add soai --type http --url "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp" \
  --header Authorization "Bearer ${SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}"
```

```bash
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
export SSL_CERT_FILE='/path/to/ca-bundle-containing-soai.pem'
crush run 'Explain what this project does.'
```

Set context, output, reasoning, and image flags to the selected SoAI model's actual capabilities. Ask [Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush) to invoke a harmless exposed tool to verify MCP after loading the configuration.

#### Troubleshooting

If model discovery is enabled, an unavailable or filtered model can change the resulting catalog; the example pins one model deliberately. Model authentication uses the SoAI API key. MCP uses its separate token. **Do not place either secret directly in a committed `crushrc`, and do not disable TLS verification.**

### Using Cursor with SoAI [page: using-cursor-with-soai]

[Cursor Editor and Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/) can use SoAI's MCP server. **Cursor's bring-your-own-key settings cover its listed model providers but do not accept an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible base URL, so this integration is MCP-only.**

#### Configure MCP access

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)).

##### Add SoAI MCP in Cursor Editor

1. Open [Cursor](https://cursor.com/) Settings and select **MCP Tools**.
2. Select **New MCP Server** and open the MCP JSON configuration.
3. Add the Streamable HTTP server below and save.
4. Return to MCP Tools, confirm that `soai` is connected, inspect the discovered tools, and enable only what the workspace needs.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

##### Use the same server in Cursor CLI

[Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/) shares MCP configuration with the editor. Run `cursor-agent mcp list` to inspect connection status and `cursor-agent mcp list-tools soai` to inspect discovered tools. Inside an interactive CLI session, use `/mcp list`. No additional model-provider configuration is needed for this MCP-only path.

### Using DeepSeek Harness with SoAI [page: using-deepseek-harness-with-soai]

[DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com/) can use SoAI as a custom OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions provider.

#### Configure model access

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)).

##### Configure the provider

Add the provider to the Harness `settings.yaml`:

```yaml
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    soai:
      displayName: SoAI
      apiKeyEnv: SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY
      api: openai-completions
      baseURL: https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1
      compat:
        supportsDeveloperRole: true
        maxTokensField: max_tokens
      models:
        - id: YOUR_MODEL_ID
          name: SoAI model
          contextWindow: 65536
          maxTokens: 4096

agent-default-model:
  provider: soai
  model: YOUR_MODEL_ID
```

```bash
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS='/path/to/soai-ca.pem'
dsh
```

##### Connect to SoAI in the DeepSeek Harness Web UI

1. Launch the official browser interface with `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` and open its local URL.
2. Open **Settings > Models** and select **Add provider**.
3. Create a custom provider with ID `soai`, display name `SoAI`, base URL `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, and protocol `openai-completions`.
4. Paste the SoAI API key, add `YOUR_MODEL_ID` to the model list, and set its real context-window and maximum-output values in the advanced model fields. Select **Apply**.
5. Use the conversation's model selector to choose **SoAI > YOUR_MODEL_ID**, then send a short verification prompt.

**Fetch available models** can query the server's OpenAI-compatible model list before applying the provider. **The browser host must trust the server CA.** [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com/) stores the key through its write-only credential service; `settings.yaml` keeps only the generated credential reference.

#### MCP status and connection checks

**[DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com/) does not provide a user-facing remote MCP server configuration.** Use the model-provider connection above. A SoAI MCP token is not used by this integration.

##### Verify and troubleshoot

Send a short prompt and confirm that the server records a Chat Completions request for the selected model. A provider error usually means the base URL, key environment variable, or exact model ID is wrong. A certificate error must be fixed by trusting the server CA. Do not disable TLS.

### Using Discord with SoAI [page: using-discord-with-soai]

A [Discord](https://discord.com/) bot can send messages to SoAI and post the replies back to [Discord](https://discord.com/). Each [Discord](https://discord.com/) channel or direct message becomes a messaging conversation in [Chat](#chat) and uses the model, workspace, sender access, and tools saved with the account.

#### Prepare the Discord bot

1. Sign in to [Discord](https://discord.com/), open its Developer Portal, and create an application, or open the application you want SoAI to use.
2. Open **General Information** and copy the **Application ID**. Then open **Bot** and copy or reset the bot token. The public key and client secret are not bot tokens.
3. Under **Bot** > **Privileged Gateway Intents**, turn on **Message Content Intent** and save the change. If [Discord](https://discord.com/) requires approval for this intent on the application, complete that approval first.
4. Under the application's installation settings, include the **bot** scope for a server install. Give the bot permission to view the intended channels and send messages there, then use the installation link to add it to that server.

Keep the bot token private. SoAI connects to [Discord](https://discord.com/) through the Gateway and does not need a public callback address for this provider.

Ordinary [Discord](https://discord.com/) messages work without a public SoAI address. Agent questions, tool approvals, and secure secret links require an HTTPS **Public Origin**. This can be a private address that the messaging account owner can reach over the local network or a VPN; [Discord](https://discord.com/) does not need to reach it. In the SoAI WebUI, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, selects **Advanced** in the page header, opens **Server**, and sets **Public Origin**. The setting is [`SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN`](#config-SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN).

**Do not expose SoAI to the public internet for [Discord](https://discord.com/).** Keep it behind the private boundary described in [Security hardening](#security-hardening) and use [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls) if the owner needs private remote access.

The **Messaging** tab requires the SoAI permissions named **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), **Public inference API access** ([`OPENAI_API`](#acl-OPENAI_API)), and **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). These permissions do not require an external [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) account or API key. SoAI also needs an available model and the MCP tool catalog before **Add account** can open. Ask an administrator to review your access if the tab is missing.

#### Add Discord in SoAI

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then select **Messaging**.
2. Select **Add account**.
3. Enter an **Account label**, choose **[Discord](https://discord.com/)** as the **Provider**, and select the language for SoAI's built-in provider messages under **Remote response language**.
4. Enter the **Bot token** and **Application ID** from the same [Discord](https://discord.com/) application.
5. Choose who may send messages. For restricted access, leave **Accept messages from anyone** off and enter one numeric [Discord](https://discord.com/) user ID per line under **Authorized provider senders**. [Discord](https://discord.com/) lets you copy a user ID after you enable Developer Mode in your [Discord](https://discord.com/) settings. If you leave the list empty, SoAI accepts no senders.
6. Under **Chat execution**, select a model and agent mode. Choose the workspace folder and display names, then select **Edit parameters** for account-specific model parameters.
7. Choose any MCP tools the account may use. Turn on **Require tool approval** if SoAI should send an approval request to the [Discord](https://discord.com/) conversation before running a tool that requires it.
8. Select **Save**.

**Remote response language** controls built-in command, status, error, and interaction messages. To require a language for model answers, select **Edit parameters** and add that requirement to the **System prompt**.

SoAI treats each supported message from an allowed user in a channel the bot can view as a prompt. The user does not need to mention the bot or enter a command. Limit the bot's [Discord](https://discord.com/) channel permissions if it should answer in only certain channels.

**Everyone admitted in the same [Discord](https://discord.com/) channel shares one SoAI conversation and its model context.** A direct-message channel has its own conversation. Editing or deleting a [Discord](https://discord.com/) message does not change the SoAI transcript; send a new correction instead.

A [Discord](https://discord.com/) message can contain file attachments with or without text. The server downloads each supported attachment, processes it with the same attachment pipeline used by Chat, and gives it to the model with the message. The file is also visible with that message in the matching Chat conversation. [Discord](https://discord.com/) and server file limits still apply. See [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context) for how models use different file types.

[Discord](https://discord.com/) supports the text-only commands `/help`, `/status`, `/cancel`, and `/new`. See [Connect messaging apps to SoAI](#connect-messaging-apps-to-soai) for what they do and how to answer agent questions or tool approval requests.

Keep **Allow plaintext secret replies** off unless you accept the risk of a secret appearing in [Discord](https://discord.com/) history or notifications. See [Secrets vault](#secrets-vault) for how tools request and store credentials.

#### Use the conversation in SoAI Chat

You can open the [Discord](https://discord.com/) conversation in [Chat](#chat) and send a message there. That message and its immediate reply stay in Chat; neither is copied to [Discord](https://discord.com/). Both remain in the conversation transcript, so the model can use them as context when it answers a later [Discord](https://discord.com/) message.

Files attached to a message sent from Chat also stay there. **They can affect later model replies, but the server does not forward them to [Discord](https://discord.com/).**

Chat locks the model, agent mode, workspace, display names, parameters, and MCP tools saved with the messaging account. To change them, or to update the [Discord](https://discord.com/) credentials or sender policy, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, select **Messaging**, and use **Edit** for the account.

This account can have its own context length and therefore its own effective compaction limit. Under **Chat execution**, select **Edit parameters**, then set **Context length (tokens)** under **Model settings**. Clear it to use the selected model's default. A lower value gives this account a smaller context budget, so SoAI compacts older context sooner. If a smaller model gives worse answers as a conversation grows, lowering this value can keep its active prompt shorter without changing your other messaging accounts.

Automatic context compaction lets the conversation continue without a fixed message-count limit. SoAI keeps recent turns and may replace older details with a summary before sending the next prompt to the model. See [Chat](#chat) for more about context compaction.

#### Check the connection

The account row under **Settings** > **Messaging** can show **[Discord](https://discord.com/) Gateway starting** while SoAI opens the connection. Wait for **Active** and **Provider connection healthy**, then send a message in a channel the bot can view or open a direct message with it. The sender must match the account's sender policy. The setup works when SoAI replies in [Discord](https://discord.com/) and the conversation appears in the SoAI Chat sidebar.

#### Fix common setup problems

If SoAI rejects the token, copy the bot token from **Developer Portal** > **Bot**. If it reports an application mismatch, copy the Application ID from the application that owns that bot. If it reports that Message Content intent is unavailable, enable the intent, save the [Discord](https://discord.com/) setting, and edit the SoAI account to try again.

A saved account shows **Degraded** when provider activation fails. Check the [Discord](https://discord.com/) bot's channel permissions and the credentials in **Settings** > **Messaging** > **Edit**, then save the account again.

### Using Gemini CLI with SoAI [page: using-gemini-cli-with-soai]

[Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/) can connect to SoAI's Streamable HTTP MCP server. This gives the client access to the tools that an administrator exposes. **The custom base URL in [Gemini CLI](https://gemini.google.com/) speaks the [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) API rather than the OpenAI-compatible protocol, so this connection is MCP-only.**

#### Configure and verify MCP access

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **MCP > MCP tokens**.
2. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ). Create a personal MCP token and copy it when shown; token creation also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ).
3. Enabling the MCP runtime and server mode and selecting the tools, resources, and prompts exposed to remote clients also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

##### Add the server

Merge this entry into the user or trusted-project [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) settings:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "type": "http",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS='/path/to/soai-ca.pem'
gemini mcp list
gemini
```

Open [Gemini CLI](https://gemini.google.com/) inside a workspace you trust through its normal folder-trust prompt. Enter `/mcp` to open the interactive MCP status panel, confirm that `soai` and its tools are connected, then ask it to use a harmless exposed read-only tool. **A saved list entry alone is not sufficient evidence.**

##### Security and troubleshooting

**Do not disable folder trust globally and do not disable TLS verification.** If the server is configured but no tools appear, check the separate server-mode switch, exposed-tool list, MCP token, and `/mcp` URL. Gemini's model authentication remains independent from the MCP token.

### Using GitHub Copilot with SoAI [page: using-github-copilot-with-soai]

[GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) has two separate SoAI connections. The standalone Copilot app can use SoAI as an OpenAI-compatible model provider. [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/), Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent, and Copilot code review can use SoAI as an MCP server. Configure only the surface you use.

#### Use SoAI models in the Copilot app

[GitHub](https://github.com/) currently labels custom model providers in the [GitHub Copilot app](https://github.com/features/copilot) as a public preview. This path requires the app and sign-in with a [GitHub](https://github.com/) account. A Copilot plan is not required when you supply the model provider.

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown.
2. Open **Models** and copy the exact ID of a model that supports the endpoint and capabilities the Copilot app will use. This requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
3. In the Copilot app, open app settings, select **Model providers**, then **Add provider**.
4. Choose **Any OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint**. Enter a display name, base URL `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, and the SoAI API key, then select **Add provider**.
5. Select the SoAI model in the app's model picker and send a short request. The app stores the credential in the operating system's credential store.

This model-provider setup applies to the standalone Copilot app. **It does not change the provider used by Copilot in [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/), Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent, or Copilot code review.**

#### Connect local MCP clients

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)).

##### Local VS Code Agent

This path requires [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) 1.99 or later and access to Copilot. For an account managed by a [GitHub](https://github.com/) Business or Enterprise organization, an administrator must also enable the **MCP servers in Copilot** policy.

1. Open the Command Palette and run **MCP: Add Server**.
2. Choose **HTTP**, enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`, and choose a user or workspace scope.
3. Open the generated `mcp.json` and add a secure prompted input for the bearer token as shown below.
4. Run **MCP: List Servers**, start `soai`, accept the trust prompt, then use **Configure Tools** in Agent chat to enable only required tools.

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "soai-mcp-token",
      "description": "SoAI MCP token",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "soai": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:soai-mcp-token}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### Copilot CLI

Use the interactive `/mcp add` form, or run:

```bash
copilot mcp add --transport http \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" \
  --tools "read_only_tool_a,read_only_tool_b" \
  soai https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp

copilot mcp list
```

User-level configuration is stored in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`; project configuration may use `.mcp.json` or `.github/mcp.json`. Avoid `--show-secrets` in shared terminals or logs.

#### Copilot cloud agent and code review

1. As a repository administrator, open the repository on [GitHub](https://github.com/). Select **Settings**, then under **Code, planning, and automation**, select **Copilot > MCP servers**.
2. Add a remote server with type `http`, its HTTPS URL, and an explicit `tools` list. The hosted services execute enabled tools autonomously, so prefer a narrow read-only list instead of `*`.
3. Create an Agents secret named `COPILOT_MCP_SOAI_TOKEN` and reference it from the Authorization header, then select **Save MCP configuration**.
4. If code review should use the server, open **Copilot > Code review** and leave **Allow Copilot to use MCP tools when reviewing pull requests** on. The setting is on by default.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://PUBLIC_SOAI_HOST/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer $COPILOT_MCP_SOAI_TOKEN"
      },
      "tools": ["read_only_tool_a", "read_only_tool_b"]
    }
  }
}
```

Repository MCP configuration is shared by Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review. Both support MCP tools but not MCP resources or prompts, and neither asks for approval before using an enabled tool. GitHub's hosted services cannot reach a private LAN address such as `192.168.x.x` or trust a private SoAI CA automatically. This flow requires a deliberately exposed, publicly resolvable HTTPS endpoint with a publicly trusted certificate and suitable network controls. **Do not expose SoAI merely to make this integration work.**

### Using goose with SoAI [page: using-goose-with-soai]

[goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) can route its OpenAI-compatible model requests through SoAI and can load SoAI as a remote Streamable HTTP extension.

#### Connect the model API

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown.
2. For tools, open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a personal token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing server mode or exposed tools also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).
3. Open **Models** and copy an exact Chat Completions model ID with tool-calling support. This requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).

##### Configure the model provider

Select the [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) provider in `goose configure`. Set its host to the SoAI origin and its base path to `v1/chat/completions`. The equivalent environment and configuration are:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export OPENAI_HOST='https://SOAI_HOST:5090'
export OPENAI_BASE_PATH='v1/chat/completions'
export SSL_CERT_FILE='/path/to/ca-bundle-containing-soai.pem'
```

```yaml
active_provider: openai
providers:
  openai:
    enabled: true
    model: YOUR_MODEL_ID
    configured: true
```

Start a session and send a short prompt. [goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) distinguishes `OPENAI_HOST` from `OPENAI_BASE_PATH`; a wrong path normally produces a 404.

##### Connect goose Desktop to the SoAI model API

1. Open the sidebar, select **Settings**, then open the **Models** tab.
2. Select **Configure providers**, choose **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**, and enter the SoAI API key.
3. Set **Host URL** to `https://SOAI_HOST:5090`. [goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) uses the default `v1/chat/completions` base path.
4. Submit the provider, select **Switch models**, choose **Use custom model**, and enter `YOUR_MODEL_ID`.

The model name at the bottom of [goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) Desktop is a shortcut to **Change Model**. **The desktop process must trust the SoAI CA before provider verification can succeed.**

#### Connect MCP tools

Merge this entry into `~/.config/goose/config.yaml`:

```yaml
extensions:
  soai:
    type: streamable_http
    name: soai
    description: SoAI MCP
    enabled: true
    uri: https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ${SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}"
    env_keys:
      - SOAI_MCP_TOKEN
    envs: {}
    timeout: 60
```

```bash
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
goose session
```

Verify the live connection by asking [goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) to list or use a harmless exposed read-only tool; a saved extension alone does not confirm a completed handshake.

##### Connect goose Desktop to SoAI MCP

1. Open the sidebar, select **Extensions**, then select **Add custom extension**.
2. Choose **Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP)**, set the ID and name to `soai`, and set the URL to `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`.
3. Add the request header `Authorization` with value `Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN`, choose an appropriate timeout, and select **Add**.
4. Confirm that the extension is enabled, then ask [goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) to use a harmless exposed SoAI tool.

[goose](https://goose-docs.ai/) stores a header entered in the Desktop form in its extension configuration. Treat that configuration as a secret and prefer the environment-referenced YAML form above on shared systems.
