### Using Hermes Agent with SoAI [page: using-hermes-agent-with-soai]

[Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) can use a SoAI model through a custom OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions provider and can load SoAI tools through its native remote-MCP client.

#### Prepare SoAI credentials

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown.
2. For tools, open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a personal token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing server mode or exposed tools also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).
3. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID. This requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ). Choose a model whose capabilities include Chat Completions and tool calling when [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) will use tools.

#### Configure model access

Add the following to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) reads the SoAI API key from the named environment variable. Set `ssl_ca_cert` to a CA bundle that contains the SoAI certificate authority.

```yaml
model:
  provider: custom:soai
  default: YOUR_MODEL_ID

providers:
  soai:
    base_url: https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1
    key_env: SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY
    transport: chat_completions
    default_model: YOUR_MODEL_ID
    models:
      - YOUR_MODEL_ID
    ssl_ca_cert: /path/to/soai-ca-bundle.pem
```

```bash
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
hermes -m YOUR_MODEL_ID -z 'Explain what this project does.'
```

##### Connect Hermes to SoAI in Hermes Dashboard

1. Start `hermes dashboard` and open the local dashboard address it prints.
2. Open **Config**, select the **model** section, and enter the same provider, default model, and SoAI base URL shown in the YAML above. Select **Save**.
3. Open **API Keys**, store the SoAI key under the environment-variable name used by the provider, then start a new session. Existing sessions can use `/reload` to reload dashboard-managed keys.
4. Open **Models** to select `YOUR_MODEL_ID` as the main model, then use **Chat** to send a verification prompt.

The dashboard edits the same profile-scoped configuration as the CLI. Check the profile switcher before saving when more than one [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) profile exists.

#### Configure MCP access

**[Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) expands `${VAR}` references in remote-server headers at connection time, so the token does not need to be written into the YAML.** Merge this entry into the same configuration:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  soai:
    url: https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ${SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}"
    ssl_verify: /path/to/soai-ca-bundle.pem
    enabled: true
```

```bash
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
hermes mcp test soai
```

A successful test performs a live connection and lists exposed tools. The official [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) documentation linked below covers filtering and timeout fields.

##### Connect Hermes to SoAI MCP in Hermes Dashboard

1. Open **MCP**, select **Add Server**, and choose **HTTP/SSE**.
2. Set the name to `soai`, the URL to `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`, and **Authentication** to **Bearer token**.
3. Paste the personal SoAI MCP token and select **Add**. [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) stores the secret in the selected profile's `.env` and keeps only an environment reference in `config.yaml`.
4. Select **Test** for the server and confirm that [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/) lists the exposed SoAI tools.

#### Troubleshooting

**A model failure is independent of an MCP failure.** Check `/v1/models`, the custom provider name, model ID, and SoAI API key for inference. Check the `/mcp` URL, personal MCP token, server mode, and exposed-tool list for tools. Never set `ssl_verify: false`; supply the SoAI CA instead.

### Using Kilo Code with SoAI [page: using-kilo-code-with-soai]

[Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/) exposes user-facing configuration for both a custom OpenAI-compatible provider and remote MCP servers.

#### Prepare SoAI

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
2. For MCP, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

#### Connect Kilo Code to the SoAI model API

1. Open [Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/), select the settings gear, and open **Providers**.
2. At the bottom, add a **Custom provider**. Choose a provider ID and display name, then set **Provider API** to **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Compatible**.
3. Enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1` and the SoAI API key.
4. Fetch the model list or add an exact model ID. Set its context, output, tool, image, and reasoning capabilities to match the SoAI catalog, then submit the provider.
5. Select the new provider and model in the model picker.

#### Connect Kilo Code to SoAI MCP in its interface

1. Open **Settings > Agent Behaviour > MCP Servers**.
2. Select **Add Server**, choose **Remote (HTTP)**, and enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`.
3. Add `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN` as a header and disable OAuth for this static bearer-token connection.
4. Save, confirm the server is active, and approve a harmless tool when prompted.

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "soai": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" },
      "oauth": false,
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 15000
    }
  }
}
```

### Using LibreChat with SoAI [page: using-librechat-with-soai]

[LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) can use SoAI models through a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint and its Streamable HTTP MCP server with static bearer authentication.

#### Connect the model API

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown.
2. If [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) will use MCP, open **Settings > MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a personal token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ).
3. Choose a server address reachable from the [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) server or container and present in its TLS certificate's subject alternative names.
4. Make the [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) process trust the server CA, for example with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. Mount the CA into the container when [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) runs in [Docker](https://www.docker.com/).

##### Add the custom endpoint

Merge a custom-endpoint entry into `librechat.yaml` and supply secrets through [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) environment interpolation:

```yaml
version: 1.3.14

endpoints:
  custom:
    - name: SoAI
      apiKey: '${SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY}'
      baseURL: 'https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1'
      models:
        default:
          - 'YOUR_MODEL_ID'
        fetch: true
      titleConvo: false
      modelDisplayLabel: SoAI
```

The YAML holds only the reference, so define `SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) reads. Restart [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) after changing its YAML, select the **SoAI** endpoint, choose a discovered model, and send a short prompt.

##### Use LibreChat's browser administration

If your deployment includes LibreChat's separate Admin Panel, sign in as a [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) administrator, open its configuration editor, and create the same `endpoints.custom` entry shown above: name `SoAI`, base URL `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, the SoAI API key, and the allowed model IDs. Save the configuration, then sign in again so the login-time configuration takes effect. Select **SoAI** and the model in a new chat before testing inference.

#### Connect MCP tools

```yaml
mcpSettings:
  allowedAddresses:
    - 'SOAI_HOST:5090'

mcpServers:
  soai:
    type: streamable-http
    url: https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp
    requiresOAuth: false
    headers:
      Authorization: 'Bearer ${SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}'
    timeout: 120000
```

**The explicit `requiresOAuth: false` is required for this static-header flow.** Without it, [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) can interpret the unauthenticated bearer challenge as an OAuth requirement and postpone normal server initialization. Keep `allowedAddresses` limited to the exact private host and port when [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) runs on another machine or in a container.

##### Connect LibreChat to SoAI MCP in its interface

1. Open **MCP Settings** from the right sidebar and select **+**.
2. Set the server name to `soai`, enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`, and choose **Streamable HTTP**.
3. Choose API-key authentication, select **Bearer**, and enable **User provides key** so each [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) user supplies a personal MCP token.
4. Create the server, open its connection controls, enter the personal token, and select **Initialize**. Confirm that its status becomes connected.
5. In a chat using the **SoAI** endpoint and a tool-capable model, open the MCP dropdown below the message input and enable `soai`. Ask for a harmless exposed tool action.

UI-created servers do not require a [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) restart. YAML-created servers do. **If the settings panel is hidden, the [LibreChat](https://www.librechat.ai/) administrator must grant the relevant MCP-server permission or define a server that needs user initialization.**

### Using LiteLLM with SoAI [page: using-litellm-with-soai]

[LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) can place another OpenAI-compatible gateway in front of SoAI and can also aggregate its MCP server. **Use this only when you need LiteLLM's key, budget, or routing layer; clients can otherwise connect directly.**

#### Connect and use the model API

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
2. For MCP, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

##### Add a LiteLLM model

In `config.yaml`, route an alias to the server with LiteLLM's custom [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) provider:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: soai-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/YOUR_MODEL_ID
      api_base: os.environ/SOAI_BASE_URL
      api_key: os.environ/SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY
```

```bash
export SOAI_BASE_URL='https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1'
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
```

[LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) resolves both `os.environ` references from the proxy's own environment, so set them before starting the proxy with that configuration, then send an [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Chat Completions request to [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) using the alias `soai-model`.

##### Use the LiteLLM interface

1. Sign in to LiteLLM's Admin UI and open **Models + Endpoints**.
2. Select **Add Model**, choose the custom [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) provider, and enter the model ID, base URL, and key.
3. Save, run the model health/test action, and use the alias from a [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) client.

#### Add the MCP server to LiteLLM

1. Open **MCP Servers** in the [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) UI and select **Add New MCP Server**.
2. Enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`, choose **Streamable HTTP**, set authentication to **Bearer token**, and supply the personal MCP token.
3. Save and confirm that [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) discovers the selected tools. Grant access only to the required [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) keys, teams, or users.

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  soai:
    url: https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp
    transport: http
    auth_type: bearer_token
    authentication_token: os.environ/SOAI_MCP_TOKEN
```

[LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) clients authenticate to [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) separately. **Do not confuse a [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) virtual key with either the upstream SoAI API key or MCP token.** Store the MCP token through LiteLLM's protected configuration or Admin UI rather than committing it to source control.

### Using LM Studio with SoAI [page: using-lm-studio-with-soai]

[LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) is a local model host, not a client for selecting a remote SoAI OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible model. Its relevant SoAI integration is MCP: a model loaded by [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) can call tools from SoAI's Streamable HTTP server.

#### Prepare SoAI MCP

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)), and creating a personal token also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Changing server mode or its exposed tools also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Trust the SoAI CA on the [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) host.

#### Add the server in LM Studio

1. For app chat, open the right-side **Program** tab, select **Install**, then **Edit mcp.json**. For local-server use, open **Developer > Local Server** and select **mcp.json**.
2. Add the entry below and replace `YOUR_MCP_TOKEN` with the actual personal SoAI MCP token.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

LM Studio's documented `mcp.json` format puts the header value in the file. Restrict access to that file. For app chat, load a tool-capable local model, enable the `soai` program in the chat, and approve a harmless read-only call.

#### Enable MCP for the local API server

1. Open **Developer > Local Server > Server Settings**.
2. Enable **Require Authentication**, then enable **Allow calling servers from mcp.json**. [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) requires authentication before it permits this server-wide MCP setting.
3. Open **Manage Tokens** and select **Create new token**. For that token, set **Allow calling servers from mcp.json** to **Allow**, then copy the token.
4. Start the local server from **Developer > Local Server**. Requests to [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) must use this LM Studio token; it is separate from the SoAI MCP token stored in `mcp.json`.

**Synchronizing `mcp.json` does not grant the local API server permission to use the integration.** If a request returns `Permission denied to use plugin`, open the [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) application and enable **Allow calling servers from mcp.json** in local-server settings.

In an `/api/v1/chat` request, attach `{"type":"plugin","id":"mcp/soai"}` in the `integrations` array. Use its `allowed_tools` field to expose only the tools needed for the task; sending a large MCP catalog can exceed a local model's context window.

#### Architecture and troubleshooting

**Do not enter SoAI's `/v1` URL as an [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) remote model provider: that reverses the intended roles.** [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) hosts the model; SoAI supplies MCP tools. For a permission error, enable the explicit local-server MCP permission. For connection errors after permission is enabled, check the token, CA trust, server mode, exposed tools, and `/mcp` URL.

### Using OpenClaw with SoAI [page: using-openclaw-with-soai]

[OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai/) can use SoAI through a custom OpenAI-compatible model provider and can connect separately to its MCP server.

#### Prepare the server

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
2. For MCP, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

#### Connect OpenClaw to the SoAI model API in Control UI

1. Start the [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai/) Gateway and open its dashboard.
2. Open **Settings > Model Providers** and add a custom provider.
3. Set its base URL to `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, API protocol to **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Completions**, and enter the SoAI API key in the API key field.
4. Add an exact model ID and its real context window, output limit, modalities, cost values, and verified compatibility capabilities.
5. Use **Test connection**. Then select the provider/model in **Default models** and save.

Choose [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Responses only for a model that advertises Responses support. **[OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai/) sends model requests to the configured base URL, so use only a trusted server address.**

#### Connect OpenClaw to SoAI MCP in Control UI

1. Open **Settings > MCP**, also available at `/settings/mcp`.
2. Use the scoped MCP editor to add a remote HTTP server with `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp` and the bearer Authorization header.
3. Select **Save & Publish** so the running Gateway applies the change, then use `openclaw mcp doctor --probe` for a live connection check.
4. In Chat, select **+ > Connectors** to enable `soai` for the current session. Apply narrow server and tool filters before approving calls.

#### Configuration equivalent

```json
{
  "models": {
    "providers": {
      "soai": {
        "baseUrl": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1",
        "apiKey": {
          "source": "env",
          "provider": "default",
          "id": "SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY"
        },
        "api": "openai-completions",
        "models": [
          {
            "id": "YOUR_MODEL_ID",
            "name": "SoAI model",
            "reasoning": false,
            "input": ["text"],
            "contextWindow": 32768,
            "maxTokens": 4096
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "soai": {
        "transport": "streamable-http",
        "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
        "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Set both environment variables before starting [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai/). Replace the example limits and capabilities with values supported by the selected model; they are placeholders, not recommendations. Keep the SoAI API key and MCP token separate.

### Using opencode with SoAI [page: using-opencode-with-soai]

[opencode](https://opencode.ai/) can use SoAI for both models and tools. The provider configuration calls SoAI's OpenAI-compatible API, and the MCP configuration calls SoAI's tool server. Keep the two credentials separate.

#### Connect the model API

In the SoAI WebUI, open **Models** from the sidebar and copy the exact model ID shown by the catalog. This requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)). You can also query it from the machine where [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) will run:

```bash
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
curl http://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

Create the SoAI API key in **Settings > [OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears to administrators with the **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)) permission. Open the model's **Capabilities** card before selecting it in [opencode](https://opencode.ai/); SoAI checks that profile for chat, tool calls, structured output, and other requested fields.

##### Configure the provider

Create `opencode.json` in the project directory, or place the same provider block in your global [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) configuration. Replace `YOUR_MODEL_ID` with the ID returned by `/v1/models` and keep the key in the environment.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "soai": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "SoAI",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1",
        "apiKey": "{env:SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY}"
      },
      "models": {
        "YOUR_MODEL_ID": {
          "name": "SoAI model"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**The provider must use `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` for SoAI's chat-completions surface.** For current provider fields and configuration precedence, see the official [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) documentation linked below.

##### Finish in the opencode interface

1. Start [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) and enter `/connect`.
2. Select **Other**, enter `soai` as the provider ID, and paste the SoAI API key. The ID must match the `soai` key in `opencode.json`.
3. Enter `/models` and select **SoAI > YOUR_MODEL_ID**, then send a short prompt.

**The `/connect` dialog stores the credential only; it does not create the provider definition or base URL.** Keep the `opencode.json` block above. For a non-interactive run, use `opencode -m soai/YOUR_MODEL_ID`.

#### Add SoAI tools through MCP

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP configuration** and enable the MCP runtime and server mode. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)); changing those server settings also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Create a personal token in **MCP > MCP tokens**. Token creation also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Set **Tools exposed by server mode**, **Resources exposed by server mode**, and **Prompts exposed by server mode** for the operations [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) may use. Then merge this `mcp` block into the same top-level object as `provider`. Set `oauth` to `false` because SoAI uses the bearer token in this configuration rather than an OAuth flow. Set `SOAI_MCP_TOKEN` in the environment before starting [opencode](https://opencode.ai/).

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "soai": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "http://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "enabled": true,
      "oauth": false,
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer {env:SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Use `opencode mcp list` to inspect the connection. The official [opencode](https://opencode.ai/) documentation covers its remote-server configuration; [MCP overview](#mcp-overview) explains SoAI-side permissions.

#### Check failures

A model-list failure can mean the base URL is wrong, the SoAI API key is missing, or the SoAI model is not available. If `soai/YOUR_MODEL_ID` returns an unsupported-capability error, select a model or plugin whose **Capabilities** card includes the requested operation. An MCP failure is separate: check the `/mcp` URL, token, server-mode setting, and exposed tools. **Do not place the MCP URL under the provider's `baseURL`; they are different protocols.**

### Using OpenHands CLI with SoAI [page: using-openhands-cli-with-soai]

[OpenHands CLI](https://openhands.dev/) can use SoAI through an OpenAI-compatible model and can load remote MCP tools from the same server.

#### Configure the model

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Copy an exact model ID from **Models**; this requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)). Then start [OpenHands](https://openhands.dev/) with these environment variables:

```bash
export LLM_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export LLM_BASE_URL='https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1'
export LLM_MODEL='openai/YOUR_MODEL_ID'
export SSL_CERT_FILE='/path/to/ca-bundle-containing-soai.pem'
openhands --override-with-envs
```

The `openai/` prefix selects OpenHands' OpenAI-compatible adapter and is not part of the model ID. `--override-with-envs` applies the `LLM_*` environment variables to that run. **It does not save them to [OpenHands](https://openhands.dev/) settings.**

#### Connect OpenHands to the SoAI model API in OpenHands settings

1. Run `openhands`, press **Ctrl+P** to open the command palette, and select **Settings**.
2. Choose the OpenAI-compatible provider and enter `openai/YOUR_MODEL_ID` as the model, `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1` as the base URL, and the SoAI API key.
3. Save the settings and send a short verification prompt. The change applies without restarting [OpenHands](https://openhands.dev/).

#### Configure MCP and check integration limits

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)), and creating a personal token also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Create the token, then add the remote server. **The command writes the resolved header into `~/.openhands/mcp.json`; restrict access to that file.**

```bash
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
openhands mcp add soai --transport http \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOAI_MCP_TOKEN" \
  https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp
openhands mcp list
```

Restart the [OpenHands](https://openhands.dev/) session after changing MCP configuration and confirm that a harmless tool is available.

##### Limits and troubleshooting

**The CLI's [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) layer may separately warn when it cannot refresh public model pricing; that does not establish a server failure.** Diagnose model and MCP credentials independently. Trust the server CA instead of disabling TLS.

### Using Open WebUI with SoAI [page: using-open-webui-with-soai]

[Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) can use SoAI as an OpenAI-compatible model connection and native Streamable HTTP MCP tool server.

#### Connect the model API

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown.
2. Open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a separate personal token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ).
3. Open **Models** and confirm the models intended for [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) advertise Chat Completions and the tool/structured-output capabilities the UI will request. This requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).

##### Add the model connection

1. Sign in to [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) as an administrator.
2. Open **Admin Settings > Connections > [OpenAI](https://openai.com/)** and add a connection.
3. Set the URL to `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1` and paste the SoAI API key.
4. Save, refresh the model list, and select an exact model ID in a new chat.

A populated picker confirms model discovery; send a message to confirm inference.

#### Add native MCP tools

**Native MCP requires [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) 0.6.31 or newer.**

1. As an [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) administrator, open **Admin Settings > Integrations** and select **+**.
2. Select **MCP (Streamable HTTP)**, enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`, and configure **Bearer** authentication with the personal MCP token in the **Key** field.
3. Select **Save**, then use **Verify Connection** and confirm that the server returns its exposed tools.
4. Open a chat, select **+ > Integrations > Tools**, and enable the SoAI integration for that chat.

Only an [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) administrator can register an MCP server. Use the integration's Access Control settings when it should be available only to particular [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) users or groups. These permissions are distinct from SoAI's MCP permissions.

#### Deployment and troubleshooting

The [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) server process (including one in a container), rather than only the browser, must trust the server CA. When [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/) also accesses public HTTPS services, use a combined bundle containing the operating-system roots and that CA. **Replacing the system bundle with only that CA can break unrelated downloads.** Never disable TLS verification.

##### Troubleshooting

If models appear but chat fails, inspect the selected model's capabilities and the SoAI API key. If MCP verification fails, inspect the separate MCP token, URL, server-mode switch, and exposed-tool list. **Do not paste the MCP token into the [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) connection or the SoAI API key into the MCP connection.**

### Using Pi with SoAI [page: using-pi-with-soai]

[Pi](https://pi.dev/) can use SoAI through a custom OpenAI-compatible model catalog. [Pi](https://pi.dev/) deliberately does not include an MCP client, so this integration covers model inference.

#### Configure model access

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Then open **Models** and copy the exact ID of a model that supports Chat Completions and has enough context and tool capability for the intended workflow. This requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)).

##### Add SoAI to Pi's model catalog

Add a provider to `~/.pi/agent/models.json`. [Pi](https://pi.dev/) supports environment-variable substitution in `apiKey`; keep the secret in the environment.

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "soai": {
      "baseUrl": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1",
      "apiKey": "${SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY}",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "models": [
        {
          "id": "YOUR_MODEL_ID",
          "name": "SoAI model",
          "reasoning": false,
          "input": ["text"],
          "contextWindow": 65536,
          "maxTokens": 4096
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
export SOAI_OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS='/path/to/soai-ca.pem'
pi --provider soai --model YOUR_MODEL_ID --print 'Explain what this project does.'
```

Match `contextWindow`, `maxTokens`, reasoning, and input modalities to the selected model rather than copying optimistic values. The official [Pi](https://pi.dev/) documentation linked below describes these fields.

##### Select SoAI in Pi's interface

1. Start `pi` after saving `models.json`.
2. Enter `/model`, or press **Ctrl+L**, to open the model selector.
3. Choose provider **soai** and model **YOUR_MODEL_ID**, then send a short prompt.

Pi's picker can select a custom provider after it exists in `models.json`, but it does not create the provider or base URL. Use `--provider` and `--model` for headless selection.

#### MCP support and troubleshooting

**[Pi](https://pi.dev/) does not include an MCP client.** Creating a SoAI MCP token does not make tools appear in [Pi](https://pi.dev/); use an MCP-capable client when SoAI tools are required.

##### Troubleshooting

If [Pi](https://pi.dev/) cannot find the model, check the provider ID and the exact catalog model ID. For TLS errors, make the server CA available to [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. **Do not disable certificate verification.**

### Using Qwen Code with SoAI [page: using-qwen-code-with-soai]

[Qwen Code](https://qwen.ai/qwencode) can use SoAI as an OpenAI-compatible model provider and as a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server.

#### Configure model access

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown.
2. Open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a personal token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing server mode or its exposed tools also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).
3. Open **Models** and copy the exact ID of a Chat Completions model. This requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).

##### Configure the model provider

Merge this provider into `~/.qwen/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "security": {
    "auth": { "selectedType": "openai" }
  },
  "modelProviders": {
    "openai": [
      {
        "id": "YOUR_MODEL_ID",
        "name": "SoAI model",
        "envKey": "OPENAI_API_KEY",
        "baseUrl": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY='YOUR_SOAI_API_KEY'
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS='/path/to/soai-ca.pem'
qwen --model YOUR_MODEL_ID
```

##### Select SoAI in Qwen Code

Start `qwen`, enter `/model`, and select **openai > YOUR_MODEL_ID**. The picker reads the provider entry from `settings.json`; it does not create the base URL. Send a short prompt after selection to verify the model connection.

#### Configure MCP and troubleshoot the connection

```bash
export SOAI_MCP_TOKEN='YOUR_MCP_TOKEN'
qwen mcp add --scope user --transport http \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOAI_MCP_TOKEN" \
  soai https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp
qwen mcp list
```

**The add command writes the resolved header to the selected Qwen settings scope, so protect that file as a secret.** Start [Qwen Code](https://qwen.ai/qwencode) in a trusted workspace, enter `/mcp`, and confirm that the interactive MCP dialog reports `soai` as connected and exposes its tools.

##### Troubleshooting

**Trust the workspace through Qwen Code's normal trust prompt; do not globally disable workspace security.** Model failures use the SoAI API key and `/v1` URL, while MCP failures use the separate token and `/mcp` URL. For either TLS path, trust the server CA with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.

### Using Roo Code with SoAI [page: using-roo-code-with-soai]

[Roo Code](https://roocode.com/) can use SoAI as an OpenAI-compatible model provider and as a separate Streamable HTTP MCP server.

#### Prepare SoAI

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
2. For MCP, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

#### Connect Roo Code to the SoAI model API

1. Open the [Roo Code](https://roocode.com/) pane, select its settings gear, and choose **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/) Compatible** as the API provider.
2. Set the base URL to `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, paste the SoAI API key, and enter an exact SoAI model ID.
3. Open the advanced model settings and declare the context window, output limit, image support, and other capabilities truthfully. [Roo Code](https://roocode.com/) requires native tool calling for agent tool use.
4. Save, select the model, and send a short task.

#### Connect Roo Code to SoAI MCP in its interface

1. Select the **MCP Servers** icon in the top navigation of the [Roo Code](https://roocode.com/) pane.
2. Scroll down and select **Edit Global MCP**, or **Edit Project MCP** for a workspace configuration.
3. Add the entry below, save it, and confirm that the server appears as connected.
4. Leave `alwaysAllow` empty initially and disable any tools the project does not need.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" },
      "alwaysAllow": [],
      "disabled": false,
      "timeout": 120
    }
  }
}
```

### Using SillyTavern with SoAI [page: using-sillytavern-with-soai]

[SillyTavern](https://sillytavern.app/) can chat through SoAI's OpenAI-compatible API. **[SillyTavern](https://sillytavern.app/) does not provide a native Streamable HTTP MCP client, so this integration covers model inference.**

#### Connect the model API and understand MCP limits

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ([`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN)). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact ID of a model that supports Chat Completions; this requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)).

##### Connect through the SillyTavern interface

1. Open **API Connections**.
2. Set **API type** to **Chat Completion**.
3. Set **Chat Completion Source** to **Custom (OpenAI-compatible)**.
4. Enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1` as the custom endpoint and paste the SoAI API key. Do not append `/chat/completions`; [SillyTavern](https://sillytavern.app/) adds the endpoint path.
5. Refresh the model list and select an exact model ID. If discovery is unavailable, enter the ID manually.
6. Select **Test Message**, then save the connection as a Connection Profile if it should be reused.

**Generic compatibility does not imply every [SillyTavern](https://sillytavern.app/) sampler or extension field is accepted.** Use controls supported by the selected model and inspect server logs if a request is rejected.

##### MCP boundary

**Do not add `/mcp` as a chat endpoint.** It is not an OpenAI-compatible inference route. Use a documented [SillyTavern](https://sillytavern.app/) extension or a separate gateway when tools are required.

### Using Telegram with SoAI [page: using-telegram-with-soai]

A [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) bot can send messages to SoAI and return the replies in [Telegram](https://telegram.org/). Each [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) chat becomes a messaging conversation in [Chat](#chat) and uses the model, workspace, sender access, and tools saved with the account.

#### Prepare Telegram and SoAI

1. In [Telegram](https://telegram.org/), search for and open the verified **@[BotFather](https://telegram.org/)** account. Run `/newbot` and follow the prompts, or select an existing bot, then copy its bot token.
2. Create a private webhook secret between 16 and 256 characters. Use letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. You will enter this value in SoAI; you do not need to register the webhook yourself.
3. Confirm that the SoAI server has a public HTTPS address. In the SoAI WebUI, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, selects **Advanced** in the page header, opens **Server**, sets **Public Origin**, and selects **Save**. The setting is [`SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN`](#config-SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN).

The public origin must be an HTTPS address whose [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) callback route is reachable from the internet. If a reverse proxy handles TLS, finish that routing first. Enter the base address without a [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) webhook path; SoAI builds and registers the callback. The rest of the SoAI interface can remain private when you follow the selective callback routing in [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls). Keep the bot token and webhook secret private.

**[Telegram](https://telegram.org/) requires the callback route to be public, not the complete SoAI WebUI or API.** Exposing SoAI directly to the public internet is not recommended. Review [Security hardening](#security-hardening) before enabling this integration.

The **Messaging** tab requires the SoAI permissions named **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), **Public inference API access** ([`OPENAI_API`](#acl-OPENAI_API)), and **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). These permissions do not require an external [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) account or API key. SoAI also needs an available model and the MCP tool catalog before **Add account** can open. Ask an administrator to review your access if the tab is missing.

#### Add Telegram in SoAI

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then select **Messaging**.
2. Select **Add account**.
3. Enter an **Account label**, choose **[Telegram](https://telegram.org/)** as the **Provider**, and select the language for SoAI's built-in provider messages under **Remote response language**.
4. Enter the **Bot token** from @ [BotFather](https://telegram.org/) and the private **Webhook secret token**.
5. Choose who may send messages. For restricted access, leave **Accept messages from anyone** off and enter one numeric [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) user ID per line under **Authorized provider senders**. This is the `message.from.id` value in a [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) Bot API update, not a username or chat ID. If you leave the list empty, SoAI accepts no senders.
6. Under **Chat execution**, select a model and agent mode. Choose the workspace folder and display names, then select **Edit parameters** for account-specific model parameters.
7. Choose any MCP tools the account may use. Turn on **Require tool approval** if SoAI should send an approval request to the [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) conversation before running a tool that requires it.
8. Select **Save**.

**Remote response language** controls built-in command, status, error, and interaction messages. To require a language for model answers, select **Edit parameters** and add that requirement to the **System prompt**.

SoAI checks the token before it stores the account, then installs its [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) webhook. If **Save** reports that [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) already sends this bot to a different webhook, turn on **Replace an existing provider callback** only when SoAI may replace it, then select **Save** again. A callback failure after storage leaves the account in **Degraded** state.

A [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) message can contain a photo, document, audio file, voice message, or video, with or without supported message text or a caption. The server downloads the file, processes it with the same attachment pipeline used by Chat, and gives it to the model with the message. The file is also visible with that message in the matching Chat conversation. [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) and server file limits still apply. See [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context) for how models use different file types.

[Telegram](https://telegram.org/) supports `/help`, `/status`, `/cancel`, and `/new`. Use the command by itself in a direct message. In a group, address it to the bot, for example `/new@BotUsername`. See [Connect messaging apps to SoAI](#connect-messaging-apps-to-soai) for what the commands do and how to answer agent questions or tool approval requests.

Keep **Allow plaintext secret replies** off unless you accept the risk of a secret appearing in [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) history or notifications. See [Secrets vault](#secrets-vault) for how tools request and store credentials.

#### Use the conversation in SoAI Chat

You can open the [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) conversation in [Chat](#chat) and send a message there. That message and its immediate reply stay in Chat; neither is copied to [Telegram](https://telegram.org/). Both remain in the conversation transcript, so the model can use them as context when it answers a later [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) message.

Files attached to a message sent from Chat also stay there. **They can affect later model replies, but the server does not forward them to [Telegram](https://telegram.org/).**

Chat locks the model, agent mode, workspace, display names, parameters, and MCP tools saved with the messaging account. To change them, or to update the [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) credentials or sender policy, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, select **Messaging**, and use **Edit** for the account.

This account can have its own context length and therefore its own effective compaction limit. Under **Chat execution**, select **Edit parameters**, then set **Context length (tokens)** under **Model settings**. Clear it to use the selected model's default. A lower value gives this account a smaller context budget, so SoAI compacts older context sooner. If a smaller model gives worse answers as a conversation grows, lowering this value can keep its active prompt shorter without changing your other messaging accounts.

Automatic context compaction lets the conversation continue without a fixed message-count limit. SoAI keeps recent turns and may replace older details with a summary before sending the next prompt to the model. See [Chat](#chat) for more about context compaction.

#### Check the connection

Wait for the account row under **Settings** > **Messaging** to show **Active** and **Provider connection healthy**. Open the bot in [Telegram](https://telegram.org/), select **Start** if [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) shows it, and send a direct message. The sender must match the account's sender policy. The setup works when SoAI replies in [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) and the conversation appears in the SoAI Chat sidebar.

Direct messages provide the simplest test. For a group, add the bot to the group first. SoAI treats each supported message [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) delivers from an allowed user as a prompt; Telegram's [BotFather](https://telegram.org/) privacy setting controls which group messages [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) delivers to the bot.

**Everyone admitted in the same [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) group shares one conversation and its model context.** Each direct chat has its own conversation. Editing or deleting a [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) message does not change the Chat transcript; send a new correction instead.

#### Fix common setup problems

If [Telegram](https://telegram.org/) rejects the credentials, copy the current bot token from @[BotFather](https://telegram.org/) and check the webhook secret. If SoAI reports a callback conflict, confirm that the previous service no longer needs the bot before allowing SoAI to replace its webhook. A missing or non-HTTPS **Public Origin** also prevents callback setup.

A saved account shows **Degraded** when provider activation fails. Correct the public address, credentials, or callback choice under **Settings** > **Messaging** > **Edit**, then save the account again.

### Using WhatsApp with SoAI [page: using-whatsapp-with-soai]

The server can answer messages sent to a [WhatsApp Business](https://www.whatsapp.com/) phone number. Each sender becomes a messaging conversation in [Chat](#chat) and uses the model, workspace, sender access, and tools saved with the account.

#### Prepare WhatsApp and SoAI

1. In the [Meta](https://www.meta.com/) developer console, add the [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) product to an application, connect a [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) Business Account, and add the business phone number that SoAI will use.
2. In [Meta](https://www.meta.com/) Business Settings, create or select a System User, assign it the application and [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) Business Account assets, then generate a permanent access token with `whatsapp_business_management` and `whatsapp_business_messaging` permissions.
3. Copy the Phone number ID and Business account ID from the application's [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) setup. Copy the Application ID and App secret from the same application's basic settings. Note the active Graph API version in the `vNN.N` format, and create a private verify token between 16 and 256 characters for the callback check.
4. Confirm that the SoAI server has a public HTTPS address. In the SoAI WebUI, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, chooses **Settings**, selects **Advanced** in the page header, opens **Server**, sets **Public Origin**, and selects **Save**. The setting is [`SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN`](#config-SERVER.PUBLIC_ORIGIN).

**The application, token, business account, and phone number must belong together.** The public origin must be an HTTPS address whose [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) callback route is reachable from the internet. If a reverse proxy handles TLS, finish that routing first. Enter the base address without a [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) webhook path; SoAI builds and registers the callback. The rest of the SoAI interface can remain private when you follow the selective callback routing in [Network and TLS](#network-and-tls). Keep the access token, App secret, and verify token private.

[WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) requires the callback route to be public, not the complete SoAI WebUI or API. Exposing SoAI directly to the public internet is not recommended. Review [Security hardening](#security-hardening) before enabling this integration.

The **Messaging** tab requires the SoAI permissions named **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)), **Public inference API access** ([`OPENAI_API`](#acl-OPENAI_API)), and **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). These permissions do not require an external [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) account or API key. SoAI also needs an available model and the MCP tool catalog before **Add account** can open. Ask an administrator to review your access if the tab is missing.

#### Add WhatsApp in SoAI

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then select **Messaging**.
2. Select **Add account**.
3. Enter an **Account label**, choose **[WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/)** as the **Provider**, and select the language for SoAI's built-in provider messages under **Remote response language**.
4. Enter the **Access token**, **Phone number ID**, **Business account ID**, **Application ID**, **API version**, **App secret**, and **Verify token** from the same [Meta](https://www.meta.com/) setup.
5. Choose who may send messages. For restricted access, leave **Accept messages from anyone** off and enter one [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) sender ID per line under **Authorized provider senders**. Use the exact `messages[].from` sender ID for that user from a [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) webhook event, not the business **Phone number ID**. If you leave the list empty, SoAI accepts no senders.
6. Under **Chat execution**, select a model and agent mode. Choose the workspace folder and display names, then select **Edit parameters** for account-specific model parameters.
7. Choose any MCP tools the account may use. Turn on **Require tool approval** if SoAI should send an approval request to the [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) conversation before running a tool that requires it.
8. Select **Save**.

**Remote response language** controls built-in command, status, error, and interaction messages. To require a language for model answers, select **Edit parameters** and add that requirement to the **System prompt**.

SoAI checks the [Meta](https://www.meta.com/) application, token permissions, business account, and phone number before it stores the account. It then subscribes the application to messages and installs the [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) callback. If **Save** reports that the application already uses a different callback, turn on **Replace an existing provider callback** only when SoAI may replace it, then select **Save** again. A callback failure after storage leaves the account in **Degraded** state.

A [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) message can contain an image, document, audio file, video, or sticker, with or without supported message text or a caption. The server downloads the file, processes it with the same attachment pipeline used by Chat, and gives it to the model with the message. The file is also visible with that message in the matching Chat conversation. [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) and server file limits still apply. See [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context) for how models use different file types.

[WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) supports the text-only commands `/help`, `/status`, `/cancel`, and `/new`. See [Connect messaging apps to SoAI](#connect-messaging-apps-to-soai) for what they do and how to answer agent questions or tool approval requests.

Keep **Allow plaintext secret replies** off unless you accept the risk of a secret appearing in [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) history or notifications. See [Secrets vault](#secrets-vault) for how tools request and store credentials.

#### Use the conversation in SoAI Chat

You can open the [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) conversation in [Chat](#chat) and send a message there. That message and its immediate reply stay in Chat; neither is copied to [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/). Both remain in the conversation transcript, so the model can use them as context when it answers a later [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) message.

Files attached to a message sent from Chat also stay there. **They can affect later model replies, but the server does not forward them to [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/).**

Chat locks the model, agent mode, workspace, display names, parameters, and MCP tools saved with the messaging account. To change them, or to update the [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) credentials or sender policy, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, select **Messaging**, and use **Edit** for the account.

This account can have its own context length and therefore its own effective compaction limit. Under **Chat execution**, select **Edit parameters**, then set **Context length (tokens)** under **Model settings**. Clear it to use the selected model's default. A lower value gives this account a smaller context budget, so SoAI compacts older context sooner. If a smaller model gives worse answers as a conversation grows, lowering this value can keep its active prompt shorter without changing your other messaging accounts.

Automatic context compaction lets the conversation continue without a fixed message-count limit. SoAI keeps recent turns and may replace older details with a summary before sending the next prompt to the model. See [Chat](#chat) for more about context compaction.

#### Check the connection

Wait for the account row under **Settings** > **Messaging** to show **Active** and **Provider connection healthy**, then send a message to the business number from an allowed [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) number. **A [Meta](https://www.meta.com/) development setup may limit messages to its configured test recipients.** The setup works when SoAI replies in [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) and the conversation appears in the SoAI Chat sidebar.

Each [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) sender has a separate conversation and model context. Editing or deleting a [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) message does not change the Chat transcript; send a new correction instead.

#### Fix common setup problems

If [Meta](https://www.meta.com/) rejects the access token, replace an expiring test token with a permanent System User token and check both required permissions. Application, business account, or phone mismatch errors mean that at least one ID came from a different [Meta](https://www.meta.com/) setup. Copy the values again from the application and [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/) Business Account that own the phone number.

A missing or non-HTTPS **Public Origin** prevents callback setup. If SoAI reports a callback conflict, confirm that the previous service no longer needs the subscription before allowing SoAI to replace it. A saved account shows **Degraded** when activation fails; correct the settings under **Settings** > **Messaging** > **Edit**, then save the account again.

### Using Devin Desktop with SoAI [page: using-devin-desktop-with-soai]

[Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) is the primary local agent in [Devin Desktop](https://docs.devin.ai/) and the default for new tabs when it is available. Connect it to SoAI as an MCP client so it can use the tools, resources, and prompts that the SoAI administrator exposes. [Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) does not accept SoAI as an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible model provider, so this integration adds SoAI tools rather than replacing the model service used by [Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/).

#### Prepare SoAI MCP

In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP configuration**. Enable the MCP runtime and server mode, and limit **Tools exposed by server mode**, **Resources exposed by server mode**, and **Prompts exposed by server mode** to what the workspace needs. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)), and changing server settings also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)).

Open **MCP > MCP tokens**, create a personal token, and copy it when shown. Token creation also requires **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). Keep this token separate from any SoAI API key used for model requests.

#### Select Devin Local

1. Open a new tab in [Devin Desktop](https://docs.devin.ai/) and select **[Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/)** from the agent selector.
2. If it is absent, open the command palette, run **Devin User Settings**, open **Agents**, enable **[Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/)**, and restart [Devin Desktop](https://docs.devin.ai/).

**On an enterprise plan, an administrator must also enable [Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) and MCP access for the team.** If the team enforces an MCP registry or allowlist, it must permit the `soai` server ID and its endpoint before the local configuration can connect.

#### Add SoAI MCP to Devin Local

Use `.devin/mcp_config.local.json` in the workspace for a personal configuration that is excluded from version control. **A shared project entry belongs in `.devin/mcp_config.json` and must not contain a secret.** A user-wide entry belongs in `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json` on [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) and [macOS](https://www.apple.com/macos/) or `%APPDATA%\devin\mcp_config.json` on [Windows](https://www.microsoft.com/windows/).

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "transport": "http",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Set `SOAI_MCP_TOKEN` in the environment inherited by [Devin Desktop](https://docs.devin.ai/) before starting it. The client must trust the certificate authority for the SoAI endpoint; do not disable certificate verification. Local clients on the SoAI host can use `http://127.0.0.1:5090/mcp` instead.

##### Verify the connection and permissions

1. Start a new [Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) session after saving the configuration.
2. Open **Customizations** and confirm that the `soai` MCP server is connected, or run `devin mcp list` in a terminal.
3. Ask [Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) to call one harmless read-only SoAI tool that the server exposes.
4. Review the MCP approval request and allow only the tool or server scope the workspace needs.

[Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) asks before MCP tool calls by default. A missing server normally means the configuration path or JSON is wrong, while a disconnected server can mean the URL, token, certificate trust, SoAI server mode, team policy, or exposed-capability list is blocking the connection.

#### Legacy Cascade configuration

Cascade is the legacy agent in [Devin Desktop](https://docs.devin.ai/). Keep this separate configuration only for an existing Cascade workflow; [Devin Local](https://docs.devin.ai/) does not read it.

1. Select the **MCPs** icon at the top right of Cascade, or open **Devin Settings > Cascade > MCP Servers**.
2. Open `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` and add the entry below.
3. Refresh the MCP list, confirm that `soai` connects, and inspect the enabled tools.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "soai": {
      "serverUrl": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:SOAI_MCP_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Cascade accepts `url` or `serverUrl` for remote servers and supports environment and file interpolation. **Cascade can expose at most 100 tools at once.** If that limit is reached, reduce the SoAI server-mode tool list to the least-privilege set the workspace needs before reconnecting.

### Using Zed Agent with SoAI [page: using-zed-agent-with-soai]

[Zed Agent](https://zed.dev/) can use a custom OpenAI-compatible SoAI provider and a remote SoAI MCP server. **External agents hosted in [Zed](https://zed.dev/) through ACP keep their own model configuration unless that agent documents otherwise.**

#### Prepare SoAI

1. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, and open **[OpenAI](https://openai.com/)**. This tab appears only to an Administrator with **API key management** ( [`OPENAI_API_ADMIN`](#acl-OPENAI_API_ADMIN) ). Select **Create key** and copy the key when it is shown. Open **Models** and copy the exact model ID; this requires **Model read access** ( [`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ) ).
2. For MCP, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then open **MCP > MCP tokens**. The MCP tab appears only to an Administrator with **MCP administration** ( [`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN) ), and creating a token also requires **MCP usage** ( [`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE) ). Changing the MCP runtime, server mode, or exposed capabilities under **MCP configuration** also requires **Configuration changes** ( [`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH) ).

#### Connect Zed Agent to the SoAI model API

1. Run **agent: open settings**, then open **LLM Providers**.
2. Select **Add Provider** and choose an OpenAI-compatible provider.
3. Enter a provider name, `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/v1`, the SoAI API key, an exact model ID, and the model's real context window.
4. Choose Chat Completions unless the selected model advertises Responses support. Configure tool, image, parallel-tool, reasoning, and output-token settings only when supported.
5. Select the model in the Agent Panel and send a short request. [Zed](https://zed.dev/) stores UI-entered keys in the system keychain, not in `settings.json`.

#### Connect Zed Agent to SoAI MCP in Zed Settings

1. Open **Settings > AI > MCP Servers**.
2. Select **Add Server > Add Remote Server**.
3. Name it `soai`, enter `https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp`, and add the `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN` header.
4. Confirm the status indicator is green and says **Server is active**, then enable only the required tools in the Agent profile.

```json
{
  "context_servers": {
    "soai": {
      "url": "https://SOAI_HOST:5090/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Built-in agent tools

### Agent tools overview [page: agent-tools-overview]

SoAI's built-in tools let a model inspect or change resources through typed operations. The model requests a tool by name, SoAI validates its arguments and access conditions, and the result returns to the active turn. The Chat transcript keeps each call, approval decision, and result visible.

Use this overview to choose tools and set their policy. The generated [Built-in tool reference](#built-in-tool-reference) is the canonical inventory of tool names, arguments, result schemas, and annotations.

#### Choose and enable tools

| Family | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [Web and knowledge tools](#web-and-knowledge-tools) | Search providers, page retrieval, indexed Knowledge, and MCP resources. |
| [File and shell tools](#file-and-shell-tools) | Workspace reads and mutations, patches, searches, and persistent shell sessions. |
| [Browser automation tools](#browser-automation-tools) | Browser navigation, interaction, snapshots, tabs, downloads, and profiles. |
| [Media reading tools](#media-reading-tools) | Images, audio, video frames, documents, and OCR. |
| [Image generation tools](#image-generation-tools) | Image creation through the configured image backend. |
| [Memory and history tools](#memory-and-history-tools) | Cross-conversation memory and access to permitted conversation history. |
| [Planning and agent control tools](#planning-and-agent-control-tools) | Plans, todo items, questions, subagents, and automation operations. |
| [Productivity and feed tools](#productivity-and-feed-tools) | Mail, calendars, weather, news, feeds, and HTTP requests. |
| [Utility tools](#utility-tools) | Arithmetic, units, hashing, encoding, and date operations. |
| [Hardware tools](#hardware-tools) | Hardware snapshots and protected GPU control or benchmark operations. |
| [Secrets vault](#secrets-vault) | Credential collection and autofill without placing plaintext in those tools' arguments or results. |

##### Enable tools in a conversation

1. In the SoAI WebUI, open the conversation and select **Chat configuration > Tools**.
2. Turn on **Tools enabled** under MCP settings.
3. Choose tools separately for Chat, Plan, and Execute mode.
4. Choose whether protected calls require approval, then select **Save**.

The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)), the installation-wide tool runtime must be enabled, and the selected model must support tool calling. The saved selection applies on the next turn. SoAI locks these controls while a turn is generating.

##### Use mode-specific selection

The active conversation mode selects one of three saved lists. Chat is intended for ordinary conversation and bounded lookups. Plan allows investigation but blocks a tool whose metadata marks it destructive or does not provide valid destructive metadata. Execute can use the complete set the user selected. **Plan mode does not mean that every allowed tool is read-only; selected tools can still reach external systems.**

**Reset** stages SoAI's canonical selection for the active mode. **Default tools (new chats)** controls the starting lists used by later conversations. Indexed Knowledge can keep its required access tools selected while that conversation has indexed content and retrieval is active. See [Agent mode, tool approvals, and checkpoints](#agent-mode-tool-approvals-and-checkpoints) for the complete mode lifecycle.

Tool selection also changes SoAI's [built-in system prompt](#soai-system-prompt). SoAI removes built-in capability guidance that depends on unavailable or unselected tools. It does not rewrite the custom system prompt saved under **Chat configuration > Parameters**; instructions written there still reach the model even when the named tool is unavailable.

#### Permissions and approvals

With **Require tool approval** enabled, an interactive WebUI turn shows the tool name, call ID when present, and arguments before a protected call runs. Approve or deny the call. Remembered approval normally applies to that tool for the signed-in account; browser-autofill approvals are limited to the destination site. If SoAI cannot establish that scope, it refuses to save an unscoped remembered autofill approval.

A tool prompts when its metadata marks it destructive, explicitly requires approval, or has missing or invalid destructive metadata. Approval dialogs belong to interactive WebUI turns. **API and background runs cannot pause for that dialog.** An Administrator can clear their own remembered decisions through **Settings > Reset > Tool approvals**.

##### Understand selection, permission, and availability

**Selecting a tool only makes it eligible for the model.** Each call still has to pass its runtime feature setting, account permissions, ownership checks, conversation mode, and argument validation. For example, shell calls require **Terminal and shell access** ([`TERMINAL_USE`](#acl-TERMINAL_USE)) in addition to MCP usage.

Administrators receive a catalog that also includes protected conversation-stop, hardware-control, and hardware- benchmark operations. Standard accounts, automations, and MCP server mode use the public catalog. The protected administrator-only tools cannot be exposed through MCP server mode.

##### Control installation-wide availability

An Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, then **Advanced** in the page header. Paste the full configuration path into settings search, change the value, and select **Save**. These controls can disable the whole tool runtime or specific families. The main switches are:

- [`TOOLS.MCP.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.ENABLED) for the complete tool system.
- [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.ENABLED) for browser tools.
- [`TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.ENABLED) for new shell work and shell input.
- [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENABLED) for image generation.
- [`TOOLS.RAG.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.ENABLED) for indexed Knowledge and its tools.

**A disabled family rejects its calls even if the tool remains selected in an existing conversation.** Some settings require a restart; Advanced Settings reports that state after Save.

#### External clients and the trust boundary

SoAI's MCP server publishes a configured subset of the public catalog to clients that authenticate with an MCP token. Its exposure list is deliberately narrower than the integrated-agent catalog. A client still needs the owning account's required ACL actions. See [Use SoAI as an MCP server](#use-soai-as-an-mcp-server) for tokens, transport, and exposure controls.

SoAI can also use tools supplied by external MCP servers. Those connections are configured separately and appear beside built-in tools in the conversation picker. See [Connect MCP servers to SoAI](#connect-mcp-servers-to-soai).

A compatible `/v1/chat/completions` request that carries a SoAI conversation ID can use that conversation's server-side agent configuration. Request-supplied compatible tool definitions are different: SoAI passes them through for the API client to execute. See [HTTP API reference](#http-api-reference) for the boundary.

##### Apply the trust boundary

Start with the smallest tool set that can complete the work. **A read-only label does not grant account access, and a confirmation prompt does not make an unsafe deployment trustworthy.** Shell and file tools act with the SoAI process's host access; browser, mail, calendar, HTTP, and search tools can cross the installation boundary. Review [Security hardening](#security-hardening) and the [Hardening checklist](#hardening-checklist) before enabling high-impact tools for other users or external clients.
