### Web and knowledge tools [page: web-and-knowledge-tools]

Sixteen tools search public sources, fetch pages, query the conversation's indexed Knowledge, read resources published by connected MCP servers, and consult the documentation installed with SoAI. These paths have different setup, cost, and failure modes.

In the SoAI WebUI, use a tool in a chat by selecting **Chat configuration** in the chat header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, choose tools for the required mode, and select **Save**. The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)). The conversation web-search controls and direct search endpoint also require **Web search** ([`WEB_SEARCH`](#acl-WEB_SEARCH)). The selected model must support tool calling, and the relevant provider, indexed collection, or connected MCP server must be available.

#### Installed SoAI documentation

`soai_documentation` searches and reads the documentation bundled with the installed SoAI release. It works offline and needs no search provider, embedding model, or index configuration. Search with a concise English phrase or an exact configuration key or tool name. Results include canonical page IDs and matching excerpts; pass one of those IDs as `page` to read the page, then continue with `next_offset_chars` while the response is truncated.

New conversations include this tool in the standard Chat, Plan, and Execute selections. A conversation with a customized saved tool list keeps that list, so enable `soai_documentation` explicitly in its tool picker when needed. The bundle describes the installed release. Use the settings and status pages for live system state, and consult the [SoAI website](https://soai.to/) when you need information about a newer release.

#### Web search

SoAI gives each search provider its own tool rather than one tool with a provider argument. All six take a `query` and an optional `limit`, which defaults to 5 and stops at 25. The rest of the arguments differ by provider.

| Tool | Needs | Extra arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web_search_brave` | A [Brave Search API](https://brave.com/search/) key | `country`, `search_lang`, `freshness` |
| `web_search_duckduckgo` | [DuckDuckGo](https://duckduckgo.com/) needs no account or key. | `region` |
| `web_search_google` | A [Google Programmable Search](https://www.google.com/) API key and engine ID | `safe` |
| `web_search_searxng` | Your own [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/) instance | `categories`, `engines` |
| `web_search_serper` | A [Serper](https://serper.dev/) API key | `gl`, `hl` |
| `web_search_tavily` | A [Tavily](https://tavily.com/) API key | `search_depth`, `include_domains`, `exclude_domains` |

`web_search_duckduckgo` is the only search tool in the default Chat, Plan, and Execute lists, and the only provider that works on a fresh installation without configuration. **Every other provider needs a credential or, for [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/), a configured instance.** Running your own [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/) keeps queries on infrastructure you control while still aggregating several engines.

##### Adding a provider key

An administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)) selects **Open settings menu** at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **MCP**. Find **Search provider API keys**, select the provider, paste the key, and save. SoAI stores it encrypted rather than writing it into `config.yaml`, and the list shows it masked from then on. A key supplied through the environment shows up in the same list marked as coming from the environment.

Provider defaults are installation-wide configuration. An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects **Open settings menu** at the right of the header, then **Settings**, then **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/) needs its base URL set at [`TOOLS.RAG.SEARXNG.BASE_URL`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.SEARXNG.BASE_URL) before its tool can reach anything, and [Google](https://www.google.com/) needs [`TOOLS.RAG.GOOGLE.SEARCH_ENGINE_ID`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.GOOGLE.SEARCH_ENGINE_ID). The rest are optional: default country and language for [Brave](https://brave.com/search/), search depth for [Tavily](https://tavily.com/), geolocation and language for [Serper](https://serper.dev/), safe-search level for [Google](https://www.google.com/), categories and engine list for [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/). SoAI applies [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.SEARCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.SEARCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS) and [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.SEARCH_RETRY_DELAY`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.SEARCH_RETRY_DELAY) across all providers. Select **Save** after editing.

#### Fetching a page

`web_fetch` downloads one URL and pulls the readable content out of it. `extract_mode` selects `markdown`, `text`, or `html`. It also grabs a screenshot through the browser runtime so the model can see the layout, which you can switch off for a single call with `screenshot: false`. When browser tools are disabled installation-wide, SoAI skips the screenshot and fetches the text anyway (rather than failing the request). **The extraction step runs no JavaScript, so use [Browser automation tools](#browser-automation-tools) for client-rendered pages, login screens, or bot challenges.**

SoAI caps the response. `max_chars` defaults to [`TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS), 50,000. If a call requests more than [`TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.MAX_CHARS_LIMIT`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.MAX_CHARS_LIMIT), SoAI accepts the call but applies the 100,000-character limit. Content past the effective cap carries a truncation marker.

#### The conversation Knowledge base

Every conversation can hold its own document collection. On the **Chat** page, open the **Add attachments** dialog from the composer and choose its **Knowledge** tab. Use **Upload file**, **Upload folder**, or **Load from Workspace** to add source material. The same tab shows processing status. **Reindex** appears after documents exist and becomes available when an embedding model is configured. See [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context) for the WebUI flow and the difference between direct files, workspace references, and Knowledge.

Retrieval controls live elsewhere. Open **Chat configuration**, choose the **Knowledge** tab, and use the **Knowledge settings** section to select the embedding model, chunking method, and retrieval strategy. [Knowledge and document collections (RAG)](#knowledge-and-document-collections-rag) covers the pipeline in full. The five tools below are the part an agent can drive.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `knowledge_config_get` | Reads back the retrieval strategy, chunking settings, embedding model, and reranking config. |
| `knowledge_list` | Lists the indexed documents with their processing status. Paginated. |
| `knowledge_reindex` | Re-embeds the whole collection with a different model. Destructive, needs `confirm: true`, and runs as a background job instead of blocking the turn. |
| `knowledge_search` | Searches everything indexed for the conversation, local files and ingested web pages alike. Takes `retrieval_strategy` (*similarity*, *mmr*, or *hybrid*), `top_k`, and `similarity_threshold`. |
| `knowledge_web_fetch` | Fetches a URL, indexes it, and returns immediate context from the new document. Accepts chunking, embedding, and retrieval arguments. |

**`web_fetch` returns extracted content without adding it to Knowledge.** `knowledge_web_fetch` also accepts chunking and embedding settings, then indexes the page so a later `knowledge_search` can find it. Use the second when the page is reference material the conversation will return to, and the first for a one-off lookup.

When a conversation has indexed Knowledge attached, SoAI keeps the knowledge tools enabled and marks them as managed in the tool picker. The tools stay enabled while that content remains active.

#### Resources from connected MCP servers

When you connect SoAI to external MCP servers, those servers can publish resources as well as tools. An administrator with **MCP administration** ([`MCP_ADMIN`](#acl-MCP_ADMIN)) selects **Open settings menu** at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **MCP**. Add servers under **MCP servers**; what they expose then appears in the **Resources** and **Tools** panels on the same tab.

Three tools read those resources. `mcp_resources_list` enumerates them, `mcp_resource_templates_list` enumerates URI templates, and `mcp_resource_read` fetches one by server ID and URI. Leave the `server` argument off either list tool and it queries every connected server at once. [MCP overview](#mcp-overview) covers registering servers and their transports.

#### Network behaviour

Search and fetching share one HTTP layer. Its installation-wide switch is [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.ENABLED). The related controls cover user agent and rotation, an optional proxy or proxy pool, a URL cache with a TTL, per-request and total timeouts, and a download ceiling of [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.MAX_URL_SIZE_MB`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.MAX_URL_SIZE_MB), 10 by default.

[`TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS) defaults to `true`, so `web_fetch` blocks destinations on private networks. [`TOOLS.MCP.HTTP_REQUEST.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HTTP_REQUEST.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS) does the same for `http_request`. Turn off a tool's setting only when that tool must reach a trusted LAN service; doing so permits private-network egress for that tool. [Security hardening](#security-hardening) explains why these per-tool controls do not replace the deployment's private network boundary.

With offline mode on, SoAI refuses search outright and restricts fetching to URLs that resolve to the local machine. The tool returns an error naming the flag rather than hanging until it times out.

When web extraction falls back to browser-backed rendering, [`TOOLS.RAG.WEB.BROWSER_RENDER_BLOCK_ADS`](#config-TOOLS.RAG.WEB.BROWSER_RENDER_BLOCK_ADS) applies the shared [EasyList](https://easylist.to/) request filter and defaults to `true`. **This reduces malicious-ad exposure but does not make fetched content or its instructions trustworthy.** See [Browser ad blocking](#browser-ad-blocking) for the boundary.

### File and shell tools [page: file-and-shell-tools]

Eleven tools let an agent work with files and run commands: seven read and edit files inside a folder you choose, while four drive a real interactive shell on the host. The risk differs sharply between those groups, so SoAI applies separate controls to each one.

In the SoAI WebUI, let an agent use these tools by selecting **Chat configuration** in the chat header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, choose tools for **Chat mode**, **Plan mode**, or **Execute mode**, and select **Save**. The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)) and the selected model must support tool calling. Shell calls also require **Terminal and shell access** ([`TERMINAL_USE`](#acl-TERMINAL_USE)).

#### Choosing the folder an agent works in

File tools operate inside one folder, the same one the Files page shows for your account. To point a single conversation somewhere else, open **Chat configuration**, go to the **Files** tab, and use the **Folder** section: **Change folder** picks a new one, **Inherit default** puts it back. SoAI rejects paths that leave that folder and resolves relative paths inside it.

An administrator with **User administration** ([`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **Users**, to set an account's default folder. In the **Users** section, find the account and select **Folder**. Pointing several accounts at the same folder gives them a shared workspace.

**This boundary covers the file tools only.** The shell tools run commands as the SoAI process (outside that folder boundary) and can reach anywhere on the host that the process can.

#### Reading

`read_file` reads UTF-8 text: source, config, logs. It has three modes.

- *slice*, the default, returns a run of lines chosen with `offset` and `limit`. `limit` defaults to 2000 lines.
- `indentation` centres the view on an anchor line and follows the indentation structure around it, which gets a whole function without the model guessing line numbers.
- `raw` reads the entire file and rejects the slicing arguments outright.

In the first two modes, `render` chooses between unnumbered output, which is what a patch needs, and numbered output for display. For images, audio, video, and PDFs, reach for the [Media reading tools](#media-reading-tools) instead.

`list_dir` walks a directory to a given `depth`. `glob_files` matches paths by pattern and sorts by name or modification time. `grep_files` searches file contents through a managed ripgrep build, with `include` filters, context lines before and after, case folding, multiline matching, and a choice of output modes for content, matching file names, or counts.

#### Writing

| Tool | Use it for | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apply_patch` | Several edits across several files in one call | Snapshots support rollback if an operation fails |
| `replace_in_file` | Swapping an exact string | `expected_replacements` makes the call fail if the count differs; `replace_all` and `allow_noop` cover the other cases |
| `write_file` | Creating a file, or replacing one whole | `overwrite` must be set before it clobbers an existing file |

`write_file` and `replace_in_file` both take `dry_run`, which reports what would change and writes nothing. Every edit that does land shows up in the transcript as an expandable **Code diff**, so you can read what the agent changed without leaving the chat.

The catalog marks all three destructive, so Plan mode refuses them. When **Require tool approval** is on, the approval dialog appears before each call.

##### Read before write

**SoAI requires an agent to read a file before editing it.** The guard catches the failure mode where a model rewrites a file from memory and silently drops everything it did not remember. It is on by default. To turn it off, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**. Select **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. Search for [`TOOLS.MCP.FILE_GUARD_READ_BEFORE_WRITE.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.FILE_GUARD_READ_BEFORE_WRITE.ENABLED), set it to `false`, and select **Save**.

#### The shell

**Shell commands run on the SoAI host as the operating-system account that runs SoAI.** They do not run on the MCP client. Shell tools are excluded from the default server-mode exposure list; adding them to [`TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.EXPOSED_TOOLS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SERVER_MODE.EXPOSED_TOOLS) is an explicit high-impact opt-in. On a network-exposed deployment, that opt-in appears in the WebUI security audit. An MCP call does not receive the WebUI terminal approval dialog.

Expose shell and server-side file tools only within the local trust boundary described in [Security hardening](#security-hardening). A green audit does not make remote MCP exposure safe, and a same-host connection remains unsafe when prompts, models, repository content, or other inputs are untrusted.

`shell` runs a command in a real pseudo-terminal and returns a session ID along with the output. The session stays alive, so a later call can write to the same prompt instead of starting over. The persistent session lets an agent run interactive programs: it can start [Python](https://www.python.org/), answer a password prompt, or drive an installer that expects a keystroke.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `shell` | Runs `cmd`, optionally in a `workdir`, under a login shell, with a `tty` of a given size. `run_in_background` returns immediately and leaves it running. |
| `shell_output_read` | Pages through a session's transcript, from the start or `from_end`. |
| `shell_output_search` | Searches a session's transcript for a string. |
| `shell_write_stdin` | Sends `chars` or named `keys` to a live session, and can resize its terminal. |

Long-running commands do not have to block the turn. With `run_in_background`, the agent starts a build or a test suite, does something else, then comes back with `shell_output_read`. `max_output_tokens` caps each response, and the two reader tools page through the rest.

While a command runs you can stop it yourself. The tool call in the transcript carries a **Stop command** control.

#### Shell controls

[`TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.COMMAND_BLACKLIST`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.COMMAND_BLACKLIST) exists and is empty by default. Filling it in blocks the commands you name. **Treat it as a guard against a model doing something careless, not as a security boundary.** It matches command text, and anything the SoAI process can do on the host, a shell call can still do by some other spelling.

##### Installation switch

[`TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SHELL.ENABLED) is `true` by default. An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**. Select **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. Search for the key, set it to `false`, and select **Save**. All four shell tools then refuse to run and name the key in the error.

##### Account permission

Every shell tool checks the caller's **Terminal and shell access** ([`TERMINAL_USE`](#acl-TERMINAL_USE)) permission at call time. An administrator with **ACL administration** ([`ACL_ADMIN`](#acl-ACL_ADMIN)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **ACL**, to grant it. Administrators hold it by default. It is absent from the Standard user's default actions, although **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)) is present. **Terminal** appears in the default sidebar for administrators and for Standard users granted this permission, unless that user has hidden the item in their sidebar settings. The direct route is `/#terminal`. A permitted user can also use shell tools through an agent.

For the interactive terminal a person drives directly, see [Terminal](#terminal). The [Hardening checklist](#hardening-checklist) covers locking this down.

### Browser automation tools [page: browser-automation-tools]

SoAI drives a real [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) browser through [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/). Twenty-four tools cover navigating, clicking, typing, reading the page, and debugging what went wrong. Two more fill in credentials without returning the plaintext in their own arguments or results, and those live on the [Secrets vault](#secrets-vault) page.

Reach for these when `web_fetch` comes back thin: a page that renders client-side, a login wall, a form to submit, or anything that needs a second click before the content appears.

In the SoAI WebUI, make these tools available by selecting **Chat configuration** in the chat header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, choose the required tools under **Chat mode**, **Plan mode**, or **Execute mode**, and select **Save**. The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)), the selected model must support tool calling, and both [`TOOLS.MCP.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.ENABLED) and [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.ENABLED) must be on. **[Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) must also be installed or available for automatic installation while SoAI is online.**

#### Page representation

In the standard reference-based workflow, `browser_snapshot` returns an accessibility tree rather than raw HTML: the elements a screen reader would announce, each with a role, a name, and a short reference string. The structured action tools use those references instead of CSS selectors, which survives class name churn and minified markup. `browser_eval` is the exception. When enabled, it runs JavaScript in the page and can query or change the DOM directly.

**References go stale as soon as the page changes.** After a click that navigates or re-renders, the old references point at elements that no longer exist. Most action tools accept `include_snapshot` so the agent gets a fresh tree back in the same call rather than spending a round trip on it. SoAI caps snapshots at [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SNAPSHOT_MAX_CHARS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SNAPSHOT_MAX_CHARS), 20,000 characters by default, and `start_char` pages through a longer one.

#### The tools

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Going somewhere | `browser_navigate` handles a URL or moves back and forward through the active tab's history. It can also carry HTTP basic auth credentials when a site demands them |
| Acting on the page | `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_press_key`, `browser_hover`, `browser_select_option`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_drag`, `browser_upload_file` |
| Reading the page | `browser_snapshot`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_pdf`, `browser_eval` |
| Waiting | `browser_wait_for` blocks on elapsed time, text appearing or disappearing, or a URL matching |
| Session and tabs | `browser_tabs`, `browser_resize`, `browser_close` |
| Debugging | `browser_console`, `browser_network`, `browser_dialog`, `browser_downloads`, `browser_status` |
| Profiles | `browser_profiles`, `browser_persistence_reset` |

`browser_eval` runs JavaScript in the page and covers tasks the structured tools cannot express. SoAI caps scripts at 10,000 characters and 15 seconds. You can switch it off on its own with [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.JS_EVAL_ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.JS_EVAL_ENABLED) while leaving the rest of the browser working.

**JavaScript evaluation can read values from the page DOM, including a password that an autofill tool has placed in a field.** Disable it and leave `browser_eval` out of the selected tools when using protected credentials. See [Passwords and credential tools](#passwords-and-credential-tools) for the full boundary.

The tool catalog classifies `browser_persistence_reset` as destructive because it wipes a profile's saved cookies and storage. It needs `confirm: true`, and Plan mode refuses it. Ordinary clicks, typing, uploads, and JavaScript evaluation are not classified as destructive even when the target site gives them lasting effects.

#### Browser failures

Three tools provide the evidence a stuck agent needs. `browser_console` replays console messages with a severity filter, which catches the JavaScript error behind a button that does nothing. `browser_network` lists requests with status filters and can include response bodies up to 64 KiB, which catches the API call returning 403. `browser_dialog` handles a native alert, confirm, or prompt that has blocked the page: without it, a modal dialog leaves the agent waiting on a page that will never respond.

Both log buffers keep [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.LOG_MAX_ENTRIES`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.LOG_MAX_ENTRIES) entries, 500 by default, and both accept a `since` marker so an agent reads only what happened after its last action.

#### Sessions and profiles

A browser session is a running [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) instance with its own cookies and tabs. [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SESSION_SCOPE`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SESSION_SCOPE) decides how widely one is shared, and defaults to `conversation`, so each chat gets its own browser and two conversations cannot see each other's logins.

Profiles hold the persistent state. The default profile stores cookies and local storage as a [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) storage state file, saved automatically after changes and reused next time. Named profiles defined in [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.PROFILES`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.PROFILES) can go further and use a full [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) user data directory, which keeps extensions and everything else a real browser profile holds. A profile can also point at an existing browser through a CDP endpoint, which attaches to a Chrome you started yourself instead of launching a new one.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.AUTO_INSTALL`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.AUTO_INSTALL) | `true` | Download the [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) runtime on first use |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_ADS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_ADS) | `true` | Filter known advertising requests using [EasyList](https://easylist.to/) |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_FONTS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_FONTS) | `true` | Skip web fonts |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_IMAGES`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_IMAGES) | `false` | Images load, since screenshots need them |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_MEDIA`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.BLOCK_MEDIA) | `true` | Skip audio and video |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.DEFAULT_ACTION_TIMEOUT_SEC`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.DEFAULT_ACTION_TIMEOUT_SEC) | `15` | How long a click or type may take |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.DEFAULT_NAV_TIMEOUT_SEC`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.DEFAULT_NAV_TIMEOUT_SEC) | `30` | How long a navigation may take |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.ENABLED) | `true` | Off means every browser tool refuses to run |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.HEADLESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.HEADLESS) | `true` | Run without a visible window |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.MAX_CONCURRENT_PAGES`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.MAX_CONCURRENT_PAGES) | `10` | Ceiling on open pages |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SESSION_SCOPE`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SESSION_SCOPE) | `conversation` | How widely one browser session is shared |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SNAPSHOT_MAX_CHARS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.SNAPSHOT_MAX_CHARS) | `20000` | Cap on one accessibility snapshot |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.STORAGE_STATE_ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.BROWSER.STORAGE_STATE_ENABLED) | `true` | Keep cookies between sessions |

**Ad blocking is a security feature as well as a performance setting.** SoAI evaluates [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) requests against a packaged or refreshed [EasyList](https://easylist.to/) matcher and keeps the existing matcher if a refresh fails. This reduces contact with known advertising infrastructure and malicious ads, but it does not block every tracker or hostile script and does not replace the private-network navigation policy. See [Browser ad blocking](#browser-ad-blocking) for its security role and limits.

An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) can edit these keys: select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, then select **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. Search for a key, edit it, and select **Save**. Blocking fonts and media by default keeps pages loading quickly; images stay on because a screenshot without them is not much use.

The [Chromium](https://www.chromium.org/) runtime downloads on first use, which can take a while on a slow connection. With offline mode on SoAI will not install it, though a runtime that is already installed keeps working.

#### Where the browser may go

Browser navigation follows its own rule, separate from the private-network switches the other tool families use. **While SoAI is online, the browser navigation policy blocks private and loopback addresses, and no setting relaxes that policy.** An agent cannot point the browser at your router or SoAI's own admin interface.

Changing [`TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.WEB_FETCH.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS) or [`TOOLS.MCP.HTTP_REQUEST.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HTTP_REQUEST.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS) affects only that named HTTP tool. Neither setting changes browser navigation policy.

Offline mode inverts the rule: SoAI allows only URLs that resolve to the local machine.

#### Browser authority

A browser session carries real cookies. If you sign a profile in to webmail or an admin panel, an agent with browser tools can act as that account (within the site's own permissions). **The tool layer does not distinguish reading a page from clicking Delete.**

Give browser tools their own profile rather than one holding your day-to-day logins. The **Require tool approval** toggle prompts for credential autofill and persistence reset, but ordinary navigation, typing, uploads, JavaScript evaluation, and clicks pass without a prompt because their catalog metadata is nondestructive. Use `browser_persistence_reset` when a profile has picked up state you did not intend it to keep.

### Media reading tools [page: media-reading-tools]

Four tools let an agent open something that is not text: a photo, a scanned invoice, a recording, a video. Each one turns its input into something a model can reason about, and which tool you want depends on what you need out of the file rather than on its extension.

In the SoAI WebUI, enable a media tool by selecting **Chat configuration** in the chat header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, choose the tool in the required mode, and select **Save**. The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)) and the selected model must support tool calling. `read_image` also needs a vision-capable model; `read_audio` and audio extraction from `read_video` need an installed [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) backend and model.

#### Picking the right one

| Tool | Use it when | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read_audio` | You want a recording transcribed | The bundled [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) plugin |
| `read_document` | You want the text out of a PDF, an office file, or a scan | Nothing for text PDFs; OCR components for scans |
| `read_image` | The model should look at a picture and describe or judge it | A model with vision |
| `read_video` | You want frames, and usually the spoken audio with them | ffmpeg, plus [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) for the audio track |

**The distinction between the first two catches people out.** A photograph of a whiteboard goes to `read_image` if you want the model to interpret the diagram, and to `read_document` if you want the words typed out. The tool descriptions say the same thing: use `read_document` only when you need OCR or text extraction.

#### Images

`read_image` takes a `file_path` inside the conversation's folder and passes the image to the model as an image, not as a description of one. Three limits apply at different stages.

- SoAI rejects a file bigger than [`TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.MAX_SOURCE_BYTES), 128 MiB by default. The agent gets an error rather than a truncated picture.
- SoAI scales down an image with more pixels than [`TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.MAX_PIXELS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.MAX_PIXELS), 4 million by default, before encoding. A 6000 by 4000 photo is 24 million pixels, so it arrives shrunk. This works for describing a scene but can lose small print in a corner.
- The JPEG starts at [`TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.JPEG_QUALITY`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.JPEG_QUALITY), 85 by default. If its Base64 payload exceeds [`TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.MAX_ENCODED_CHARS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE.MAX_ENCODED_CHARS), 16,777,216 characters by default, SoAI lowers JPEG quality as far as 60 and then shrinks the dimensions. It rejects the image if 16 preparation attempts still cannot fit the payload under the limit.

When the detail matters, crop before you hand it over, or use `read_document` so OCR runs at full resolution.

To change these limits, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**. Select **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. Search for [`TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.READ_IMAGE), edit the required key, and select **Save**.

#### Documents

`read_document` extracts text and accepts exactly one of four sources: a `file_path` in the conversation folder, a `file_id` from SoAI storage, a `document_id` from the conversation's Knowledge, or a `url`. Passing more than one is an error, which keeps the agent from silently reading the wrong thing.

**Long documents come back in chunks.** Set `max_chars` and `offset_chars`, and when the response reports that it was truncated, continue from the offset it hands back. That keeps a 400-page PDF from filling the context window in one call.

For PDFs with no text layer, scans, and photographs of text, the pipeline falls back to OCR. SoAI provisions its managed Tesseract runtime during startup; if that cannot complete, raster-only document OCR reports as unavailable. This is also the path that reads text out of video frames.

#### Audio

`read_audio` transcribes with [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) and returns more than the words: timing, container and source metadata, speech pacing, silence gaps, and Whisper's own confidence figures. Set `language` when you know it, since forcing the right language beats letting [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) guess on a short or noisy clip. The `task` argument switches between transcribing in the original language and translating to English.

`include_word_timestamps` adds per-word timing, which is what you want for subtitles or for quoting an exact moment. It makes the response considerably longer, so leave it off otherwise.

[Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) comes from a bundled plugin. On the **Plugins** page, locate [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) and click **Install backend**, choose a compatible build, then click **Start installation**. On the **Models** page, click **Add model**, stay on the **Download model** tab, and choose the [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) plugin and model. Larger models transcribe accented or noisy speech better and cost more time per minute of audio.

#### Video

`read_video` pulls frames out of a local video and, by default, transcribes the audio alongside them. Narrow the work with `start_seconds` and `end_seconds` rather than feeding in an hour-long file: frame extraction is the slow part.

**Sampling runs at one frame per second, which is both the default and the ceiling.** The initial call records a job and blocks until the selected range finishes or is cancelled. Its result includes a `job_id` and the first page of up to 60 frames. The agent passes the returned `cursor` to read later pages, or uses `cancel` with a job ID or cursor to request cancellation. Two jobs may run at once, and completed results are kept for a week.

SoAI caps frames at 2 million pixels and encodes them as JPEG at quality 85. It transcribes audio in five-minute chunks using the `base` [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) model unless you change [`TOOLS.MCP.READ_VIDEO.WHISPER_MODEL`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.READ_VIDEO.WHISPER_MODEL). An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) can change these controls in Advanced settings. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, select **Advanced** in the Settings page header, search for the key, and select **Save** after editing.

In the chat transcript, a completed video read shows its extracted **Frames** and transcript inline, so you can check the material sent to the model.

### Image generation tools [page: image-generation-tools]

One tool, `generate_image`, turns a text prompt into a picture. SoAI does not generate images itself. It hands the work to one of three backends and returns the result to the conversation, so the setup effort goes into the backend rather than into SoAI.

In the SoAI WebUI, open a chat and select **Chat configuration** in its header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, select `generate_image` in **Execute mode**, and select **Save**. The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)), the selected model must support tool calling, and the selected image engine must be configured and reachable. **Plan mode refuses this destructive tool.**

#### Calling it

**Only `prompt` is required, and the tool contract requires English (even when the user writes in another language).** Its description tells the model to translate or rewrite other languages before calling because non-English prompts can produce poor output. A user can ask in any language; the prompt sent to the backend should be English.

| Argument | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | 1 to 2000 characters | Required |
| `negative_prompt` | Up to 2000 characters | [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.NEGATIVE_PROMPT`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.NEGATIVE_PROMPT), empty |
| `width`, `height` | 64 to 2048, in steps of 8 | 704 by 704 |
| `steps` | 1 to 150 | 20 |
| `cfg_scale` | 1.0 to 30.0 | 7.0 |
| `seed` | 0 to 2,147,483,647 | Random |

A fixed `seed` asks the selected engine for deterministic generation. Reproducibility still depends on the same backend, model, workflow, and engine version. The catalog requires approval for this tool, so with when **Require tool approval** is on, you see the prompt before anything is generated.

#### The three backends

| Engine | Runs where | Trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [AI Horde](https://aihorde.net/) | Somebody else's GPU, via a volunteer network | No local GPU needed. You queue behind other people and wait. |
| [Automatic1111](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui) | Your machine, on your GPU | The default. Widely documented, and the simplest to point SoAI at. |
| [ComfyUI](https://www.comfy.org/) | Your machine, on your GPU | Node graphs give far more control, and need a workflow exported first. |

An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) chooses one through [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENGINE`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENGINE): select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, then select **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. Search for the key, choose an engine, and select **Save**. Each engine reads its own block of settings, so switching back and forth does not mean re-entering them.

##### Automatic1111

Start [Automatic1111](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui) with its API enabled, then set [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AUTOMATIC1111.BASE_URL`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AUTOMATIC1111.BASE_URL). The default already points at `http://127.0.0.1:7860`, so a local install on the standard port needs nothing changed. The remaining controls in that block cover basic authentication, sampler and scheduler selection, and extra API parameters.

##### ComfyUI

[ComfyUI](https://www.comfy.org/) needs more than a URL because the graph is the configuration. Build your workflow in [ComfyUI](https://www.comfy.org/), export it in API format, and paste it into [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.COMFYUI.WORKFLOW_JSON`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.COMFYUI.WORKFLOW_JSON). In [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.COMFYUI.WORKFLOW_NODES`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.COMFYUI.WORKFLOW_NODES), add mapping objects that name a node, its input field, and the request value to insert. Supported values include the prompt, negative prompt, dimensions, steps, guidance scale, seed, model, and a literal. Use [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.COMFYUI.OUTPUT_NODE_IDS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.COMFYUI.OUTPUT_NODE_IDS) to prefer particular output nodes. When that list is empty, SoAI scans every output for the first image.

##### AI Horde

[AI Horde](https://aihorde.net/) runs on donated GPUs. Leave [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AI_HORDE.API_KEY`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AI_HORDE.API_KEY) empty and SoAI uses the shared anonymous key. SoAI limits anonymous requests to nine per minute. A registered key avoids that local anonymous limit, but the provider still schedules work through its queue. Set [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AI_HORDE.MODEL`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AI_HORDE.MODEL) to a model the network currently offers, and expect long waits when it is busy. [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AI_HORDE.MAX_GENERATION_WAIT_SEC`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.AI_HORDE.MAX_GENERATION_WAIT_SEC) gives up after an hour by default.

**This is the one engine that sends your prompts to a third party.** Every prompt goes to a volunteer's machine, so keep private or identifying detail out of them.

#### Shared settings

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS) | `true` | Blocks private addresses, with an exception for local endpoints |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENABLED`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENABLED) | `true` | Off means the tool refuses to run and names the key |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENGINE`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.ENGINE) | [Automatic1111](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui) | Which backend to use |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.MAX_IMAGE_BYTES) | 128 MiB | Largest image SoAI will accept back |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.POLL_INTERVAL_SEC`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.POLL_INTERVAL_SEC) | `1.0` | How often SoAI checks a queued job |
| [`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.TIMEOUT_SEC`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.TIMEOUT_SEC) | `3600` | Ceiling on one generation |

#### Local endpoint policy

[`TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.GENERATE_IMAGE.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS) defaults to `true`, and both local engines default to a `127.0.0.1` address. The endpoint policy treats loopback differently from other private addresses.

SoAI treats an endpoint that resolves to the local machine as local and allows it over plain `http://`. **It requires `https://` for any other host.** While the private-network block is on, SoAI also rejects hosts in private address ranges. A local [Automatic1111](https://github.com/AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui) or [ComfyUI](https://www.comfy.org/) works out of the box, as does a remote service over HTTPS. Another machine on your LAN requires you to turn the block off.

### Memory and history tools [page: memory-and-history-tools]

Five tools give an agent something a single conversation cannot: knowledge that survives when the chat ends. Four maintain a memory graph that persists across conversations. The fifth reads your past chats.

In the SoAI WebUI, let an agent use these tools by selecting **Chat configuration** in the chat header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, choose the tools for the required mode, and select **Save**. The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)) and the selected model must support tool calling. The **Memory** tab remains available for reviewing stored memory even when these tools are not selected.

You can see the result without asking an agent about it. Open **Chat configuration** and switch to the **Memory** tab. **User memories** lists what SoAI has stored for your account with its observations and relations, and **Refresh memory** reloads it after a turn has written something new. **The tab is read-only, so removing an entry means asking an agent to forget it.**

**Open profile form** on the same tab is the shortcut for seeding memory yourself. It asks for your preferred name, how you want SoAI to communicate, your role, current goals, recurring projects, and anything to avoid. Filling it in beats repeating the same preamble in every conversation, and it works whether or not an agent has the memory tools enabled.

#### Write and maintain the memory graph

SoAI stores memory as three kinds of record rather than as free-form notes.

- *Entities* are the things worth remembering: a person, a project, a piece of software, a preference. Each has a name and a type.
- **Observations** are facts attached to an entity. *Prefers tabs over spaces* hangs off a person; *deploys on Thursdays* hangs off a project.
- **Relations** connect two entities, so an agent can follow from a person to the project they own.

This structure supports targeted searches. An agent can query an entity by name and follow its relations without reading every stored observation.

**Memory belongs to the account.** Your entities are yours, another user's are theirs, and no conversation reads across that line.

##### The four memory tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `memory_forget` | Deletes entities, observations, or relations. Destructive, and deleting an entity takes its observations and relations with it. |
| `memory_recall` | Fetches one entity by its exact name, with all its observations and relations. |
| `memory_search` | Searches names and observation text by keyword or wildcard, ranking exact name matches first. `*` returns everything. Filter with `entity_type`. |
| `memory_store` | Writes entities, observations, and relations in one call. Flagged for approval, so with when **Require tool approval** is on, you see what the agent wants to remember before it does. |

`memory_search` and `memory_recall` answer different questions. Recall is for when the agent already knows the name and wants the record. Search is for when it does not, which is most of the time. An agent that searches `*` at the start of every conversation is doing it wrong and will fill its context with things nobody asked about.

`memory_store` asks for approval because a stored record remains available to later conversations. A wrong fact can shape a later answer when an agent searches or recalls it. The approval dialog lets you catch the mistake before it enters the graph.

##### Keeping it useful

Edit memory as it grows. An agent that stores everything can create contradictions, such as an old preference or several spellings of the same project. Ask the agent to review the graph and use `memory_forget` for records that no longer apply.

**There is no wipe-everything button.** Read the **Memory** tab to see what is there, then ask an agent with `memory_forget` to drop what you no longer want.

#### Read conversation history and choose storage

`memory_conversation_history` reaches your earlier chats. It takes one `action`:

| Action | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `list` | Conversations newest first, paged with `last_modified_before` |
| `search` | Matches across conversations for a `query`, with separate caps on matches, conversations, matches per conversation, and characters per match |
| `read` | Messages from one `conv_id`, paged backwards from a timestamp or message ID |

It returns your messages and the model's, leaving tool calls out, so a search does not drown in shell output. The caps exist because the alternative is one call that pulls a year of chat history into the context window.

SoAI stores automation runs as conversations. A normal chat excludes them by default. An automation conversation includes them by default so a scheduled job can inspect its previous runs. Set `include_automation` to override either behavior.

If automation runs clutter your sidebar, **Hide automation runs** on the **Appearance** tab of **Chat configuration** hides them from the list. **That is a display setting and does not change what this tool sees.**

##### Choosing the right storage

Memory, Knowledge, and plans serve different scopes.

- **Memory** holds small facts that apply across conversations. Use it for preferences, people, and long-running context.
- **Knowledge** holds documents, chunked and embedded for retrieval. Use it for reference material. See [Knowledge and document collections (RAG)](#knowledge-and-document-collections-rag).
- *Plans* hold the current task's reasoning inside one conversation and do not outlive it. See [Planning and agent control tools](#planning-and-agent-control-tools).

Putting a 40-page specification into memory as observations works badly. Putting *the user wants replies in French* into a document collection works badly too.

### Planning and agent control tools [page: planning-and-agent-control-tools]

Fifteen tools manage the agent's work. They track what it needs to do, hand parts to subagents, ask you for input, and schedule later runs.

#### Todo lists and plans

A conversation holds one todo checklist and one plan document. They serve different scales of work, and both show up in the chat as you go.

`todo_write` writes the checklist, which appears above the composer as **Todo** and expands to show the items. **Every call replaces the whole list.** There is no add-one or mark-done operation, so the model has to restate every item and its status each time, which stops it leaving a finished step marked in progress. Only one item may be in progress at a time.

`plan_write` stores a Markdown document of up to 50,000 characters with an optional title. `plan_get` reads it back. Writing an empty string clears it. The plan appears in the chat as a **Plan** widget showing its revision number and size, and **View plan** opens the whole thing.

The split is about lifespan. The todo list is the steps in front of the agent right now. The plan is the reasoning you do not want it to rebuild after the conversation is compacted.

Plan mode can produce this document while SoAI blocks tools marked destructive in the catalog. Other selected Plan tools can still have external effects. When the plan looks right, **Execute plan** on the widget switches the conversation to Execute mode and tells the agent to implement it. The plan tools themselves are nondestructive and remain available in Plan mode.

#### Subagents

`subagent_spawn` starts a background agent for the current turn and returns an ID. Give it a `task`, and optionally `context`, a `mode`, a `model` override, a `workspace_path`, a `display_name`, and a `max_iterations` cap. Running subagents show up in the transcript with their own activity stream, so you can watch what each one is doing.

Spawning works from Plan or Execute mode. **A Plan-mode parent may only spawn Plan-mode subagents, so delegation cannot bypass the destructive-tool policy.**

The `tools` argument means three different things depending on how it is passed: leave it out for the default subagent set, pass an empty array for text-only operation with no tools, or pass names to provide only those tools.

SoAI then removes a fixed set regardless of the requested names. A subagent cannot call `subagent_spawn`, `subagent_observe`, or `subagent_cancel`, so subagents cannot nest. It cannot call `ask_user` or `notify_user`, so it cannot interrupt you while its parent is mid-turn. It cannot touch `todo_write`, `plan_write`, or `plan_get`, which belong to the parent. SoAI also blocks every automation tool. In Plan mode the destructive filter applies to subagents exactly as it does to the parent. SoAI refuses the spawn if that filtering leaves no tools in Plan or Execute mode.

`subagent_observe` checks on one. `mode: current` returns a snapshot straight away; `mode: terminal` blocks until the subagent finishes, is cancelled, fails, or is abandoned. `timeout_ms` bounds that wait and defaults to [`TOOLS.MCP.SUBAGENT.OBSERVE_TIMEOUT_MS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.SUBAGENT.OBSERVE_TIMEOUT_MS), which is `0` out of the box; pass `null` to wait with no limit.

`subagent_cancel` asks one to stop. Cancellation is cooperative and asynchronous, so work already in flight may still finish before it takes effect.

#### Talking to you

`ask_user` pauses the turn and puts questions in the chat, then waits for your answer. One to six questions per call, and the schema advises one to three with two to four options each, because a wall of questions is worse than asking twice. The agent can mark confidential free text as secret. **Credentials belong in [the vault tools](#secrets-vault), which keep the value away from the model.** [`TOOLS.MCP.ELICITATION.WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.ELICITATION.WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS) bounds the wait to one hour by default.

`notify_user` goes the other way and does not wait. It posts to the notification centre in the header with a type of `info`, `success`, `warning`, or `error`, a title, a message, an optional source label, and an optional link. Use it to report that a long job finished. Use `ask_user` when the answer changes what the agent does next.

#### Pausing and stopping

`wait` sleeps. Give it `seconds`, up to a week, or an ISO 8601 `until` timestamp with an optional `timezone` when that timestamp carries no offset. A `reason` labels the pause in the transcript, so the agent does not spend turns polling.

`stop_conversation` ends the current model turn cleanly without closing the conversation. Authorized conversation users, including non-administrators, can select it. It cannot be exposed through MCP server mode.

#### Automations

An automation is a scheduled agent run with its own conversation. In the SoAI WebUI, create, enable, inspect, and stop it from **Automation** in the sidebar. [Automations](#automations) covers the WebUI form, recurrence, run history, limits, and approval behavior. The tools below let an agent manage its owner's automations from a conversation.

##### Automation tools in a conversation

Five tools let an agent manage automations directly, each one limited to the calling user's own.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `automation_create` | Creates one, with the same fields the Create automation form collects |
| `automation_run_enqueue` | Runs one now, without waiting for its schedule |
| `automation_run_get` | Fetches one run record by `run_id` |
| `automation_run_wait` | Blocks until a run reaches a terminal state. `timeout_ms` of `0` returns the current state immediately, `null` waits indefinitely, and leaving it out uses a 60-second wait. |
| `automation_update` | Changes an existing one by `automation_id`. Every field except the ID is optional. |

Scheduling takes a `timezone`, a local `start_local` of the form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`, and a `recurrence` of `none`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, or `yearly`. **Cron expressions are not accepted, in either the form or the tool.**

##### Run permissions

**Automation runs always use Execute mode, and they get no tools at all unless the automation's own model settings switch tools on.** An automation created without that is a plain multi-turn prompt.

Administrators have one installation-wide control that an automation cannot override. An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**. Select **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. Search for [`AUTOMATION.DISALLOWED_UNQUALIFIED_TOOLS`](#config-AUTOMATION.DISALLOWED_UNQUALIFIED_TOOLS). It is an empty list by default. A tool named there is unavailable to every automation run, whatever its own configuration says. Select **Save** after editing. Add shell tool names there when scheduled jobs must never reach the shell.

### Productivity and feed tools [page: productivity-and-feed-tools]

Twenty-three tools connect the agent with mail, calendars, weather, news, RSS feeds, and HTTP endpoints. Mail and calendar list and read tools usually use SoAI's local cache. **Sync, search, and mutation calls contact the configured service and can act in your name.**

Mail and calendar need setting up before they do anything. Weather, news, RSS, and `http_request` work as soon as an agent has them enabled.

#### Connecting a mailbox

In the SoAI WebUI, select **Open settings menu** at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **Mail & calendar**. Select **Add account** under **Mail accounts**. Pick **IMAP + SMTP** or **POP3 + SMTP**, give the account a name, and fill in the inbound host and port, usually 993 for IMAP over TLS or 995 for POP3, along with the SMTP host and port for sending.

**Inbound security** and **SMTP security** accept **TLS** or **STARTTLS**, and the form offers no plaintext transport. Inbound mail uses IMAP or POP3, while outbound mail always uses SMTP.

For **Authentication type**, **Password** stores a secret and **OAuth2** walks through an authorization flow instead. Providers that have turned off password logins need the OAuth2 path; fill in the client ID, endpoints, and scopes under **OAuth configuration**, save, then use **Connect OAuth** on the account.

**Test** checks the connection before you rely on it, and **Sync now** pulls mail straight away rather than waiting for the schedule. Each account shows its **Last sync** time and its **Last error**, which is the first place to look when the tools come back empty.

#### Mail tools

SoAI keeps a local cache of your folders and messages and syncs it in the background. Most tools read that cache rather than hitting the server, which is why they answer quickly and why the cache boundary matters.

| Tool | Reads cache | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mail_account_sync` | no | Forces a refresh, the same as **Sync now** |
| `mail_accounts_list` | yes | Your configured accounts |
| `mail_attachment_download` | yes | Saves one attachment into SoAI file storage |
| `mail_folder_backfill` | no | Pulls the next older batch of history into the cache |
| `mail_folder_update` | no | One `action`: `create`, `rename`, `delete`, `subscribe`, or `unsubscribe`. Destructive. |
| `mail_folders_list` | yes | Cached folders for one account |
| `mail_message_compose` | no | Sends or drafts. `mode` of `new`, `reply`, `reply_all`, or `forward`; `delivery` of `send` or `save_draft`. Destructive. |
| `mail_message_read` | yes | One cached message, chunked for long bodies |
| `mail_message_update` | no | One `action`: `mark_read`, `mark_unread`, `flag`, `unflag`, `archive`, `unarchive`, `move`, `copy`, `delete`, or `restore`. Destructive. |
| `mail_messages_list` | yes | Cached messages in a folder, with filters |
| `mail_messages_remote_search` | no | Searches on the server and imports what it finds |

Most mail-list surprises come from the cache boundary. `mail_messages_list` sees only synchronized messages, so an item older than the cache window will not appear no matter how the agent phrases the query. Use `mail_folder_backfill` to pull more history, or `mail_messages_remote_search` to ask the server directly.

Background sync runs every 120 seconds and keeps 30 days of history, excluding `Junk` and `Spam`, with a limit of 5000 messages per folder. Reads cap at 50,000 characters per call, snippets at 500, and attachments at 25,000,000 bytes. To change these defaults, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects **Open settings menu** at the right of the header, then **Settings**. Select **Advanced** in the Settings page header. The page becomes **Advanced settings** and the control changes to **Basic**. Search for [`INTEGRATIONS.MAIL`](#config-INTEGRATIONS.MAIL), edit the required key, and select **Save**.

SoAI requires every remote search to include a narrowing filter. A full-text search also needs a time bound. These requirements prevent an agent from starting an unbounded scan of a large mailbox.

`mail_message_compose` is the one to think hardest about. **It sends real mail to real people from your own address.** Plan mode blocks it, Execute mode does not, and a mistake here is not something you can take back. Turn on **Require tool approval** for any conversation that can compose, and read the arguments in the approval dialog rather than clicking through.

#### Calendar

Calendar works over CalDAV with the same cache-first design. Select **Open settings menu** at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **Mail & calendar**. Under **Calendar accounts**, add an account with the CalDAV base URL and either a password or OAuth2.

Set **Linked mail account** while you are there. When an event names an organizer, `calendar_invite_respond` requires an SMTP-ready linked account before it updates the event. It saves the CalDAV attendee response first, then sends the organizer an email. If that send fails after the save, the tool returns the updated event with a warning.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `calendar_account_sync` | Rediscovers calendars and refreshes the cache |
| `calendar_accounts_list` | Configured calendar accounts |
| `calendar_calendars_list` | Cached calendars in one account |
| `calendar_event_read` | One cached event in full |
| `calendar_event_update` | Creates, changes, or deletes an event. Destructive. |
| `calendar_events_list` | Cached events in a time window |
| `calendar_invite_respond` | Replies `accept`, `tentative`, or `decline`, with an optional comment. Destructive. |
| `calendar_window_sync` | Refreshes one specific time window from the server |

The synced window runs 90 days back and 365 forward, refreshed every 300 seconds. **Ask about a date outside it and the agent needs `calendar_window_sync` first.** Recurring events expand up to 500 occurrences each, which is why a daily meeting with no end date does not produce an endless list. An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) can change these defaults in Advanced settings: select **Open settings menu** at the right of the header, then **Settings**, select **Advanced** in the Settings page header, search for [`INTEGRATIONS.CALENDAR`](#config-INTEGRATIONS.CALENDAR), and select **Save** after editing.

#### Weather

`weather` takes a `location` as a place name and returns current conditions plus a forecast. `forecast_days` runs 1 to 14 and defaults to 3. `hourly_hours` adds hour-by-hour detail up to 48 and defaults to 0. `units` is `metric` or `imperial`, and `country_code` settles a place name that exists in several countries.

It uses [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/) and needs no key, so it works out of the box. Separate controls set the geocoding and forecast URLs: [`TOOLS.MCP.WEATHER.GEOCODING_BASE_URL`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.WEATHER.GEOCODING_BASE_URL) and [`TOOLS.MCP.WEATHER.FORECAST_BASE_URL`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.WEATHER.FORECAST_BASE_URL), so pointing SoAI at your own [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/) instance means changing two settings.

#### News

`news` queries [GDELT](https://www.gdeltproject.org/). Pass *latest* or *today* for current headlines, a `YYYY-MM-DD` date for one day, or any phrase to search for it. `language` defaults to *en* and `country` to `US`. `max_results` defaults to 10 and caps at 25. SoAI raises any lower value to 10.

SoAI prefers GDELT's DOC 2.0 API for full-text country-filtered results and falls back to the Article List feed for global headlines when DOC is unavailable, so a query returns less precise results instead of failing. No key required.

#### RSS

`rss_read` fetches one RSS or Atom feed by `url` and returns structured items. `max_items` defaults to 10 and caps at 100. **There is no subscription list and no polling: an agent reads a feed when asked.** For a feed you want checked regularly, pair it with an automation from the **Automation** page, described under [Planning and agent control tools](#planning-and-agent-control-tools).

#### HTTP requests

`http_request` handles APIs that have no dedicated SoAI tool. It supports GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS with custom headers and a body, then returns status, headers, body, and timing. Text comes back as UTF-8 and binary content as Base64.

SoAI retries safe methods automatically. For a mutating method with `retries` above zero, SoAI requires a nonempty `Idempotency-Key` header. That requirement prevents an agent from submitting the same order twice after a timeout. `session_mode` returns an updated `session` payload containing cookies and headers. Passing that payload into the next call carries the session through a multi-step API flow.

The remaining arguments are limits: `timeout` up to 120 seconds, `max_response_bytes` with a truncation flag, `follow_redirects`, `detect_blocked` for bot and CAPTCHA responses, and the backoff and jitter behind `retries`.

**[`TOOLS.MCP.HTTP_REQUEST.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS`](#config-TOOLS.MCP.HTTP_REQUEST.BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORK_EGRESS) defaults to `true`, the opposite of `web_fetch`.** So an agent with this tool cannot reach your LAN or SoAI's own admin interface until you turn that off. Weigh that before you do: after the change, the tool can send a described request to permitted private addresses, including internal services.

### Utility tools [page: utility-tools]

SoAI provides eight small tools that do one thing each. Seven work entirely from their arguments without using the network or disk, while the eighth, `message_parse`, reads a file. None is destructive, so Plan mode permits any of them when selected. The default Plan list includes only `calculator` and `datetime_current` from this family.

In the SoAI WebUI, use one in a chat by selecting **Chat configuration** in the chat header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, choose the tool for the required mode, and select **Save**. The account needs **MCP usage** ([`MCP_USE`](#acl-MCP_USE)) and the selected model must support tool calling.

These tools improve accuracy. A language model can answer *what is 17.5% of 84,300* without help but can return a plausible wrong result. Handing the arithmetic to code removes that failure mode.

#### Calculations and data transforms

`calculator` evaluates a mathematical `expression`. It does not use Python's `eval`: SoAI parses the expression and walks the syntax tree, allowing only the operators and functions on a fixed list. An expression that tries to reach anything else is rejected rather than executed.

Available are the arithmetic and comparison operators including floor division, modulo, and both `**` and `^` for powers; the constants pi, e, and tau; and the functions `sqrt`, `abs`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `trunc`, the trigonometric and hyperbolic families with their inverses, `log`, `ln`, `log10`, `log2`, `exp`, `hypot`, `min`, `max`, `degrees`, `radians`, plus `pct(p, x)` for percentages and `clamp(x, low, high)`. An optional `variables` object supplies named values, so an agent can write a formula once and substitute numbers into it.

`unit_convert` converts a `value` between units across temperature, length, weight, and data sizes. It works out the category from the units unless you set `category` yourself.

##### Hashing and encoding

`hash` returns MD5, SHA1, SHA256, or SHA512 of a string. `base64` encodes or decodes, with a `variant` for standard Base64, URL-safe Base64, or Base32.

Both take text as an argument, which limits them to short strings that fit in a prompt. To hash a file, use the shell or the Files page instead.

##### Random values

`random_generate` produces one of five things depending on `type`: an `integer` in a range, a `float`, a `uuid`, a random `string` from a charset, or a `choice` from a list you supply. `count` asks for several at once.

Use `random_generate` because models are poor random number generators. Asked for a number between 1 and 100, they overproduce a small set of values. Use the tool for a lottery draw, sample, or shuffle.

With `type: string` and `charset: password`, the tool uses a cryptographic random source, but the generated value is returned to the model as ordinary tool output. **Do not confuse it with the protected vault path.** See [Passwords and credential tools](#passwords-and-credential-tools) before using it for a live credential.

#### Time, text, and chat exports

`datetime_current` covers four operations. `now` returns the current time in a `timezone`, `convert` moves a timestamp between zones, `add_days` does date arithmetic, and `format` renders a timestamp with a custom pattern. It accepts IANA zone names and epoch milliseconds.

**A model response has no reliable clock.** Use `now` for anything relative to the current date or time. `datetime_current` is included in the default Chat mode tool list.

##### Text and chat exports

`text_stats` counts characters, words, tokens, sentences, and estimated reading time for a block of text.

`message_parse` reads an exported chat log and returns structured messages. It handles [WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/), [Telegram](https://telegram.org/), [Discord](https://discord.com/), [Signal](https://signal.org/), [Facebook Messenger](https://www.messenger.com/), and [MSN Messenger](https://www.msn.com/) exports in `.txt`, `.json`, `.xml`, `.csv`, `.html`, and `.zip` form. Point it at a file with `file_path`, a stored file with `file_id`, or an indexed document with `document_id`. It usually detects the `platform` on its own, and `max_messages` caps how much comes back, which matters for a group chat with years of history in it.

Upload the export through the Files page first, or attach it to the conversation, and the agent can read it from there. See [Attachments and file context](#attachments-and-file-context) for the available Chat attachment methods.

### Hardware tools [page: hardware-tools]

Three tools let an agent inspect and tune the physical machine. `hardware_snapshot` reads sensors. `hardware_control` changes GPU settings, while `hardware_benchmark` starts and manages load tests. The last two require an administrator, Execute mode, an active agent turn, selection for that turn, and tool approval when approvals are enabled.

In the SoAI WebUI, open **Hardware** from the sidebar to inspect the machine. The page is available to accounts with **Hardware read access** ([`HARDWARE_READ`](#acl-HARDWARE_READ)). Its GPU controls appear only for accounts with **GPU tuning** ([`HW_GPU_TUNING`](#acl-HW_GPU_TUNING)) and only when the detected GPU supports those controls. For a one-off change, use that page directly. The agent tools are useful when a reading leads to a controlled change and a follow-up benchmark.

These tools and that page are two routes to the same hardware. [Hardware monitoring](#hardware-monitoring) is the manual way to read the machine, and it adds stored history, the **Chart** time ranges, and **Export**, which no tool provides. The [GPU controls and tuning](#gpu-controls-and-tuning) page is the manual way to change a GPU, and it owns the saved slots and **Apply at boot**. Reach for the tools instead when you want a model to run the read, change, and benchmark loop rather than driving each step yourself.

To use the tools in a chat, select **Chat configuration** in the chat header, then **Tools**. Turn on **Tools enabled**, select `hardware_snapshot` for the required mode, and select **Save**. The control and benchmark tools are administrator-only and are available only in **Execute mode**.

#### Reading the machine

`hardware_snapshot` returns live readings. Ask for the components you need through `components`, which accepts `uptime`, `os`, `cpu`, `cpus`, `memory`, `swap`, `gpu`, `motherboard`, `disk`, `disk_speed`, `network`, and `network_speed`. Left unset it returns uptime, OS, CPU, memory, and GPU.

**`disk_speed` and `network_speed` run measurements rather than reading a counter, so they take noticeably longer than the rest.** Ask for them only when you want them.

Any authenticated account can call this tool. `include_processes`, which adds the per-GPU process list, requires an administrator, because that list shows what everyone on the machine is running.

The GPU device IDs in the response are what the other two tools need.

#### Changing GPU settings

`hardware_control` has two actions. `list` reports which controls a card supports, and `set` applies them. Always call `list` first: support varies by vendor, driver, and model, and setting an unsupported control fails rather than silently doing nothing.

| Setting | Unit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core_clock` | MHz | Raising it can hang the driver or corrupt output |
| `fan_speed` | Percent | Manual control means the fan no longer responds to temperature on its own. |
| `mem_clock` | MHz | Memory errors from this are silent and show up as wrong results |
| `power_limit` | Watts | The safest lever. Lower it to cut heat and noise at some cost in performance. |
| `reset_clocks` | Boolean | Puts clocks back to stock. Do not combine it with clock values. |

Each numeric control accepts `auto` where the card supports it, handing control back to the driver. The schema permits several settings in one call, but its description recommends one changed field at a time. That makes a failed stability test easier to diagnose.

The **Hardware** page exposes the same controls under **GPU controls**, labelled **Power limit**, **Fan speed**, **Core clock offset**, and **Memory clock offset**, with an **Automatic control** toggle and **Apply**, **Save**, **Reset**, and **Test** buttons. Saved profiles go into numbered slots, and a slot can be marked **Apply at boot**. The panel carries its own warning that incorrect settings may damage your GPU. **That applies equally when an agent is the one setting them.**

#### Benchmarking

`hardware_benchmark` runs a load and measures it, through four actions: `start` launches a run and returns a `run_id`, `status` polls it, `stop` asks it to cancel, and `history` lists earlier runs for a device.

Two profiles. `soaibench` is the certified SoAIBench workload, which is the one to use for a number you want to compare against anything else. `stress_test` pushes the card hard to see whether it stays stable, which is what you want after changing clocks.

`temperature_limit_celsius` stops the run when the card reaches that temperature and defaults to 100 C for certified SoAIBench. Lower it when you are testing an overclock, so the run aborts before the card gets hot rather than after.

Runs are asynchronous. An agent starts one, polls `status`, and reads the result when it finishes. The **Hardware** page has the same thing as **Bench**, **Stress**, **Stop**, and **History** buttons on the GPU panel.

#### Control and benchmark prerequisites

`hardware_control` and `hardware_benchmark` check four things on every call, and fail with a clear reason when any of them is missing.

- The calling account is an administrator.
- The conversation is in **Execute** mode. Chat and Plan mode cannot reach them at all.
- The call is happening through the MCP tool context inside a live agent turn.
- The tool appears in the selected tool map for that turn.

**Both also belong to the admin catalog, so MCP server mode never exposes them.** Third-party software that uses SoAI as an MCP server does not see them in its tool list at all: it can call `hardware_snapshot`, which is in the public catalog, but it cannot change or stress a GPU. Model-orchestrated GPU control is internal to SoAI. Their catalog metadata also marks them destructive, so Plan mode would refuse them even without the mode check.

#### Doing this safely

**Tuning by trial and error is what these tools are for, but the failure modes are physical.** Work in this order.

- Read a baseline with `hardware_snapshot` so you have something to compare against.
- Call `hardware_control` with `list` and change only what it reports as supported.
- Change one setting per call.
- Run `stress_test` with a `temperature_limit_celsius` you have chosen deliberately, and watch the temperature while it runs.
- Keep `reset_clocks` in mind as the way back.

Leave **Require tool approval** on for any conversation that can reach these tools. Both are flagged for approval, so you see the exact settings before SoAI applies them. [GPU controls and tuning](#gpu-controls-and-tuning) and [Hardware monitoring](#hardware-monitoring) cover the same ground from the WebUI side.
