## Extending

### Plugins overview [page: plugins-overview]

SoAI connects local engines and remote providers through `.soaiplugin` packages. A plugin declares its supported operations, manages any backend it owns, and supplies models to the shared catalog. The WebUI presents those declarations as the actions and capability badges on each plugin and model.

#### Bundled plugins

| Plugin | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [CTranslate2](https://opennmt.net/CTranslate2/) | Offline CPU neural machine translation. |
| External | A connector for OpenAI-compatible APIs. |
| [Llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | A [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) backend. |
| [Llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) Embeddings | A [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) backend dedicated to embeddings. |
| [Melo TTS](https://github.com/myshell-ai/MeloTTS) | A frozen [MeloTTS](https://github.com/myshell-ai/MeloTTS) text-to-speech backend. |
| [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) | An [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) backend and [Ollama Cloud](https://ollama.com/) provider. |
| [vLLM](https://vllm.ai/) | A [vLLM](https://vllm.ai/) backend. |
| [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) | An [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) speech-to-text backend. |

The bundled package metadata is the source for these descriptions. Read [Bundled plugins reference](#bundled-plugins-reference) before choosing a backend, since a plugin's capabilities and the capabilities of an individual model are separate.

#### Add a plugin in the SoAI WebUI

Opening **Plugins** requires **Plugin read access** ([`PLUGIN_READ`](#acl-PLUGIN_READ)). Installing or changing a package requires the Administrator-only **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)) action. **A plugin can execute code under the SoAI service account, so inspect its source and [license](#license-and-legal) before adding it.**

1. Open **Plugins** and select **Add plugin**.
2. Select **Download plugin from URL**, enter the **Plugin URL**, and select **Download plugin**; or select **Upload plugin**, choose a `.soaiplugin` file, and select **Upload plugin**.
3. Keep the dialog open to review progress, or open the **Tasks** panel in the header. Wait for a terminal result before using the new card.

The server rejects uploads when [`PLUGINS.FEATURES.UPLOADS`](#config-PLUGINS.FEATURES.UPLOADS) is disabled and URL downloads when [`PLUGINS.FEATURES.DOWNLOADS`](#config-PLUGINS.FEATURES.DOWNLOADS) is disabled. A URL download is also rejected in offline mode. The tabs can still be visible, so a rejected operation means the administrator must change the relevant setting or use an allowed installation method.

To change either transfer setting, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then select **Settings** from its menu. Select **Advanced** in the page header, select the **Plugins** tab and **Features** group, change **Uploads** or **Downloads**, then select **Save**. **Advanced** requires an Administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)).

**Add plugin manually** appears only for an Administrator account. It shows the configured plugins folder and provides **Copy**, **Open Files**, and **Restart**. Place the package in the shown folder, then use **Restart**; manually placed packages are discovered after the application restarts.

#### Read the actions on a plugin card

| Control | When it appears or succeeds |
| --- | --- |
| **Clone plugin** | The plugin supports cloning, is enabled, and is not locked. Cloning also requires **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)). |
| **Edit configuration** | The plugin declares configuration support and is not locked by an active operation. Saving configuration requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). |
| **Install backend** | The plugin supports backend installation, is not permanently disabled or waiting for a compatibility override, and its status is **Backend not installed** or **Install error**. |
| **Manage backend** | The plugin declares backend management support. Backend mutations require **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)) and a compatible plugin with the required system capabilities. |
| **Stop plugin** | The current runtime state is stoppable. Persistent plugins are not stoppable from this control. |

The card exposes only what the plugin and its current state support. For model download, provider, cloning, and backend-maintenance procedures, see [Install and manage plugins](#install-and-manage-plugins).

#### Package and worker boundary

Before activating a package, SoAI audits its archive, reads its literal manifest, validates declared package dependencies, prepares the package and its [Python](https://www.python.org/) environment, then starts a dedicated worker process. With [`PLUGINS.SECURITY.SAFETY_VALIDATION`](#config-PLUGINS.SECURITY.SAFETY_VALIDATION) enabled, package safety validation also checks source imports. The host talks to the worker through authenticated IPC. **The worker boundary separates runtime state, but it is not an operating-system sandbox: package code retains the permissions of the account running SoAI.**

### Bundled plugins reference [page: bundled-plugins-reference]

SoAI includes eight bundled plugins. Seven provide managed local backends or local media capabilities, while **External** connects to remote OpenAI-compatible providers. To use a local backend in the SoAI WebUI, open **Plugins**, select its card, open **Manage backend**, choose an available backend variant, and start installation. Then open **Models > Add model** to add a model for that plugin.

The availability of a backend variant is based on the current operating system, hardware, drivers, and required runtime. Read the compatibility message in **Manage backend** before installing. The capability badges on a plugin or model describe what the selected backend and model can handle; a model does not automatically support every operation its plugin can proxy.

#### Local inference backends

[Ollama](https://ollama.com/) is a managed local inference backend and can also connect to [Ollama Cloud](https://ollama.com/). It supports chat completions, completions, Responses, embeddings, vision, tool calling, structured output, and JSON Schema when the selected model supports the operation. It can search for and download models, and its plugin can be cloned when you need a separately configured instance.

For separate local instances, select **Clone plugin** on the [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) card. Give the clone a different configuration, including its GPU binding or port where appropriate, before running both instances. Use this only when the host has capacity for the additional backend and model files.

##### vLLM

[vLLM](https://vllm.ai/) is a managed local backend for plugin-declared GPTQ, AWQ, GGUF, and transformer models. Its capabilities include chat completions, completions, Responses, embeddings, vision, input audio, tool calling, structured output, and JSON Schema where the chosen model supports them. [vLLM](https://vllm.ai/) can also be cloned.

The bundled variants include CPU builds for [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) x64 and arm64, plus an [Apple](https://www.apple.com/) Silicon CPU build. GPU-oriented variants are available for [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/) [CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-zone) on [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/), [AMD](https://www.amd.com/) [ROCm](https://www.amd.com/) on [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) x64, and an [Intel](https://www.intel.com/) XPU container on [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) x64. **The [Apple](https://www.apple.com/) GPU variant and the Windows-through-WSL variant are currently marked unavailable in SoAI.** Select the variant in **Plugins > [vLLM](https://vllm.ai/) > Manage backend**; do not rely on a generic statement that every [vLLM](https://vllm.ai/) installation requires the same operating system or accelerator.

##### Llama.cpp

[Llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) is the bundled GGUF backend. It supports chat completions, completions, Responses, embeddings, vision, tool calling, structured output, and JSON Schema where the model supports them. SoAI can install a suitable backend variant, search and download models, and clone the plugin.

The managed variants cover CPU and selected [CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-zone), [ROCm](https://www.amd.com/), [Vulkan](https://www.vulkan.org/), [OpenVINO](https://www.intel.com/), [SYCL](https://www.khronos.org/sycl/), [OpenCL](https://www.khronos.org/opencl/), and [Metal](https://developer.apple.com/metal/) paths across the platforms shown in **Manage backend**. Pick from that live list instead of copying a backend port or build setting from another host.

Mixed-vendor hosts can run separate compatible plugin instances or backends for [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/), [AMD](https://www.amd.com/), and [Intel](https://www.intel.com/) GPUs. [CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-zone), [ROCm](https://www.amd.com/), and XPU bindings validate that every selected GPU belongs to the matching vendor. Clone a plugin when separate instances need different runtime variants or GPU bindings; one vendor-specific backend instance cannot combine [CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-zone), [ROCm](https://www.amd.com/), and XPU devices. See [Mixed-vendor GPU systems](#mixed-vendor-systems) for the hardware boundary.

#### Task-specific local backends

[CTranslate2](https://opennmt.net/CTranslate2/) is an offline CPU neural machine translation backend, not a general-purpose chat model engine. It uses [CTranslate2](https://opennmt.net/CTranslate2/) model entries from the [Helsinki-NLP](https://huggingface.co/Helsinki-NLP) repository and exposes translation through chat-completions and completions compatibility surfaces. It does not provide embeddings, Responses, vision, tool calling, or audio operations.

Use it when the job is translation. You can install its backend, download a translation model, and clone the plugin for an independently configured instance from the same **Plugins** workflow.

##### Llama.cpp Embeddings

[Llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) Embeddings is a separate, persistent GGUF embedding runtime. It supports the embeddings endpoint and not chat completions, completions, Responses, media, or tool calling. It can be installed, configured, searched, downloaded, and cloned like the other local model plugins.

Use this plugin when you want a dedicated local embedding model for Knowledge collections or embedding API work. In Chat, open **Chat configuration > Knowledge**, then choose **Embedding model** after the model is installed and appears in the catalog.

##### Melo TTS

[Melo TTS](https://github.com/myshell-ai/MeloTTS) is a persistent local text-to-speech backend. It supplies the audio speech capability, downloads its language packs as models, and allows one active request at a time. It is not a chat, completion, embedding, or transcription backend.

The plugin offers CPU, [CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-zone), [Apple](https://www.apple.com/) MPS, and container variants where the current host can use them. Choose the displayed variant in **Manage backend**, then add the language pack needed for the voice workflow.

##### Whisper

[Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) is a persistent local speech-to-text backend. It provides audio transcription and audio translation, can search for and download compatible models, and allows one active request at a time. It is not a chat, completion, embedding, image, or text-to-speech backend.

Use **Plugins > [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) > Manage backend** to choose an available CPU or accelerator variant, then add a [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) model from **Models > Add model**. The displayed backend variants show the choices compatible with the current platform and detected drivers.

#### External providers

External is a persistent connector for remote OpenAI-compatible APIs, including [OpenAI](https://openai.com/), [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/), [Groq](https://groq.com/), and [Together AI](https://www.together.ai/). **It does not install, download, delete, or run a provider on the SoAI host.** Instead, it stores a provider connection and imports the models that provider reports.

Open **Models > Add model > Add provider**, choose **External**, then enter the **Provider name**, **API URL**, and **API key**. A **Models filter** is optional. After the provider is saved, SoAI discovers models through the provider's OpenAI-compatible `/models` response and applies that filter. Provider and model capability data can vary, so confirm the imported model's capabilities before using media, tools, structured output, or Responses features.

### Install and manage plugins [page: install-and-manage-plugins]

Plugins provide the backend behind each local engine or remote provider. In the SoAI WebUI, use **Plugins** for backend installation, updates, configuration, cloning, and health checks. Use **Models** to add, download, inspect, enable, or remove the model entries served through those plugins.

#### Access to plugin and model controls

Opening **Plugins** requires **Plugin read access** ([`PLUGIN_READ`](#acl-PLUGIN_READ)), and opening **Models** requires **Model read access** ([`MODEL_READ`](#acl-MODEL_READ)). Backend installation, updates, cloning, deletion, and related plugin controls require **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)). Model downloads and deletion require **Model administration** ([`MODEL_ADMIN`](#acl-MODEL_ADMIN)). Editing a plugin configuration or a capacity setting also requires **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)). Administrators receive these actions by default; see [Administration overview](#administration-overview) to manage exceptions in ACL.

#### Install and update a local backend

Open **Plugins** and select the plugin you want to use. When its status is **Backend not installed**, select **Install backend**. In the backend dialog, choose a backend variant that is available for the host, review its compatibility message, and select **Start installation**. Installation progress remains visible in the dialog. When it finishes, open **Models > Add model** to search for, download, or register a model for that plugin.

To maintain an installed backend, select **Manage backend** on its plugin card. Use **Check for updates**, then select **Update** only when an update is offered. Select **Uninstall** to remove the managed runtime. The WebUI confirms that model files are preserved during backend uninstallation, so remove models separately from **Models** when that is what you intend.

External providers are different: they do not have a local backend to install. Add one through **Models > Add model > Add provider**, choose **External**, and enter the **Provider name**, **API URL**, **API key**, and optional **Models filter**. SoAI discovers models from the provider after the connection is saved.

#### Read plugin states

The status badge describes the current backend or runtime condition. Transient states normally resolve on their own; error and compatibility states need an operator decision.

##### Backend operations

`Backend not installed`, `Backend installing`, `Backend updating`, `Removing backend`, and `Deleting` mean that the plugin is waiting for a runtime, running a backend operation, or being deleted. Wait for the operation to finish, or open the plugin dialog to inspect its progress and error message.

##### Normal lifecycle

`Stopped`, `Starting`, `Loading`, `Ready`, `Ready (pending dispatch)`, `Ready (modified)`, `Idle`, `Processing`, and `Stopping` are normal lifecycle states. No repair is usually needed. A request can start or load a stopped local backend when routing permits it.

##### Persistent services

`Persistent` means the plugin is declared persistent, such as a dedicated embedding or audio service. Check its capability and capacity requirements before treating it like an unloadable chat backend.

##### Errors, quarantine, and incompatibility

`Install error`, `Load error`, `Update error`, `Backend uninstall error`, `Delete error`, `Error`, `Quarantined`, and `Incompatible` mean an operation or runtime failed, recovery quarantined the plugin, or the host and plugin do not meet a declared requirement. Read the card's compatibility or error detail, open **Logs**, then follow [Reset an open circuit](#recover-an-unavailable-plugin) or [Make a quarantined plugin available again](#make-a-quarantined-plugin-available-again) for the reported state.

##### Missing or disabled state

`Status unknown`, `Not detected`, `Absent`, and `Disabled` mean SoAI lacks current state data, the plugin is missing, it is absent from its expected location, or it is deliberately offline. Restore or add a trusted plugin only if it is required, or enable the intended plugin after reviewing its state.

#### Clone a plugin

A clone is a separate plugin instance for a plugin that supports cloning. On the plugin card, select **Clone plugin**. The dialog lets you choose a **Custom name** and whether to **Clone models**. Include model files only when you want an additional copy and have enough storage. After the clone exists, select **Edit configuration** on the original and clone to give them distinct host, port, model-path, or GPU-binding values where those fields are available.

**Cloning does not make two model instances fit in memory.** Before starting both, review [Capacity planning](#capacity-planning) and the hardware data in the WebUI.

#### Add third-party plugins carefully

Open **Plugins** and select **Add plugin**. The dialog offers **Upload plugin**, **Download plugin from URL**, and **Add plugin manually**. These controls require **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)). **A plugin can execute code on the SoAI host, so install only a package you trust.** If a backend already offers an OpenAI-compatible API, use the External provider route instead of installing a plugin solely to proxy it.

The manual tab displays the plugin folder, offers **Open Files**, and shows **Restart** after you place a `.soaiplugin` file there. SoAI loads that manually placed plugin after the restart.

### Creating a new plugin [page: creating-a-new-plugin]

A SoAI plugin is a `.soaiplugin` ZIP archive whose root `__init__.py` defines one direct `Plugin` class derived from `plugin_sdk.BasePlugin`. [Plugin architecture](#plugin-architecture) describes how the host inspects, prepares, and runs that package, and [Plugin SDK reference](#plugin-sdk-reference) documents the import surface it may use, so this page is the build path: how to lay out the archive, what the manifest has to declare literally, which methods you must implement, and how to get the result loaded and tested. Work in a source directory outside the plugins folder and package from there. Review [License and legal](#license-and-legal) for the terms that apply to independently written plugins and Core SDK files, and read [Security hardening](#security-hardening) before installing a package from another source, because a worker runs with the permissions of the operating-system account that runs SoAI.

#### Lay out the archive

```
my_plugin_source/
  __init__.py
  request_adapter.py
  model_parameters.json
  LICENSES/
    LICENSE_SOAIPLUGIN.txt

my_plugin.soaiplugin
  __init__.py
  request_adapter.py
  model_parameters.json
  LICENSES/
    LICENSE_SOAIPLUGIN.txt
```

Archive the contents of the source directory rather than the directory itself, keep the entrypoint at the root, and put cohesive modules beside it with relative imports. The bundled packages under `plugins/` are ordinary ZIP archives you can open as a working reference for a specific backend type. Every source member must decode as UTF-8 and parse, and inspection rejects bytecode and `__pycache__` along with an archive carrying more than 512 source members, a single member over 8 MiB, or more than 64 MiB of source in total. An optional root `model_parameters.json` must be a JSON object that follows the model-parameter schema and stay under 8 MiB. Keeping credentials, local model files, `plugin_sdk` itself, and the generated `.soaiplugin.yaml` sidecar out of the archive is author discipline rather than a validated rule, so nothing will reject a package that ships them; SoAI writes the sidecar itself from `DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION` and keeps it next to the archive.

A plugin package may include one optional, case-sensitive root `logo.png` or `logo.webp` file; it must be a static PNG or WebP image no larger than 1 MiB and 512 pixels on either side. SoAI sanitizes valid artwork for automatic display in plugin and model catalogs, and uses the existing built-in or generic artwork when the logo is absent or invalid.

**The archive filename decides the installed identity.** SoAI takes the file stem, which must be alphanumerics, dashes, or underscores and must not begin with an underscore, and uses it as the plugin ID throughout the catalog, while `NAME` is only the display name. Installed packages live in the directory named by [`PLUGINS.PATHS.PLUGINS`](#config-PLUGINS.PATHS.PLUGINS), which resolves to `plugins` inside the SoAI directory unless you change it.

#### Declare the manifest as literals

SoAI reads the manifest by parsing the entrypoint before the package ever runs, so every required value must be a plain literal assigned directly on `Plugin`. A computed expression, a property, an inherited default, or an imported constant is rejected even when it would produce the correct value at runtime, and an annotation is fine, since `NAME: str = "Acme"` and `MODEL_TYPES: typing.ClassVar[list[str]] = ["acme"]` both read as literal assignments. `EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_MODE` is the one exception and may be written as a `plugin_sdk.ExternalProviderMode` member, a string, or `None`. These required fields are defined in `backend/plugins/manifest/class_field_contract.py`.

| Group | Required literal assignments |
| --- | --- |
| Identity and licensing | `NAME`, `VERSION_SOAIPLUGIN`, `AUTHOR_SOAIPLUGIN`, `DESCRIPTION_SOAIPLUGIN`, `WEBSITE_SOAIPLUGIN`, `WEBSITE_BACKEND`, and `LICENSE_SOAIPLUGIN`. |
| Compatibility and dependencies | `REQUIRED_SOAI_VERSION`, `PLUGIN_DEPENDENCIES`, `PACKAGE_DEPENDENCIES`, and `REQUIRED_SYSTEM_CAPABILITIES`. |
| Models and resources | `MODEL_REPOSITORY`, `MODEL_TYPES`, `ALIASES`, `SUPPORTED_MODALITIES`, `LOCAL_RESOURCES`, and `LOCAL_MODELS`. |
| Runtime and management | `PERSISTENT`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`, `SUPPORTS_BACKEND_INSTALLATION`, `SUPPORTS_BACKEND_PROCESS_TRACKING`, `SUPPORTS_MODEL_DELETION`, `SUPPORTS_MODEL_DOWNLOAD`, `SUPPORTS_CONFIGURATION`, `SUPPORTS_EXTERNAL_PROVIDERS`, `EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_MODE`, and `SUPPORTS_CLONING`. |

**Every flag in `OPENAI_FEATURE_MATRIX` is required as a literal boolean too.** The matrix covers Chat Completions, Completions, Responses and its subresources, embeddings, images, audio endpoints, image edits and variations, vision, input audio, tool calling, parallel tool calls, structured output, and JSON Schema, and it is exported through the top-level SDK and defined in `backend/core/openai/capability_taxonomy.py`. The worker repeats that check against the loaded class and adds `SUPPORTED_MODALITIES`, so a flag inherited from a base class instead of assigned on `Plugin` passes archive inspection and then fails at load.

Everything outside those two lists is optional and falls back to the BasePlugin default when omitted, including `DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION`, `BACKEND_VARIANT_OPTIONS`, `CLONABLE_FIELDS`, `WELCOME_MESSAGE`, `LICENSE_MANAGED_BACKEND`, `EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_DEFAULTS`, `SUPPORTS_GPU_BINDING`, `SUPPORTS_MODEL_SEARCH`, `SUPPORTS_MODEL_VARIANT_DISCOVERY`, and `SUPPORTS_PROMPT_TOKEN_COUNTING`. The last four have a fallback implementation on the base class that raises a state error when the flag is set and the method is not overridden, so declaring one of them early turns a missing feature into a failed request rather than a quiet no.

`PERSISTENT` changes when the plugin runs. A persistent plugin is brought up during initial load, where SoAI calls `get_status` and `health_ping` and attempts `start` if it is unhealthy, and the Guardian keeps polling it afterwards. A non-persistent plugin is started on demand around a request through `start_with_model` and can be evicted when the instance is at its concurrency limit. Report health honestly from both methods, since an optimistic `health_ping` is what turns a broken backend into repeated dispatch instead of quarantine.

##### Declare every third-party dependency

Each plugin gets its own [Python](https://www.python.org/) environment rather than sharing the host runtime, and that environment already carries the worker baseline of dnspython, httpx2, psutil, pydantic, typing-extensions, and zstandard at the versions SoAI pins, so those need no declaration. Anything else your code imports needs a pinned entry in `PACKAGE_DEPENDENCIES`, and an import with no matching entry fails the audit as a security error rather than surfacing later as a missing module. The check matches import roots against distribution names, so a distribution whose import name differs from its package name resolves only when that distribution is installed on the host and publishes a `top_level.txt`, with built-in aliases for PyYAML and piper-tts alone. Prefer a distribution whose import name matches its name.

#### Implement the BasePlugin contract

**Capability declarations do not remove abstract methods.** Implement every BasePlugin method, including operations your plugin does not expose through a capability.

| Area | Abstract methods |
| --- | --- |
| Configuration and backend | `get_parameter_schema`, `get_default_configuration`, `check_system_dependencies`, `install_backend`, `update_backend`, and `remove_backend`. |
| Status and lifecycle | `get_status`, `check_for_backend_update`, `health_ping`, `get_log_file_path`, `discover_models`, `start`, `start_with_model`, and `stop`. |
| Models and requests | `cancel_task`, `load_model_in_service`, `unload_model_in_service`, `get_model_download_plan`, `download_model`, `delete_model`, and `handle_request`. |

The base class supplies defaults for partial-install cleanup and backend-process PID reporting. [Plugin SDK reference](#plugin-sdk-reference) lists the contexts, helpers, and error types available through the top-level SDK, and `backend/plugin_sdk/__init__.pyi` is the maintained typing stub that gives an editor the whole lazily resolved surface. Import from `plugin_sdk` itself and use package-local relative imports; a `plugin_sdk.*` submodule import and a direct import of a Core package are both rejected, as are `__import__`, `eval`, `exec`, `compile`, `importlib`, and `runpy` in aliased and `getattr` forms, so an optional dependency cannot be lazily loaded. That audit always runs on upload whatever [`PLUGINS.SECURITY.SAFETY_VALIDATION`](#config-PLUGINS.SECURITY.SAFETY_VALIDATION) is set to, while a package you place in the plugins folder is checked through safety validation instead, which that setting can disable.

#### Declare what the host must provide

`REQUIRED_SOAI_VERSION` is a [Python](https://www.python.org/) version specifier set matched against the running Core version, so an open lower bound and a lower bound paired with an exclusive upper bound are both valid, while an unparsable value marks the package broken. **A package outside the range loads as version incompatible with a message naming the update or downgrade target, and that verdict cannot be overridden.** `REQUIRED_SYSTEM_CAPABILITIES` is a mapping whose keys are lowercased before comparison, where `os`, `platforms`, `arch`, and `gpu` are recognized, values normalize to SoAI's platform identifiers, and `any` matches everything; a host that fails one of those is recorded with its own reason and an administrator can override it on the plugin record. An upload that fails either check is kept rather than deleted, so the card carries the reason and you delete the package from Plugins before uploading a corrected build.

#### Install and test the package

1. Sign in as an Administrator with **Plugin administration** ( [`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN) ).
2. In the SoAI WebUI, open **Plugins**, then select **Add plugin**.
3. Select **Upload plugin**, select **Choose file**, choose the `.soaiplugin` archive, then select **Upload plugin**.
4. Watch the modal progress, or select the bell at the right of the header and expand **Tasks**. Once the task reaches a terminal result, open the new card and read its status and compatibility details.
5. Use only the actions the package declares. **Install backend**, for example, appears only when the current plugin state and capability permit it.

Upload requires [`PLUGINS.FEATURES.UPLOADS`](#config-PLUGINS.FEATURES.UPLOADS) to be enabled, and the server refuses a name that already exists in the catalog or on disk, so an upload cannot replace an earlier test build. For a tight iteration loop, use **Add plugin manually** instead: copy the archive into the plugins folder that dialog shows, then restart. Reconciliation re-audits every package in that folder at each start and the prepared package cache is keyed by the archive hash, so new bytes under the same name are inspected again rather than reused.

#### Create a plugin with an AI coding agent

Give the agent access to the SoAI source tree, the backend's official documentation, and a disposable SoAI instance. The current SDK and bundled plugins define the contract. **Keep production credentials out of the brief.**

Fill in the bracketed fields in the prompt below, leaving a field blank when it does not apply. The Copy button copies the whole prompt.

```text
You are building and verifying a third-party SoAI plugin against the public Plugin SDK.

PLUGIN BRIEF

Plugin filename without extension: [LOWERCASE ID, FOR EXAMPLE acme_chat]
Display name: [DISPLAY NAME]
Plugin purpose: [ONE CONCRETE PARAGRAPH]
Backend or upstream API: [NAME, VERSION, AND OFFICIAL PROJECT OR DOCUMENTATION ROOT]
Local process or remote service: [LOCAL / REMOTE / HYBRID]
Authentication: [NONE / API KEY / OAUTH / OTHER]
Models and discovery source: [HOW MODELS ARE FOUND]
OpenAI endpoints to support: [CHAT COMPLETIONS / RESPONSES / EMBEDDINGS / IMAGES / AUDIO]
OpenAI features to support: [STREAMING / TOOLS / VISION / JSON SCHEMA / OTHER]
Supported operating systems: [LINUX / WINDOWS / MACOS]
Supported hardware: [CPU / NVIDIA / AMD / INTEL / APPLE SILICON]
Backend installation or model downloads: [DESCRIBE OR NONE]
Configuration fields: [NAMES, TYPES, DEFAULTS, AND WHICH HOLD CREDENTIALS]
Cancellation behavior: [HOW AN ACTIVE BACKEND REQUEST IS STOPPED]
License for the plugin: [SPDX NAME OR LICENSE TEXT]
Acceptance test: [THE REQUEST AND RESULT THAT PROVE THE PLUGIN WORKS]

Create the plugin source, focused tests, a deterministic build step, and the final .soaiplugin package. Test the final package in a disposable SoAI installation before treating it as complete.

Public contract

1. Read Creating a new plugin, Plugin SDK reference, Plugin architecture, Install and manage plugins, and Security hardening in the documentation for the SoAI version that will load the package. Treat those published pages and the installed top-level plugin_sdk surface as authoritative. If a requested feature is not expressible through that public surface, stop and identify the missing contract instead of importing private application modules.

2. Determine the current BasePlugin methods, metadata fields, OpenAI capability flags, supported helper types, import rules, and package limits from the public SDK documentation. Implement the exact contract for the target SoAI version. Do not change SoAI or weaken its validation to make the plugin load.

3. Ask for a missing plugin-specific fact only when it cannot be determined from the brief, the upstream project's public documentation, or the public SoAI plugin documentation. Never request or embed a production credential. Use named configuration fields for secrets and ensure their values cannot reach logs, exceptions, fixtures, or the archive.

Package contract

4. Build a ZIP-format file named [PLUGIN ID].soaiplugin. Put exactly one regular __init__.py at the archive root. That entrypoint defines one direct Plugin class derived from plugin_sdk.BasePlugin. Do not wrap the package in another directory.

5. Put cohesive implementation modules and resources beside the entrypoint and use relative imports within the package. Keep tests, fixtures, mocks, build scripts, caches, bytecode, local environments, credentials, and generated .soaiplugin.yaml files outside the archive. Do not bundle plugin_sdk or other SoAI files.

6. Import only the Python standard library, top-level plugin_sdk exports, package-local modules, and third-party distributions declared in PACKAGE_DEPENDENCIES. Do not import plugin_sdk submodules or private SoAI packages. Use static imports and declare only dependencies the plugin actually uses.

7. Set every required metadata and OpenAI capability field directly on Plugin with literal values, including false and empty values. Set capabilities from implemented, tested behavior. Use the plugin metadata names documented for the target SoAI version and declare an accurate REQUIRED_SOAI_VERSION range.

8. Put non-secret defaults in DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION and let SoAI create the runtime configuration sidecar. Include model_parameters.json only when the plugin exposes per-model parameters. Every discovered model must have a stable, non-empty source model ID and truthful provider, format, ownership, and capability data.

Behavior and resilience

9. Implement every required BasePlugin method with the exact public signature. Disabled operations return the documented truthful result; they never fabricate success. Validate inputs before mutation and use atomic writes or explicit rollback for plugin-managed state.

10. Return standard OpenAI-compatible payloads for declared endpoints. Streaming responses emit valid OpenAI server-sent event frames and end with data: [DONE]. Preserve documented tool-call and usage fields. Do not add private SoAI envelopes to OpenAI streams.

11. Use the SDK request context, cancellation hook, HTTP client, file access, configuration, runtime services, and public error types. Enforce offline policy before network access when required. Clean up subprocesses, streams, files, locks, and tracked tasks after success, failure, cancellation, and shutdown. Cancellation must stop only the selected request.

12. Classify invalid input, configuration problems, missing resources, upstream failures, process failures, and invalid state with the matching public SDK error type. Log an unexpected failure once at its owning boundary. Never log secrets, authorization headers, credentials, or unsafe upstream payloads.

13. Retry only idempotent operations with bounded attempts, backoff, cancellation, and duplicate prevention. Installation, updates, removal, model downloads, and model deletion must finish in a truthful success, failed, or cancelled state. Preserve unrelated plugins and models when one operation fails.

Build and acceptance

14. Keep source, tests, build output, and runtime scratch data separate. Write focused tests outside the archive for metadata, dependency declarations, configuration, stable model discovery, health success and failure, request translation, non-streaming output, streaming framing, cancellation, timeouts, malformed upstream data, secret redaction, and cleanup. Test installation, updates, removal, and model-file operations when supported.

15. Make the build reproducible: sort archive paths, normalize ZIP timestamps and regular-file modes, reject symbolic links, inspect the final archive listing, and confirm unchanged source produces the same SHA-256 digest. Keep only intended runtime files in the final archive.

16. Upload the final archive through Plugins > Add plugin > Upload plugin in a disposable SoAI installation. Wait for the upload task to finish, then inspect Plugin information for version, compatibility, state, modalities, capabilities, and file hash. Confirm configuration validation and saving without exposing credentials.

17. Confirm each expected model appears in Models with a stable source identity. Run Test model, complete the acceptance request through Chat or the documented API, verify non-streaming output, verify streaming and [DONE] when supported, and cancel an active request. Check the visible task and plugin states and review logs for tracebacks, secret exposure, repeated failure loops, or quarantine events.

18. Exercise one deliberate health or upstream failure and confirm the plugin becomes truthfully degraded, failed, or quarantined without breaking another plugin. If the plugin manages a local backend or model files, also test interruption, restart recovery, repeat of one idempotent operation, and removal with each supported data-retention choice.

Completion requires the final archive, its SHA-256 digest, passing focused tests, successful SoAI package validation and loading, stable model discovery, the acceptance request, cancellation evidence, and a clear list of capabilities or hardware paths that remain unsupported or untested.
```

### Plugin SDK reference [page: plugin-sdk-reference]

`plugin_sdk` is the public [Python](https://www.python.org/) boundary for a `.soaiplugin` package. It gives plugin authors the contracts, contexts, helpers, and error types needed to work with SoAI without importing private backend implementation modules.

#### SDK imports and Core contracts

```
import plugin_sdk
from plugin_sdk import BasePlugin, Config, JSONDict, ModelContext, PluginRuntimeServices, RequestContext
```

**Import public names from `plugin_sdk` only.** `plugin_sdk` resolves those names lazily, and `dir(plugin_sdk)` returns the public export list supported by the installed SoAI release.

Do not import a `plugin_sdk.*` submodule or a private package such as `core`, `features`, `database`, `plugins`, `models`, or `orchestrator`. Relative imports within the package are allowed. With [`PLUGINS.SECURITY.SAFETY_VALIDATION`](#config-PLUGINS.SECURITY.SAFETY_VALIDATION) enabled, package safety validation rejects the prohibited imports.

##### Core contracts

| Export | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `BasePlugin` | The required plugin lifecycle, model-management, cancellation, and request-handling contract. |
| `Config` and `ConfigError` | Configuration access and configuration failures. |
| `JSONDict` and `JSONValue` | JSON-compatible payload types used throughout the SDK contract. |
| `PluginRuntimeServices` | The runtime service bundle passed to the plugin constructor. |
| `RequestContext` and `ModelContext` | Per-request identity and the selected model context for lifecycle and request methods. |

BasePlugin stores the supplied configuration, event bus, metrics, model registry, plugin manager, runtime reporter, hardware and storage services, runtime flags, files helper, HTTP client, and installation path. Use the `PluginRuntimeServices` object passed at construction for available runtime capabilities rather than reaching into SoAI internals.

##### Capability and request helpers

The SDK exports `OPENAI_FEATURE_MATRIX`, `OPENAI_CAPABILITY_CATEGORIES`, `OpenAIEndpoint`, `OpenAIImageFeature`, `OpenAIChatFeature`, and `OpenAIModality`. Use them to keep manifest declarations and request handling aligned with the current capability taxonomy. It also exports helpers for compatible provider request bodies, provider headers, audio upload errors, structured-output errors, embedding batches, and prompt-token-count results.

`handle_request` receives a request payload, `RequestContext`, and `ModelContext`. It returns either a JSON response or an async byte stream. The response type must match the endpoint capability declared in the package manifest.

#### Privileged operations and failures

| Area | Selected public exports |
| --- | --- |
| Outbound network access | `create_guarded_async_http_client`, `guard_outbound_http_request`, `enforce_offline_policy`, `require_online_mode`, and `validate_runtime_host_port`. |
| Paths and files | `Files`, `PluginPathResolver`, `safe_join_under_base`, asynchronous file helpers, archive extractors, and disk-reservation protocols. |
| Processes | `ManagedProcessSession`, `spawn_logged_process`, `terminate_logged_process`, and verified loopback-listener helpers. |
| Transfers and artifacts | Download progress types, `async_stream_download_to_file`, artifact descriptors, model-variant builders, hashing, and transfer-format helpers. |

Use the guarded network helpers for outbound requests so offline and egress policy are applied consistently. Use the SDK path and archive helpers for files owned by the plugin. These helpers preserve the host's validation and resource-management rules.

##### Errors and runtime outcomes

The SDK exports `SoAIError`, `ValidationError`, `ConfigurationError`, `PluginConfigurationError`, `ExternalServiceError`, `OfflineModeError`, `ProcessError`, and resource-exhaustion errors. Convert a problem into the appropriate typed result or exception at the operation boundary. **Do not substitute an apparent success after a failed backend operation.**

#### Install and inspect a package in the SoAI WebUI

To test a package, sign in as an Administrator with **Plugin administration** ([`PLUGIN_ADMIN`](#acl-PLUGIN_ADMIN)), open **Plugins**, select **Add plugin**, choose **Upload plugin**, select **Choose file**, then select **Upload plugin**. Follow progress in the dialog or the **Tasks** panel in the header. SoAI checks the archive, manifest, dependencies, and compatibility before it loads the worker.

## SoAI OS

### SoAI OS overview [page: soai-os-overview]

SoAI OS is not yet available and will be released in the future.

SoAI OS is the appliance edition of SoAI for [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) 13. It includes SoAI Core and private services that manage the host, including [NetworkManager](https://networkmanager.dev/), [APT](https://www.debian.org/), SSH, storage, and GPU drivers. **A Core artifact does not include the `soai_os` tree or its host-management routes.**

SoAI OS is not yet available and is not currently distributed. Purchases, licenses, and installation media are not being issued. Contact [info@soai.to](mailto:info@soai.to) to join the waitlist; joining does not grant a license or promise an availability date.

SoAI OS installation media supports amd64 and arm64 computers. The installer needs internet access to reach the [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) repositories. On the first boot, it installs the SoAI runtime, enables the SoAI service, and waits for the health check to pass before starting the desktop. Open the **SoAI** desktop shortcut, then complete the licensing and administrator steps in the setup wizard. See [SoAI quickstart](#soai-quickstart) for the first WebUI session.

#### Start SoAI OS and find its host controls

Use `./soai_os/soai-os.sh` for appliance lifecycle commands. **Do not run `./soai.sh` in that installation.** The appliance launcher selects the SoAI OS entry point; a configuration value or environment variable cannot turn a Core installation into the appliance edition.

##### Find host controls in the SoAI WebUI

Host controls exist only in the SoAI OS frontend. Most require the **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)) action. The default Administrator role has that action, although an administrator with **ACL administration** ([`ACL_ADMIN`](#acl-ACL_ADMIN)) can change grants. A missing page, tab, or action usually means that the current edition, administrator status, or assigned actions do not meet its requirements.

- Select **Network** or **Storage** in the sidebar's **System** section to manage those host resources. Both pages require **SoAI OS administration** ( [`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN) ).
- For SSH or drivers, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**. The **SSH** and **Drivers** tabs require a current administrator and **SoAI OS administration** ( [`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN) ).
- The **Users** tab requires a current administrator with **User administration** ( [`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN) ). The host actions in its **SoAI OS Users** section also require **SoAI OS administration** ( [`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN) ). Standard accounts cannot open the Users tab.
- Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Updates** to open the updates page. Opening it requires **Software updates** ( [`SOFTWARE_UPDATE`](#acl-SOFTWARE_UPDATE) ); [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) package checks and installations in the **SoAI OS updates** section also require **SoAI OS administration** ( [`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN) ).
- **Power** is separate from the SoAI OS permission. It requires a current administrator with **System power control** ( [`SYSTEM_POWER`](#acl-SYSTEM_POWER) ); host restart, shutdown, suspend, and hibernate actions can also be disabled in configuration.

#### Tasks and rollback windows

Driver, package-update, partition, network safe-apply, and SSH safe-disable operations run as tasks. Follow their progress in the originating page, or open the header bell and select **Tasks**. Network safe apply and SSH safe disable have a deadline: commit a working change before it expires, or SoAI OS restores the earlier state.

The host-management API is available under `/api/v1/os` and enforces the same server-side action checks as the WebUI. Use the [HTTP API reference](#http-api-reference) only when automating a workflow that is already understood in the WebUI.

### SoAI OS GPU drivers [page: soai-os-gpu-drivers]

**Drivers** is an appliance Settings tab. In the SoAI WebUI, select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **Drivers**. The tab is available only in the appliance edition to a current administrator with **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). **Core has neither this tab nor the corresponding host-driver routes.**

#### Read the driver state first

Select **Refresh** before making a change. The **Driver status** cards report detection, package installation, active kernel modules, runtime tools, readiness, and whether a reboot is required. **Installed packages alone do not mean that the driver is ready.** Read a card's warnings, then check the **Secure Boot** and **DKMS modules** sections when they are relevant to the hardware.

SoAI lists an actionable driver only when it detected that family or can uninstall a previously managed driver. The **Driver ID**, **Driver variant**, and preview actions stay unavailable until an actionable target is selected. When no target is available, the tab shows **No matching GPU drivers detected.**

#### Install a driver

1. Choose a target under **Driver ID** and, when shown, choose its **Driver variant**.
2. Select **Preview install**. The **Driver preview** dialog lists **Planned commands**, **Predicted effects**, and **Warnings**.
3. Check that the plan matches the host, then select **Install driver** in the dialog and confirm the same action.
4. Wait for task completion, select **Refresh**, and review the card again. Restart the host only if the card reports **Reboot required**.

The current catalog supports [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/), [AMD](https://www.amd.com/), and [Intel](https://www.intel.com/). [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/) can offer the **[Debian](https://www.debian.org/)** and **[NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/) 590** variants; [AMD](https://www.amd.com/) and [Intel](https://www.intel.com/) use **[Debian](https://www.debian.org/)**. The [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/) 590 variant is for Turing and newer GPUs. **Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta GPUs must use the [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) variant.** The offered choices reflect detected hardware and package availability, so a detected GPU does not guarantee that every package plan will succeed.

#### Uninstall carefully

Select **Preview uninstall**, inspect the **Driver preview**, then select **Uninstall driver** and confirm it. **Do not remove the only working display or inference driver unless console access or another recovery path is available.** For [AMD](https://www.amd.com/) and [Intel](https://www.intel.com/), uninstall removes only SoAI-managed driver tools; it leaves firmware, Mesa, media, and display packages in place.

### SoAI OS network management [page: soai-os-network-management]

In the SoAI WebUI, **Network** appears in the sidebar's **System** section only in SoAI OS. It requires **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). The page reads [NetworkManager](https://networkmanager.dev/) devices and connections, then lets an authorized user stage an editable connection profile or enable and disable a managed connection.

#### Inspect and stage a connection profile

1. Select **Network**, then **Refresh**.
2. Find the device. **Configure network device** appears only when it has an associated connection and SoAI reports that the profile is editable.
3. In **Configure <connection>**, set the IPv4 and IPv6 method, addresses, gateway, DNS servers, and **Autoconnect** as needed. Automatic IPv4 and IPv6 fields show the current assignment and are read-only; choose a manual method to edit them.
4. Select **Preview** to inspect **Planned commands**, **Predicted effects**, and **Warnings**. Select **Save** when the stored profile is correct.

**Saving updates the stored [NetworkManager](https://networkmanager.dev/) profile only.** It does not activate the profile. Use the device connection toggle when you are ready to activate or deactivate it. The toggle is unavailable for an unmanaged device or one without an associated connection.

#### Use safe apply for a risky connection change

Changing a device toggle opens an enable or disable confirmation. **Safe apply (automatic rollback)** is off by default, so the WebUI commits an accepted change immediately unless you turn safe apply on. Enable it before confirming when losing connectivity would be a problem.

With safe apply enabled, **Rollback timeout (seconds)** defaults to 120 and accepts whole values from 1 to 3,600. SoAI then shows **Commit network change**. Select **Confirm** before the deadline to keep the change. Declining that dialog offers **Rollback network change**; if no commit arrives by the deadline, SoAI restores the earlier connection state automatically.

**Keep local console access before changing the connection that carries the WebUI session.**

### SoAI OS storage management [page: soai-os-storage-management]

In the SoAI WebUI, **Storage** appears in the sidebar's **System** section only in SoAI OS. It requires **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)) and shows block devices, partitions, mounts, and an `fstab` table. Use it for appliance storage work, not for a model's storage configuration.

#### Read the current state

Select **Refresh storage status** before a mutation. Device cards report the disk, partitions, filesystem, UUID, mount state, and read-only state. A ZFS volume is labelled **ZFS volume managed outside SoAI** and is read-only here. SoAI does not offer destructive actions for a target it reports as read-only.

#### Create, format, mount, and persist a partition

**Warning:** **Create partition** initializes the selected disk with a GUID Partition Table (`GPT`) before creating the new partition. **Treat it as a whole-disk destructive operation.** SoAI rejects this operation when the disk contains the root filesystem or a mounted filesystem, and it requires the current device fingerprint from the latest snapshot.

1. Select the relevant device or partition control: **Create partition**, **Format partition**, **Mount partition**, or **Unmount partition**.
2. Complete the dialog and select **Preview**. Read **Commands**, **Effects**, and **Warnings** before selecting **Execute**.
3. After the accepted task reaches a terminal state, select **Refresh storage status** and verify the reported mount and filesystem state before another destructive operation.

Formatting supports `ext4` and `exfat`. If the selected partition has existing signatures, select **Allow wiping existing signatures** before formatting can continue.

#### Make a mount persistent

In the **fstab** panel, select **Add fstab entry**. Choose a partition UUID, enter a mount point below `/mnt/soai`, choose the filesystem, preview the plan, and select **Execute**. SoAI creates or verifies the mount point, adds or replaces the UUID-based `/etc/fstab` entry for that mount point, reloads [systemd](https://systemd.io/), and mounts it. Use **Remove fstab entry** for an existing entry; it reloads [systemd](https://systemd.io/) but does not unmount, format, or remove the partition.

If a format task leaves a **Recovery required** card in **Ready to review** state, select **Review recovery** to reopen the format dialog. Select **Release quarantine** only after verifying the physical target or retiring it. The **Release storage quarantine** dialog requires the exact partition path and removes the storage conflict lock without rerunning the format.

### SoAI OS package updates [page: soai-os-package-updates]

The **Updates** page has separate jobs in the appliance edition: updating the application and updating [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) packages on the host. The **SoAI OS updates** section manages [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) packages only. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Updates**. Opening the page requires **Software updates** ([`SOFTWARE_UPDATE`](#acl-SOFTWARE_UPDATE)); the package section also requires **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). Application release updates are covered in [Updating SoAI](#updating-soai).

#### Check the host before installing

1. Select **Check OS updates**.
2. Wait for **SoAI OS updates** to load its package table. The check refreshes [APT](https://www.debian.org/) package lists and simulates an upgrade. It does not install packages or restart the host.
3. Review each available package's **Current** and **New** version, **Download** size, and **Security** status.

**Host update checks and installs need an online runtime because they contact [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) repositories.** They are unavailable when [`SYSTEM.RUNTIME.STAY_OFFLINE`](#config-SYSTEM.RUNTIME.STAY_OFFLINE) is enabled.

#### Install packages from the SoAI WebUI

1. Select individual packages, or use **Select all upgradable packages** at the left of the table header to select every available package.
2. **Use dist-upgrade** is available only when the header checkbox selects every listed package. With individual packages selected, SoAI uses an [APT](https://www.debian.org/) install for those packages.
3. Select **Preview install** and read **Planned commands**, **Predicted effects**, and **Warnings**. Changing the package selection or the dist-upgrade choice invalidates the preview.
4. Select **Execute install**, confirm it, and follow **Task progress** on the page.

SoAI serializes [APT](https://www.debian.org/) work, refreshes package lists before installation, simulates the selected operation, and reserves reported disk space when necessary. **The task never restarts the host.** If the result requires a restart, select **Power** in the sidebar's **System** section, then select **Restart system**. Power requires a current administrator with **System power control** ([`SYSTEM_POWER`](#acl-SYSTEM_POWER)) and is unavailable when [`SYSTEM.RUNTIME.HOST_SYSTEM_ACTIONS_DISABLED`](#config-SYSTEM.RUNTIME.HOST_SYSTEM_ACTIONS_DISABLED) is enabled.

### SoAI OS SSH and host maintenance [page: soai-os-ssh-and-host-maintenance]

The SoAI OS WebUI exposes SSH and power controls for host maintenance. **It does not provide a general page for [systemd](https://systemd.io/) service management, journal queries, or time synchronization.** Use the API only when those documented host operations are required outside the WebUI.

#### Manage SSH in the SoAI WebUI

Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **SSH**. This tab exists only in SoAI OS and requires a current administrator with **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). Select **Refresh** to see the service name, runtime status, **Start on boot**, and last check time.

1. Select **Enable SSH** and confirm it to start SSH and enable it at boot.
2. To turn it off safely, select **Reset** beside **Disable SSH**. Despite the button label, it opens **Disable SSH safely**; it does not reset the service.
3. Set **Rollback timeout (seconds)**. It defaults to 120 and accepts whole values from 1 to 3,600. Select **Review**, inspect **Planned commands**, **Predicted effects**, and **Warnings**, then select **Disable SSH**.
4. When the pending operation becomes **Ready to finalize**, select **Commit disable** to keep SSH disabled or **Rollback now** to restore it. If no commit arrives before the deadline, SoAI OS restores the prior state automatically.

Keep console access or another recovery path available. **Disabling SSH can end the session used to operate the WebUI.**

#### Restart or shut down the host

Select **Power** in the sidebar's **System** section. The page requires a current administrator with **System power control** ([`SYSTEM_POWER`](#acl-SYSTEM_POWER)), which is separate from **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). Use **Restart system** or **Shut down**, set the available delay or force options, and confirm the request. The server rejects host power actions when [`SYSTEM.RUNTIME.HOST_SYSTEM_ACTIONS_DISABLED`](#config-SYSTEM.RUNTIME.HOST_SYSTEM_ACTIONS_DISABLED) is enabled. **Check active tasks first because a restart or shutdown ends SoAI and other running host processes.**

### SoAI OS host users and SSH keys [page: soai-os-host-users-and-ssh-keys]

The appliance keeps a SoAI WebUI identity separate from a [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) login. Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **Users**. The **Users** tab is available only to a current administrator with **User administration** ([`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN)). The host actions in its **SoAI OS Users** section require **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). Standard accounts do not have a Users-tab password, rename, or host user control.

#### Review and synchronize a mapped account

**User mapping** lists each WebUI user with the corresponding [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) account, its existence, lock state, UID, GID, groups, home directory, and shell. SoAI derives the [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) name from the WebUI user ID as `soaiu<id>`, so changing a WebUI user name does not rename the [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) account.

1. Under **Sync user**, choose the account by **WebUI user ID**. Each option shows the user name and ID.
2. Select **Execute sync**, then confirm the same action.
3. Read the result and refreshed mapping. A successful sync creates the [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) account if necessary, uses a home directory below `/home` and the `/bin/bash` shell, then locks its password.

**Synchronization never copies a WebUI password.** It reconciles managed group membership from the user's WebUI administrator status and synchronizes managed SSH keys from the WebUI profile when available. SoAI also reconciles the account after WebUI user creation, deletion, password, role, and user-name changes. Deleting a WebUI account locks the mapped [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) account, removes its SoAI-managed SSH keys and privileged managed groups, and leaves the [Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) account and home directory in place.

#### Manage SSH keys

1. Under **SSH keys**, choose the account by **WebUI user ID**.
2. Enter one or more public keys in **Public keys (one per line)**. The **Execute SSH key sync** control appears only after the field contains a non-empty key.
3. Select **Execute SSH key sync** and confirm it. This creates the mapped account if needed and keeps its password locked.

SoAI manages a marked block in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and preserves lines outside that block. It sets the SSH directory to mode `700` and the file to mode `600`. To remove SoAI-managed keys from the current WebUI, use **Lock user** and confirm **Execute lock**. That action locks the account password and removes its managed privileged groups.

**[Linux](https://www.kernel.org/) SSH login also requires SSH to be enabled.** Select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings** and **SSH**; that tab requires a current administrator with **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)).

### SoAI OS security model [page: soai-os-security-model]

**SoAI Core does not register host-management routes.** SoAI OS adds privileged routes under `/api/v1/os` for networking, storage, drivers, SSH, Linux-user synchronization, and [Debian](https://www.debian.org/) package updates.

#### Host authority is a separate action

SoAI OS host routes require **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). A signed-in user, including an administrator without that action, cannot use them. The default access policy grants the action to Administrators, but access policy changes can alter that. Limit it to people trusted to change the appliance itself.

Individual controls add their own requirements. The **SSH** and **Drivers** tabs require an administrator and **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)). The **Users** tab also requires **User administration** ([`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN)). The **Power** page instead requires an administrator with **System power control** ([`SYSTEM_POWER`](#acl-SYSTEM_POWER)). That action is separate from the SoAI OS host-management action.

**When SoAI OS creates its managed `soai.service` unit, it runs as `root` and starts `soai_os/soai-os.sh`.** This permits controlled use of [NetworkManager](https://networkmanager.dev/), [APT](https://www.debian.org/), [systemd](https://systemd.io/), and storage tools. Protect administrator accounts, retain backups, and keep a console recovery path.

#### Controls have their own safeguards

**Storage formatting and partition creation require the latest device fingerprint and reject root or mounted filesystems.** Network activation and SSH disable can use timed safe-apply workflows: an explicit commit keeps the change, while an expired deadline restores the previous state. Drivers, storage operations, and package work run as tasks with a terminal state that can be reviewed in the WebUI.

#### Harden the network edge

**The default HTTP and discovery bind addresses are `0.0.0.0`, and TLS is disabled.** Review [`SERVER.HTTP.NETWORK.HOST`](#config-SERVER.HTTP.NETWORK.HOST), [`SERVER.HTTP.NETWORK.DISCOVERY_HOST`](#config-SERVER.HTTP.NETWORK.DISCOVERY_HOST), and [`SERVER.HTTP.SSL.TLS_ENABLED`](#config-SERVER.HTTP.SSL.TLS_ENABLED) before connecting another device. Keep the appliance inside the boundary defined in [Security hardening](#security-hardening).

To change these values in the SoAI WebUI, an administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) selects the **Settings** button at the right of the header, then **Settings**, then the page header's **Advanced** control. Select the configuration group that contains the field, make the change, and use **Save**. Select **Restart SoAI** when the WebUI reports that a restart is required. Use explicit browser origins in [`SERVER.HTTP.CORS.ALLOWED_ORIGINS`](#config-SERVER.HTTP.CORS.ALLOWED_ORIGINS) instead of a wildcard. Pair TLS with [`SERVER.HTTP.SECURITY.REQUIRE_SECURE_TRANSPORT`](#config-SERVER.HTTP.SECURITY.REQUIRE_SECURE_TRANSPORT) and [`SERVER.WEBUI.COOKIE_SECURE`](#config-SERVER.WEBUI.COOKIE_SECURE).

## SoAI Connect

### SoAI Connect overview [page: soai-connect-overview]

SoAI Connect is the [Android](https://www.android.com/) client for your server. It opens the SoAI WebUI served by that server, so **Chat**, **Automation**, **Models**, **Files**, and **Settings** work much as they do in a browser. Models and user data stay on the server.

#### What the app adds

The main screen is the WebUI inside [Android](https://www.android.com/) WebView. The app blocks mixed-content loads and handles camera, microphone, and file access through Android's permission prompts and pickers.

Server alerts can reach the [Android](https://www.android.com/) notification shade while the app is in the background. You can also send a Wake-on-LAN packet before you connect. Open the app's settings to review certificate trust, clear WebUI data, change servers, or use Incognito Mode. The device name saved there appears in the server's session list. The app includes English and 25 translations, and follows the phone's dark theme.

#### Requirements

| Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Phone or tablet | [Android](https://www.android.com/) 8.0 (API 26) or newer. |
| SoAI account | A SoAI WebUI account on that server. An administrator with **User administration** ([`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN)) permission can select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, select **Users**, then select **Create user**. See [Administration overview](#administration-overview) for account and permission management. |
| Server | A running instance that the device can reach over HTTP or HTTPS. |

**SoAI Connect does not run models on the phone (it only presents the server's WebUI).** If the phone cannot reach the server, the WebUI does not load and [Android](https://www.android.com/) notifications cannot receive new alerts.

#### Install SoAI Connect

Open the [SoAI Connect repository](https://github.com/GetSoAI/SoAI_Connect) and select **Releases** to find the APK files. There is no app store listing. Download `SoAI-Connect-<version>-android.apk` and its matching `.sha256` file. On a computer with [Android](https://www.android.com/) SDK Build Tools installed, verify the download before copying or opening it on the phone.

```bash
sha256sum -c SoAI-Connect-<version>-android.apk.sha256
apksigner verify --print-certs SoAI-Connect-<version>-android.apk
```

Official release APKs report this signer:

```text
Signer: CN=SoAI Connect, O=SoAI, L=Rome, C=IT
SHA-256 digest: 664ee2c1ce55db7179eafab41ff22585380e236e1a8163a50e273e4691b6990b
```

After verification, open the APK on the phone. [Android](https://www.android.com/) may ask you to allow installs from the browser or file manager you used. Allow that source, install SoAI Connect, then turn the permission off if you do not use it for other packages.

Release APKs use [Android](https://www.android.com/) signature schemes v2 and v3 without a v1 JAR signature. **Do not install a package if the checksum or signer differs.** Report suspect packages to [security@soai.to](mailto:security@soai.to).

#### Data storage

| Location | Stored data |
| --- | --- |
| Device | Server address and identity, session cookies, web cache and site data, preferences, device identity, notification state, Wake-on-LAN values, and any certificate fingerprint you choose to trust. |
| SoAI server | Conversations, files, models, automations, user accounts, and active session records. |

[Android](https://www.android.com/) backup is disabled for SoAI Connect. Incognito Mode clears cookies and WebUI data when you leave the app. It also turns off [Android](https://www.android.com/) notifications because their background connection needs your signed-in session.

### Connect to a SoAI server [page: connect-to-a-soai-server]

SoAI Connect remembers one server at a time. Enter the address of the server, check the result, and sign in with the same account you use in the WebUI.

#### Prepare the server in the SoAI WebUI

1. Open the WebUI on a computer. If the **Setup wizard** appears, finish it and select **Create account** on the **Create administrator account** step.
2. To make a separate account for the phone, an administrator with **User administration** ( [`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN) ) permission can select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, select **Users**, then select **Create user**. See [Administration overview](#administration-overview) for the full account and ACL workflow.
3. If you run SoAI OS and have **SoAI OS administration** ( [`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN) ) permission, open **Network** from the sidebar. Use the **IP ADDRESS** shown on the connected network card. With SoAI Core, use the hostname or LAN IP that already opens the WebUI from another machine.
4. Put the phone on the same LAN or VPN as the server unless you have configured secure remote access.

**Do not enter `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`; on the phone, those names point back to the phone.** An address such as `192.168.1.100` or `soai.local` is usually enough. The app also accepts IPv6 and full `http://` or `https://` URLs. Add `:port` when more than one instance runs on the host.

#### Connect for the first time

1. Open SoAI Connect and enter the server address.
2. Select **Check**.
3. Check the instance name, SoAI version, URL, active port, and connection security shown on screen.
4. Select **Connect**.
5. If the server uses a private or self-signed certificate, the certificate prompt appears before the WebUI loads. Compare its SHA-256 fingerprint with the one supplied by your administrator, then select **Trust once** or **Trust always**.
6. Sign in on the SoAI page.

After the first connection, the app opens this server directly. To start over, open the app's **Settings**, then **Data**, and select **Change server**.

#### Server discovery

If you omit the port, SoAI Connect checks discovery ports `7950` through `7960`. It validates the answer and then checks the server's health endpoint. If the server moved to a fallback runtime port, the result shows both the configured port and the port in use.

**If two instances answer on the same host, SoAI Connect does not choose between them.** Enter an explicit port for the instance you want. An explicit `http://` URL without a port uses port 80, and an explicit `https://` URL uses port 443.

#### Choose a safe transport

| Connection | What SoAI Connect does | Recommended use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTPS with a public certificate | Uses Android's normal certificate validation. | Use this when the private LAN or VPN hostname has a certificate that [Android](https://www.android.com/) trusts. |
| HTTPS with a private or self-signed certificate | Shows the subject, issuer, and SHA-256 fingerprint before it loads the WebUI. | Compare the fingerprint through a separate trusted channel before you approve it. |
| HTTP on a private network | Allows the unencrypted connection. | Keep it on a trusted LAN or inside an encrypted VPN. |
| HTTP to a public address | Warns that anyone between the phone and server can read the session. | Configure HTTPS before signing in. |

For a private certificate, **Trust once** keeps approval for the current app session. **Trust always** pins the certificate fingerprint to that server origin and instance (not merely its hostname). If the private or otherwise untrusted certificate changes, SoAI Connect stops the request and asks you to review the new fingerprint. Remove a saved pin under **Settings**, **Security**, **Reset Trusted Certificate**.

**SoAI Connect does not support client-certificate authentication.** Keep the server on the private boundary described in [Security hardening](#security-hardening). An administrator with **Configuration changes** ([`CONFIG_PATCH`](#acl-CONFIG_PATCH)) and **ACL administration** ([`ACL_ADMIN`](#acl-ACL_ADMIN)) permissions should select the **Settings** button at the right of the WebUI header, select **Settings** from its menu, open **Security**, and resolve every item in the **Security hardening audit**. Use HTTPS for the connection.

#### Connection problems

| Message or symptom | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Certificate changed | Compare the new fingerprint with the server before you replace the saved pin. |
| Invalid server address | Enter a hostname, IPv4 address, bracketed IPv6 address, or HTTP/HTTPS URL without spaces. |
| IPv6 zone identifiers are not supported | Replace a scoped address such as `fe80::1%wlan0` with a hostname or supported address. |
| Multiple SoAI servers were found | Enter `hostname:port` for the instance you want. |
| Server not found | Check that discovery ports `7950` through `7960` reach the server, or enter its runtime port. |
| Server not reachable | Confirm that SoAI is running. In SoAI OS, an account with **SoAI OS administration** ([`HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN`](#acl-HOST_MANAGEMENT_ADMIN)) permission can open **Network** in the SoAI WebUI and check that the selected network card is **Connected** and still has the address you entered. |
| The endpoint responded but is not a SoAI server | Check the address and port. Another service may be listening there. |
| The WebUI opens but sign-in fails | Use an account from this server. An administrator with **User administration** ([`USER_ADMIN`](#acl-USER_ADMIN)) permission can select the **Settings** button at the right of the header, choose **Settings**, then select **Users**. |
